review_text: Amazing! I felt like I was transported back to Texas in just one bite. As a Texan, I have a high standard for Tex-Mex and never thought I would ever be able to find it in NYC until last night. We  started with what any Texan would start with...queso and it was good!!! Smooth and creamy with a mild spice of serrano peppers. For my entrée, I kept it simple, chicken tacos, which you can't go wrong with! They come two in an order and are stuffed with lime marinated chicken, avocado and queso fresco. Yummmm! We topped it off with the traditional frozen margaritas, which were the perfect blend of tequila and lime and just what I needed to make this the best meal I have had in a long time. Bravo Javelina and thank you for bringing Tex-Mex to NYC! A note to Texans: This is the real deal, you no longer have to go back to Texas every time you are craving queso, enchiladas, tacos and ritas. To all the Non-Texans reading this, you are in for the real deal and make sure to start with queso!

FINALLY a place in New York that serves real Tex-Mex! They have queso that gives nod to two amazing places in Austin- Matt's El Rancho and Magnolia Cafe. Definitely try one of the specialty quesos. I had the Bob Armstrong dip and beef fajitas and both were delicious. The Mexican Margarita was really good as well... very similar to Trudy's in Austin! Super excited about this place, and they have a great bar for after work drinks.

This was my first visit to Javelina but most certainly won't be my last!    

The entire staff went out of their way to make sure that we enjoyed ourselves -from the hostesses, bartenders, and manager who stopped by to check on our table.  I never would have guessed it was opening night. 

I would highly recommend the classic margarita - it was one of the best I've had in the city.  Don't get me started on the queso you just need to try it for yourself....yes, its that good!

Wow. This is something unusual place in my neighbor. They greet you warmly at the beginning and that give a great warm impression of what to expect. I got my margatita and it was great. And fajitas i got was great too. 

Go here if you want to try something from hotter lands in the cold winter of NY.

Had dinner here last night, only its 3rd night open. The food was amazing! Chips and salsa were immediately brought to the table after we sat down. I don't know what this "white queso" nonsense is, but the regular queso is AMAZING! Just like back in Dallas. You can load it with brisket, chorizo, guac, whatever. Like others have said: this is the real deal, people! Spicy jalapeno margarita was great. Brisket tacos were good, but I was eyeing the enchiladas and fajitas that other tables ordered with food remorse. Good thing I'm going back again tonight...

The owner (from Texas) was walking around checking on everyone - a really nice guy. They're not messing around at Javelina - it's real Tex-mex. And I no longer have a need to ever go back to Texas now :)

How can I find Tex-Mex in NYC? Impossible until this joint.

We walked in on Saturday, 4th night open.  Wait was longggg...this place is getting a lot of hype.  Waited 1.5 hours but it was worth.

White queso...strongly recommend.  Yummy and smooth, has a little kick to it, just like Texas. Enchiladas were fabulous, sauce is good. Rice and beans are a plus. Drinks were strong and the staff was very excited. Fun night. The owner even came around to say hello before we left. Strongly recommend. Best tex-mex in NYC.

I'm giving this spot an extra star because I visited on night 3 and I'm sure they were still working out some kinks. This review is based on my criteria, which deems a place worth a mention and/or a second visit.

Conclusion: 
Overall, avoid.  There are way tastier and more vibrant places in NYC to spend your evening.

Decor: 
Bare bones, no character.

Service: 
Very attentive but timing was off; received tacos before apps.

Food: 
The chile relleno was topped with raisins, which immediately made the plate look cheap and sloppy.  Overall, food was not terrible but it wasn't memorable either.

Cocktails: 
Overpriced and not satisfying.

Atmosphere: 
The music was billboard top 50's.  Very generic.  Luckily the sound system was almost non-existent.

Scene:  
An odd mix of people were there that night.  The super intoxicated owner stumbled up to our table to ask who our night was without an intro.  I just thought he was a drunk guy wandering around the place.  Not a great look for opening week, just sayin.

Come hungry!!! I was lucky enough to try several items on the menu, the Bob Armstrong Queso is to die for and the avocado tacos, lamb tacos, and stacked pork enchiladas are All delicious!!! I thought the wait staff was very pleasant and everyone genuinely seemed excited to be part of something new in Manhattan.  The place is very lively but not pretentious.  The owner is great and I appreciated him coming to our table to make sure everything was going well.

This is as banal a restaurant as one can imagine. Menu is EXACTLY what a tex mex restaurant on the side of the road in middle Oklahoma might offer, but at Nyc prices. No innovative dishes and very uninspired. One of the kind of joints in the city that begs the question: how did this even happen? 

Space looks like they designed it on a reality show in 12 hours on a minimal budget. Awful acoustics all around.

Wait staff was eager, but not very professional. 

Had some of the most mediocre food I've experienced in awhile. Nachos...yes, like u might microwave at home...no joke. Tacos: 2 tacos for $16. Doesn't say that on the menu and given the atmosphere, I assumed it would be at least 3 for that price, but two sad lamb tacos came out. Margarita was sour mix and cheap tequila with half of the glass dripping in salt and the other half vacant. It was as if I'd ordered a drink in a packed college bar. 

Basically, the place lacks pride and I think that is lazy of the owners and sad for the customers.

Amazingly good food, a taste of home coming from San Antonio. The guacamole had a great kick to it, the chili is all beef like it's supposed to be, margaritas are tasty and frozen, the enchiladas were divine and the service was exceptional. Start with the queso, end with the sopapillas and eat every thing inbetween. It's a taste of Texas on NYC and that's a great thing.

Popped into Javelina last night. Although the night got better, we initially waited 45 mins for our reservation. It was pretty frustrating mostly because the bar is TINY so there is really no room to comfortably wait. I would not come here to have a drink ever. That being said, once we sat down, the experience turned around. We were greeted right away with chips and salsa. Our waitress asked(kinda pushed) if we wanted to try the queso -- which we certainly did! We ordered the sampler and went with the Bob Armstrong since it included meat. The queso was awesome! Then we ordered some of the enchiladas, the tacos and quesadilla. Everyone loved their food. The drinks were also great too. The service was really good -- constantly checking in to refill our water, get new drinks, bringing the food out asap. The one thing people should keep in mind is this place is LOUD. On a thursday night, I felt like I was screaming across the table. I also thought value wise, the food and portion sizes were good. We ran into some friends from Texas who were pretty pumped to try Javelina. I checked in with them at the end of the dinner to find out their "local" thoughts. They said the queso was the best but they were 50/50 on their entrees. I probably would give a 3.5 but I bump up when the overall experience was positive.

LEGIT THE BEST RESTAURANT IN NYC!!! The food was insane and the staff was assembled of God's most beautiful creatures. I have never had a better meal in my lyfe. 4realz!!

Queso and guac on FLEEK! Avocado margs = the bomb dotcom. My Texas sous chef home-girl HOOKED. IT. UP. Me and mah GURLZ be having the best time eva at Javelina. 

You MUST go here if you want to TURN UP (on a Tuesday). The folks at Javey were more than supportive of our festive antics. They even gave use free shots (OTH - On the house) for being such great patrons.

@Javelina, welcome to the awesome New York Culinary Club. We'll be seeing you guys soon. 

Yours truly,
D$

Giving this place 2 stars, as someone from the bar staff jacked up the tip on my credit card.

My friend and I came had reservations for Monday night.  Hostess was super attentive and while we were early, encouraged us to have a drink at the bar.  

Bartender was super friendly and suggested we try the spicy jalapeno margaritas, which were delicious.  

Food was underwhelming; we had the queso trio (thumbs up!), fish tacos (overcooked) and the chicken enchilada (meh...).

Javelina may be the new kids on the block, but you would never know it based on the seamless service and fantastically tasty dishes. 

The avocado margaritas are quite literally to die for and the queso dip and guac start your dining experience with flavor and a little kick. The restaurant is a bit noisy, but that only adds to the lively ambiance. The open kitchen and smiling staff made the experience for myself and 7 friends (well accommodated for in spite of our group size and collective volume) absolutely amazing.

Amazing! As a true Texas to NYC transplant, I can safely say this restaurant serves true TEX MEX. The Mexican Martinis were delicious - very very similar to Trudy's in Austin, Texas. The queso flight was out of this world good. I was getting homesick just being there. The owner also came by and said hello to us and was so friendly! I'm definitely going to go back to this fine establishment!

I had the opportunity to come here for a pre opening event so I can comfortably say that most everything is great. 

When I came back as a paying customer I went with a less traditional dish and got the seafood enchiladas. They were fantastic. The sauce starts off a little sweet then comes at you with a nice bite (spicy). They were really really good. 

I assume someone will order them based on my recommendation and then shower me with compliments.

everything came out room temp or cold. $13 for two mushroom tacos the size of my pinky finger. queso had good flavor, but was rigid within 3mins of hitting the table. spent over $100 for 2ppl and went to otto's tacos on the way home. don't buy the hype, this place is severely mediocre.

There were tiny bits of sautéed onion in the cream gravy on my CFS. 

The horror... the hoooorrrooorrrrr.

Queso and drinks were pretty solid tho, way to rip off Curras and Trudy's.

*written by a heart sick central Texan.

The queso is good, the servers are friendly but a little clueless.  Overall food is mostly bland, and I wouldn't go back. 

We were on time for a Sunday evening reservation and waited at the bar for about 10-15 minutes while our table was opening up.  We managed to down an order of the Bob Armstrong queso and order a couple of drinks.  

We ended up seated at a table crammed in between the bar area and the dining room.  As two puffy coated diners were rushing by, one accidentally spilled a pint of water all over my date.  This wouldn't be a big deal but I had to walk to the back of the restaurant to get someone to deal with the situation.  Though the waitress I spoke to was apologetic, I was miffed that even after she notified the person who seemed to be a manager or owner, he didn't so much as bat an eye in our direction or bother to apologize.  

We asked to be moved to a new table and finished our meal.  Texas chili was beefy but not very flavorful.  Enchiladas de Tejas were bland with a spongey texture.  Shrimp fajitas had a nice char flavor.  It's rare for me to turn down rice and beans but these were quite possibly the most flavorless rice and beans I've had anywhere.  

We asked for the check and we were incorrectly charged and then had to wait another ten minutes (maybe it was less but I was pretty irked at this point in the night) to have the check adjusted before we could pay and leave.  

For mediocre food and oblivious service at these prices, not worth it.

I will give them a few benefits of the doubt - brand new, so I understand there are some kinks to work out,  waiter/service was good, the owner was visible and greeting lots of tables - hence the 2nd star.  Both food and drinks stink - at best.  We ordered the white queso which was okay. I personally think the cilantro did not add anything to the dish, only subtracted - I will take that as a personal preferrance but both of us agreed and he is fan of the herb.   Next were the tamales, cold and very dry - inedible;  we were glad to have kept the queso - it allowed us the ablility to add some mediocrity to a dry and bland dish.  (We were going to order the tacos but made the decision to not waste the money, time and calories - fortunate to see both the tacos and the fajitas at the table next to us, neither of which looked appetizing - so why?)  Bad food, lack of ambiance, bitter wine, warm beer, margaritas with no alcohol and an owner that obviously has no resteraunt experience but some business back ground = I was glad I tried it but will not go back for a very long time, if at all.  I was really excited for a good and affordable tex mex place in my neighborhood but both of us were highly disappointed.  Where are you "Los Dos Molinos"?

FINALLY!!! A Mexican place I can get behind. I have been eagerly awaiting my turn to try out this hot New Mexican place in gramercy. I made reservations almost a week in advance and last night I got to try it. 

While I was waiting for my friend to arrive I decided to grab a drink and some chips & salsa. I started out with the jalapeño margarita which was perfectly spicy and delicious. The chips were perfectly crispy and reminded me of the thin properly cooked chips I get in California. The salsa was delicious too. 

When my friend arrived we decided to order the queso sampler with Bob Armstrong yellow as the main event. It was delicious. I was dreaming of queso for days before we came to this restaurant. I was not disappointed. My only complaint was the queso was a bit more lukewarm then I would have liked it but it was still really good. 

Now when I got to a real Mexican spot I have to order a quesadilla. There is nothing better than a homemade flour tortilla with some goodness melted inside. This time I chose a shrimp quesadilla- it came with pico de gallo and guacamole. It was perfectly cooked and super delicious. I would highly recommend it. My friend ordered the enchiladas de tejas and they were equally as delicious. 

Finally for dessert they brought out complimentary sopapillas- nice touch! I was impressed I'll definitely be back

The food was generally good, though I wouldn't say it was anything earth shattering. For New York City Tex Mex, it's better than anything else. When comparing it to places in Austin or Dallas, this PALES in comparison. 

Also, I personally don't believe a Tex Mex dinner should be $60 per person (for 2 of us with tax and tip it was over $120). The prices they charge are obviously up to management decision, however I see the food as significantly over priced. 2 chicken taco entrée is $14. I would expect these to be large tacos, however when it came out I mistook it for an appetizer.

Finally, the only general comment I have for management is about the service. While it was attentive, they were slightly over-attentive at times. From the time my dining partner and I walked into the restaurant, to when we received the check, was less than 45 minutes. We felt extremely rushed in our meal! Call me old fashioned, but I'm thinking if a customer is willing to pay $60 per person for dinner, it should be a much more leisurely experience, that lasts at the very minimum, over 1 hour. 

The food was generally good and the cocktails were OK, but we're not looking to go back anytime soon.

Just went for a drink at the bar (a review about food will come in a couple of wks). The avocado cilantro margarita is GREAT!  It is so creamy and a wonderful choice for those of you who do not like sweet drinks.

I don't write many reviews but I needed to write one for this place. It is amazing. I really enjoyed the decor. Javelina feels inviting right when you walk in. The staff was very accommodating to my girlfriend and I, consistently checking in on us. The owner even stopped by and said hello.

The food was incredible. Definitely start with the Bob Armstrong Queso. I think I went through three baskets of chips before I had to stop myself. The steak fajitas were some of the best I have ever had. I don't know what they put on the steak strips but the flavor was amazing. The drinks were great and top it off with a complimentary cinnamon pastry dessert and I was a happy customer.

Definitely will be back!

I had to review to contradict the naysayers. I've been in NYC for 6 years -  I grew up in San Antonio, and call Austin home. This place is the only real deal in town.  And prices...well it's NYC.  You are not going to get 4.99 mexican plates here - that's to be expected.  The prices are reasonable.  The drinks are delicious.  Chips and salsa, YES please!  We had amazing service. The owner came by to say hello and check in - our server was kind, provided recommendations, and did not rush our table full of Texans despite the wait. We had the queso sampler (yay!) and I had the enchiladas de Tejas.  FINALLY, authentic chili con carne enchiladas!  This is how you know you've found an authentic place.  Avocado margarita was spot on.  In fact, I think they may be...wait for it, better than Curra's in Austin.  Gasp, I said it!  Only recommendation is that the sopapillas were overdone.  Other than that, keep it up Javelina, Texans all over the five boroughs welcome you with open arms!

Javelina = ADDICTING!  (I have been back 4 times already!! Shhhhh!!!)

Everything that I have tried on the menu has been awesome.  Not to mention the service is great (really friendly staff!) and the ambiance is cool.  If I had to recommend any items it would be the Bob Armstrong Queso, Avocado Margarita and the stacked Enchiladas!   

This place is a WIN WIN WIN in my book!

As I'm originally from the east coast, I had no idea what tex mex was or what to expect. This place completely blew me away- with fresh ingredients, bold flavor and a lively atmosphere! I didn't expect to like Queso as I consider myself somewhat of a cheese connoisseur -- but I am officially addicted to this godly melted cheese with amazing add ins. I've now been to Javelina twice and am obsessed with the Mag Mud Queso! The sangria margarita swirl is out of this world, I can't believe no one has every mixed 2 of my faves together before!! No doubt I will become a regular here and if you haven't yet been to Javelina, I would make a rez ASAP (they are quite busy!).

I had a major flash back to the Ground Round in Rochester, NY during my college days, the year is not important...Back in those days there was a special on Monday nights that went something like this, $5 for all the draught beer, chili con queso and chips you could ingest, ahhhhh, the memories... But I digress... I scored a rockin 6:15 rese at Javelina on a Wednesday night and was uber excited to try it until I read some of the scathing comments readers of Eater had written about the fact that they think Eater is on the take with the place. I walked in right on time and the place was already jammed. The decor is nothing to speak of and the space is very generic but the Hostess was sweet! We were seated right away at the end of the booth. My bf had ordered the Texas Mule and it was an OK rendition of the Moscow kind. Our waitress was super sweet and attentive. The chips and salsa to start were a touch above average and the Pacifico draught was icy cold and hit the spot. We ordered the Bob Armstrong queso and here is where all those college Monday nights came flooding back....fondly I might add. The queso could have been a bit warmer but we did proceed to lick the bowl clean. For an entree we split the steak fajitas. Were these good? yes, were they any different from fajitas at Applebees, TGIF, or any other chain that has fajitas? No..errr, not that I would know first hand but from what I've heard ; ). The flour tortillas were standand as were the accoutrements. All in all this was a perfectly fine meal you would expect at some hole in the wall place on the LES, certainly not a destination nor worth a two hour wait or 30 day out rese,

This is as close to Tex Mex as possible in NYC, but still falls short to Texas Tex Mex. 

Food: Traditional queso and tortillas were delicious! The refried beans were good, but badly needed salt. The rice was undercooked. For the price of the tacos, they should really come with rice and beans. Fried avocado tacos were good, but needed some spice. Chicken fajitas were a little too dry.

Drinks: Traditional margarita on the rocks was not good or traditional. The first margarita I had tasted like sugar water. The waiter informed me it was made with tequila, lime juice, and agave. Sorry, that's not a margarita. He was kind enough to replace my drink and swap the agave for triple sec. Something still didn't taste right, so I'm not sure what actually went into my drink. Shiner on tap is always a plus though!

I would come back for Shiner and queso, but probably skip the food/margaritas and wait until I'm back in the Republic.

What a difference a few months makes. I recently visited Javelina again after they initially opened and they have really really gotten it together. 

The queso and drinks are still really delicious. The jalapeño margarita is spicy and not too sweet. if you have never had queso I feel bad for you

I might have to make their stacked enchiladas with an egg my go-to hangover meal. Or at least it will always be on my mind every time I am hungover from now until eternity. The pork in it was awesome it was super tasty.  My friend got the fajitas. Which he claims are as good as the local fajitas from when he missed from when he lived in Houston

The front of house staff was knowledgable and really attentive. 

Only quibble is that it's really loud. But the manager told me they are planning to install sound baffling which will make this place awesomer. 

Glad I gave them another try. Will be back!

Thanks to tips from other reviewers, we made a reservation so we didn't have to wait long for a table. We started with margaritas and they were really good if a little pricey (when it comes to margaritas I still hold out hope I'll find Texas prices on these somewhere in the city... a girl can dream). The complimentary chips and salsa is a nice and very authentically Tex-Mex, but the salsa was REALLY mild. It barely even tasted like peppers. It seems like a nice base, consistency and everything was good, just needs a few more peppers and it would be really good. The Bob Armstrong dip was also too mild, but we asked for some jalapenos and stirred those in and then it was delicious. Definitely the best/most authentic Tex-Mex queso in the city! After how mild the salsa and queso were, I was a little worried the chili con carne on my Enchiladas de Tejas would be a disappointment, but I am glad to say I had nothing to worry about. The enchilada sauce was excellent! We'll definitely be back! So excited to have a place to get queso!

Delicious food with southern hospitality!

I've been to Javelina 4 times since it opened the last 3 weeks because I'm simply obsessed! 

1) Decor - really cute and original Texas charm. Love the turquoise pony hair booth - where else are you going ot get that??
2) Drinks - best marg on the rocks in the city- hands down!
3) Food is on point - BM Queso is the best by far- you gotta try it! Even the intro salsa is delish.  For main, I really loved the carnitas enchiladas and the black and refried beans are the best I've ever had!!! And complimentary desert was so freaking good!!!
4) Staff is SO friendly- you would have no idea you're in NYC and the owner graciously walks around greeting guests and chatting, making you feel extra welcome!

Can't wait for my 6th visit!

Being a Houston native, Javelina's food was overall good however 

We started off the dinner by ordering the queso with beef. Queso was delicious and probably the best I have had in NYC. However, the chips seemed a bit over fried and stale. The salsa was meh and not very memorable.

The steak fajitas were okay and didn't come out sizzling as I had hoped for. The rice was a tad dry and wasn't that appetizing. The frozen margarita was on the sweet side and watery.

Service was a bit on the slow side. I would probably return for the queso.

Thank you small baby Jesus for bringing New York City the miracle of REAL TEX-MEX. I knew when I walked into this space and had the first sip of my frozen margarita that I had found the Holy Grail.  
Javelina is unreal! Finally there is a place that has Tex Mex that tastes like home.  I loved it so much on Friday night that I brought my entire Texas Family back on Sunday night. Tex Mex is a staple meal once or twice a week, so I will be back for MUCH more. The chefs were amazing and all from Texas so they knew how we Texans like it. 
The Queso Sampler is a MUST (i loved the Mag Mud one, it tasted the closest to Lupe Tortillas/Escalantes queso), the Frozen Avacado/Cilantro Margarita is unbelievable, and the fajitas are heaven! I also tried the Avacado Tacos (YUM!), the enchiladas (finally good enchiladas) and the Quesadilla (thank you!). 
It is a small space and very crowded so make sure you make reservations! I will be back once a week!

Based on all the positive reviews I read, my expectations were very high -- the food surpassed those expectations.  The puff taco was a great combination of crunchy taco and slow cook tender meat.  The queso sampler was so much more than just melted cheese--each bite revealed a special spice or ingredient highlighting the wonderful flavor--hands down the best queso I've had. 
I'm not a Tex-mex expert but the atmosphere feels authentic and the friendly staff gave great recommendations.  I'm looking forward to returning to try the rib eye and enjoy another jalapeño margarita.   The only downside is trying to get a reservation - we had to get a 9:30pm table on a Monday night and the place was still jammed.

Finally a decent tex mex restaurant ! It has all the hiccups of a new restaurant - with service being a little confusing and slow.  But everyone was very friendly and apologetic for the long wait times. We did get a free guac because we waited so long for our food.  The guac was delicious- very fresh and a tiny bit spicy. Drinks - margaritas - solid!   I had the fish tacos which were tasty but my friend got the fajitas and they were incredible !! Also don't forget to order the queso. Yummmmyyy. Had the white queso which super delicious.  I'm a cheese-a-holic though so maybe my opinion is skewed.  My friends thought the queso was very good but not "the best thing in life ever" as I described it.  Enchiladas were great too.  You def need a reservation bc the space is tight and the bar area is small so I wouldn't want to wait there.

If Tex Mex means no flavor and weak drinks then this place is a sure winner.  The beans and rice taste like they were from a can and a box.  

They forgot the appetizer, the famed, "queso" and one drink was so horrible that I'd rather drink NyQuil.  

Did this chef not learn anything from his experience at Rosa Mexicana and Hill Country?!?

Javelina is good eats. 
We didn't have reservations so came and took seats at the bar. The bartenders were friendly. We ordered traditional and jalapeño margaritas, both were very good. 
Started with the nachos - the refried beans were great and the nachos reminded me of the kind I had when visiting San Antonio as a kid. Crunchy, rich, cheesy. 
We had tacos for our entrees. The mushroom and guacamole. The former was very good, the latter was creamy with a crisp coating on the guac, good but we added some spices to it to kick it up a bit. I had the fish tacos which were great. 
Didn't even realize the menu had a backside but we were stuffed. Next time I will try the chicken fajitas. 
Seems like we finally have some real tex mex in town. 
(Sorry folks, they don't do dessert).

We made reservations like a month ago and were seated at table with another party, separated only by an empty chair -- very odd. 
The drinks were strong and delicious, but at $13-$14 each they better be. The over priced drink situation in NYC is getting out of control. It's kind of offensive... 
The food - 
The quesadillas were not cheesy enough and didn't have enough shrimp, but still good. 
The quesos, all delicious.
The country chicken fried steak was my least fave dish. We had to ask for salt. The gravy had zero flavor and the meat was very hard to chew. The tamal that it was served with was very good.  We were so confused about the lack Of flavor we told the waiter. He offered an apology and that's it 
My favorite dish was the Pork Stacked enchiladas Roosevelt style. Although very oily it had great flavor. 
Complimentary deserts were delicious.

Immediately saw down to warm chips and great salsa with a real nice heat to it. Jalapeno margaritas are outstanding (also perfect heat) as were the frozen avocado ones... Did the queso sampler and as someone who isn't that familiar with queso it was worth all the hype! So so good! My oklahomian dining partner concurred with this assessment. I had the veggie fajitas which came out sizzling with some of the best flour tortillas I've ever had. My friend had the brisket quesadillas which he said were totally legit/awesome and he also tried the country fried steak which he said could use some refining. All ingredients were extremely fresh... Those fried little donuty things at the end were a great touch. All this with A+ service as well.

Sadly, our reservation wasn't honored (we were first told it would be a 30 min wait, then a few minutes later told it would 45 to an hour) after my girlfriend had called many days in advance and Javelina had called to confirm the day of for an 8:30 reservation. The restaurant had booked to have 170+ people seated at 8:30 when that clearly wasn't possible. 

I also spoke to two couples who had arrived early for their reservations and had been waiting for nearly an hour without being seated. We were starving and couldn't afford to wait in the overcrowded restaurant. 

I would have loved to have been able to review the food and drinks but didn't get the chance!

Food is great. Went 2 days in a row.  The Bob Armstrong queso is a must; however when we went early the second time, it was lukewarm.  The cheese enchiladas are a must if it's your first time trying tex mex. Big kudos to one of the partners stopping by and chatting for a bit. I would have given five stars if the queso was super hot when going in at 12pm when they just opened.

Definitely the best Tex Mex in NYC... Make reservations for dinner or go for lunch. Expect a good, young scene. Great margaritas and yellow Bob Armstrong queso. This place is my new favorite. Not sure why it's not atleast a 4.5 on yelp... I live 2 blocks away, it's the best. The owner even came over to say hello and introduce himself.

In my seemingly never ending journey to find decent Tex-Mex in the city, I came here last week with two fellow Texans only to be severely underwhelmed. After a two-hour wait (very thankful for text alerts), we were seated and immediately ordered what our Lone Star stomachs were craving: queso, which was the only thing that felt up to par. My friends ordered an avocado and jalapeno margarita, which were average at best. We split an order of the parrillada mixta, which was effectively an extension of your standard fajita plate to include a few other meats. Found every item on the skillet to be very bland. I know I have biased point-of-view because I happen to have been born and bred on Tex-Mex but this was sub-standard to the already very average Tex-Mex options in the city. 

The journey continues (or will never be)... One star for the queso and one star for the friendly services but outside of that, very overrated.

Had a solid dining experience last week at Javelina.  Went with another Texan friend, and we were excited to test drive a new place that offered a taste of home.  

We started off with the Bob Armstrong queso - queso with beef and guac?  Why not?  I really didn't get much quac, but the queso was good and even better on the fajitas we ordered next.  The chips were VERY salty, so of course we needed cocktails to wash them down.  I had my heart set on sangria, but unfortunately they were "out."  But then our server, Hallie, mentioned that the last couple times she worked they didn't have sangria either.  HEY JAVE, IF YOU HAVE SANGRIA ON YOUR MENU, MAYBE YOU SHOULD HAVE IT IN YOUR RESTAURANT!  I settled for a manhattan instead, which was smooth and boozy (as it should be).  My friend ordered the mexican margarita and enjoyed it.

The fajita plate (steak) had enough meat for 4-5 tacos, along with sliced peppers and onions, rice, beans, pico, and a dollop of guacamole.  But the tortilla dish only has 3 tortillas, which is odd for people sharing a fajita plate.  They gave us 2 more when we asked. 
Unfortunately there wasn't a little pot holder glove on the sizzling skillet they brought out, so when the guy pushed the skillet onto the table, it made contact with (and burned!) my ringer finger on my right hand.  I suggested to Hallie that they invest in the little handles ASAP.  Also, ouch.  

We ordered a second round of drinks, which got lost.  I should back up and say that when we were seated at 6:03 (we were a few minutes late for our 6pm reservation, but they were ready for us!) we were one of three tables.  However, by 6:30 the tables and bar were getting full, and by 7 it was so loud I couldn't hear myself think.  I actually had to ask my friend to stop talking because I couldn't hear her and it was stressing me out - on a Wednesday night!  So I totally understand the other reviewers who had long wait times.  I'd suggest getting here before 6:30 or after 8:30.  

Our server noticed after our meal was done that we never got our second round.  I noticed her go up to the bar, wave a ticket at the bartender, and ask him to rush on the drinks.  When she turned around, I asked her just to cancel the drinks - we wanted them with food, and the food was long gone.  Nicely, Elena (manager?) came over, apologized, said they were slammed and our drinks just slipped through the cracks, and offered to give us the round on her.  How nice!  Of course we accepted.  I had another manhattan; my friend had the avocado margarita and did not like it.  It tasted more like food than it did a drink.

For dessert, we didn't see a menu but they brought out two warm sopapilla kindof things with honey - yum.  And the restrooms have pictures of Beyonce and Matthew McConaughey for ladies and gents, naturally.  (Bathroom wasn't as nice as I expected for such a new place, but hey.  Shit happens.) 

TL;DR: Still getting their sea legs.  Food is solid; worth a visit if you love TexMex but don't come between 6pm and 8pm.  No happy hour (yet?).
Avocado margaritas are a must! Amazing food and service! I will be returning again and again!

I went to Javelina for a group dinner over the weekend. We had a reservation, but still had to wait over 45 minutes to be seated. The food was mediocre, but for the steep prices (re: $17 tacos, $20 enchiladas, $25 fajitas) I was expecting a lot more in terms of both quality and quantity. Why would I pay $15 for two small fish tacos, when I can get superior ones at truly a fraction of the cost at dozens of other places in the city? I was also unimpressed with the interior, which made the place feel like a chain restaurant because of the cheap lighting and overabundance of tables and chairs. Because of the mediocre quality of food and shockingly high prices at this restaurant, I will not be returning.

Went last night; easily the worst meal of the year so far. The hostess seemed lost, they were out of prickly pear margaritas, and my puffy taco was a total disaster. A sponge full of grease. Disgusting. If I hadn't had one in San Antonio I wouldn't know how far they missed the mark ...

I thought this place was great! NYC has been needing a REAL Tex-Mex place, and they are real deal! Yes, it's more than you would pay in TX - but this is NYC! I'm sure their rent is like 90859 times more than it would be in TX, for like 1/4th of the space.

Good variety on the menu - pretty much everything you would want to order from a Mexican place. I had the chicken enchiladas and they were on point. Loved the refried beans as well. The rice was OKAY, wasn't bad by any means but could have had a bit more flavor.

We started our meal with the queso trio which tasted like it was from a place in TX. I've definitely been missing it the last 10 years I've been in NYC. You gotta try it! The chips and salsa were great too, and they were quick to refill the chips every time our basket got a little low. Waitstaff was super nice and attentive and they owner even stopped by to chat. Also LOVE the fact that they have real, homemade flour tortillas. Most NYC places do not, and the store bought ones are just awful!  

The Mexican Martini was good, but seemed very small. I also had a plain frozen marg which was just OK - I probably would not order that again. The drinks are very pricey for what you get.

We finished our meal with a basket of sopapillas (on the house). They were pretty good too. 

I'm super excited for this place to start offering brunch and BREAKFAST TACOS that had been missing in NYC. I really hope they have a deal on brunch drinks or a boozy unlimited brunch option...that would be amazing. Even if they have great breakfast tacos, I can't be paying $12 per mimosa and bloody mary...I like to get DRUNK at brunch and do not enjoy paying $200 to do so =)

I will definitely be back.

I just died in your arms tonight. Three kinds of queso and one of them was MAD MUG = QUESO ON FLEEK. Margs are also on point at this tex mex joint!  #texmex #javelina #nyc 

Ok. For real. I haven't tried their entrees so I can't 100% talk to their food, hence the four stars. I will be back. Let me tell you that. I came here tonight, a nice Friday night in April, around 5pm as we were just over that work week. You know how that is. We've all been there. Luckily there were two seats at the bar. Score. It was the off corner nubbin where the bar backs are always shuffiling around drinks. Nothing that bad but annoying.  Anywho- we good the queso sampler - white, yellow and mad mug. King. Well, I lived in Austin for grad school and my life at that time had revolved around socializing, tex mex, men, and school (actually in that order), so I was over the moon to try this place as Tacombi (my neighborhood joint) had been getting repetitive. Go try it. Just prepare to wait or get there earlier than you'd think as my new 60 yr old adjacent bar stool friend told me: "The New Yorker wrote about this place. Prepare for the onslaught of crazies."

Queso sampler.
Queso sampler.
Queso sampler.

Make a reservation right now; then go back to reading reviews. Honestly, I'd give 4 stars to a sewer that had a queso sampler like this. I don't need to move to Austin anymore because now NYC has guacamole-queso. The weakest queso (as if there is such a thing) was the "traditional" yellow cheese one.

Service was incredibly friendly -- we got a chip refill without even asking, and the chips were warm! Not a perfect 5 stars because I'd skip the tacos next time. For $13 for two tacos, I wanted way more flavor. The fried avocado ones were fine but not special. That queso tho...

Finally, some great Tex Mex in NYC!!! It's been a long time coming and Javelina does not disappoint. The decor and the vibe was great on a Friday night. We started with margaritas and queso. There is nothing like an awesome white cheese queso! Margaritas were on par with other places, so nothing extra special there. 

We had the chicken enchiladas and the chicken fajitas. Both were fantastic. The owner came over to chat, which we really appreciated and hardly ever happens in NYC. Have been recommending to friends and will be back very soon!

Can't rave about this place enough. So good we had to go two nights in a row during a short visit to NYC. Best queso I've had. Unreal avocado tacos. Even more unreal pork shoulder tacos. Quite possibly perfect steak fajitas -- and a magnificent jalapeño margarita. Add a charming space with amazing service and you have my new favorite tex-mex restaurant; just wish there was a location back in LA!

Fun place to dine (it was quite loud but the waitress was pretty good) at and you will never leave hungry! Complimentary chips and my other friends shared while I chose the fried chicken steak "Cowboy" style: with chili and cheese. It tasted flavorful, delicious and I enjoyed the rice that came with it.

Made reservations a month ago for last Saturday. Was not disappointed! Ordered the avocado margarita, guacamole, and fried avocado tacos. Obviously, I'm obsessed with avocados. First of all, they bring out complimentary chips and salsa. Chips were puffy and golden. Salsa was mild with a fruity tang. Next I received the margarita. It was incredibly creamy, a very subtle cilantro taste. Amazing. Next was the guacamole. It was not the best guac I've ever had, but they gave you a nice portion and the guacamole had plenty of tomatoes, which I prefer. Last, the TACOS. The order only came with two but... They were huge! I was shocked. The fried avocado tacos came with a black bean spread and lime slaw on top. I was in tex mex heaven. These tacos are a must. Overall, I was really satisfied. However, the prices are ridiculous. My boyfriend ordered enchiladas and a beer. Everything came out to 75. For Mexican food, it's a little steep. But I'd come back for special occasions!

Overall, loved it!
We showed up at 5:45, and thank goodness we did. Hostess asked if we had a reservation, we didn't, so she had to scramble to find us a table, as most were reserved come 6:00. (And it's true, once 6:00 hit, and the place FILLED up.)

We came for appetizers and drinks.
Started with margaritas and Shiner on tap. Enjoyable drinks. The Sangria Swirl is great. Always a fan. Avocado/Cilantro marg was great too.
Ordered the queso sampler, got something else. After solving the communication with our waiter, we got the sampler. Good stuff. Haven't had queso like that in NYC ever. I'd recommend the white queso. Yessir.
Also had the Bob Armstrong (with white queso). That's the way to go.
Sidenote, our chips and salsa were constantly being replenished.. "LIKE"

Ordered some chicken quesadillas for the table. Loved them. A bit on the spicy side from the jalepeno sauce inside.

Ordered a few more appetizers.. which never came :/ So we were a little disappointed.

Food... Great!
Drinks... Great!
Atmosphere... awesome vibe/cool decor. A little chaotic, but still enjoyable.
Service...below average. But forgiving as he seemed like he was still learning. But he better learn QUICKLY ;)

We did meet either the manager or owner, awesome dude. Redeemed the poor waitstaff.

But with bottomless chips and salsa (in NYC?!) and killer Tex-Mex queso dip, who wouldn't at least try it? But make your reservation!

I'll go back, with hope that the service will be a bit more versed.

Let me start by saying, this is the first review i have ever posted....and i felt compelled to do so, because of how much i disagree with the positive ratings for this restaurant.  The tortilla soup was quite viscous, and tasted somewhere between ketchup and chili con carne, and the brisket tacos  and the tortilla chips were similarly chewy.  Service was weak-- at one point, we had 5 empty glasses piled up on the table, and we were attempting to wave down the servers the whole meal.  I must add that the accoustics in the resto produce a deafening din... will not go back... and my four dinner companions concurred.

Food was really good. From the chips and salsa, to the puffy tacos with roasted pork and the post meal churros...top notch. 

My dining companion and I felt rushed by various employees trying to take our dishes before we were done eating and our server brought us the bill promptly and stalked it as we continued to finish our cocktails. The two girls at the table next to us who were mid meal when we arrived did not face the same treatment. Not sure if they were trying to turn over tables quickly but we were not lingering. 

The atmosphere was loud and energetic. Not a spot for a quiet dinner. 

Highly recommend the avocado and cilantro margarita. It was like a creamy avocado smoothie with a tequila kick! 

4 stars for food and drink, minus one for being rushed out and the intense volume

This review is long overdue...

After coming across a post about Javelina's opening, I read the article, and realized this place looked LEGIT. I immediately sent the link to my boyfriend with an "OMG!" comment attached...and he (being the doll he is) sent me a reservation confirmation email within 5 minutes. 

I'm a relocated Texan, originally from Dallas, who went to college in West Texas, and lived in Austin for 6 years. I have literally never been so excited to go eat somewhere. Just seeing familiar terms on the menu made me nostalgic. The space and decor actually reminds me of Austin. I believe company who designed Javelina is actually based out of Austin.

Of all the cuisine choices in NYC...Tex-Mex is the one thing missing. Our visit to Javelina did not disappoint. The Bob Armstrong dip, avocado 'rita, jalapeno rita, and puffy tacos were all fantastic. I can't wait to go back and try the rest of the menu!

You've got to be kidding me.  So I'm still sitting here waiting on an order of puffy tacos and I had to write a review.  I had read about the opening of Javalina on Urban Daddy and had already tried to come on the day that was posted to be their opening day, but either UD was wrong or they were behind schedule for the build out.  I'm Texan and while I see plenty of Mexican food restaurants in the city, I was beyond excited to see Tex-Mex.  

But I feel like I'm in the Pace Picante commercial, "Neeew York City?!"  Don't bother.  Supposedly chefs/owners are from Houston, Dallas and Austin.  Dudes - you are not representing!  (Though I did laugh as someone sure likes Chuy's, i.e. Jalapeño ranch).  But I mean come on.  I get chips with no hot sauce - waiter was completely off his game.  Then when I receive the bowl of hot sauce it lacks any heat whatsoever.  Are you scared the Northerners can't handle the heat?  And I know you've eaten at Pappasitos - those chips and sauce are addicting due to texture and flavor.  You could be knocking this out of the park with 3 Texans!!!

I order an avocado and cilantro margarita (who the hell serves this in TX?  Last time I even saw a Prickly Pear margarita I was sitting in a boat on Lake Travis like 15 years ago. Isn't jalapeño/Serrano/habenaro the way to measure up these days?). I took one sip of the avocado margarita and sent it back.  Plus the glass wasn't rimmed, it was slathered down to the base on one side with salt.  Are you trying to get turned on by a gal licking her glass top to bottom?

Let's get to food.  I LOVE brisket tacos and I have yet to see them invade NYC.  Some of these BBQ joints should recognize we like our meat many ways.  I started with the brisket tacos, thinking this would be my dinner.  I'm a 5'1" petite gal who hadn't eaten anything until 7pm.  Well the brisket tacos were ala carte (this would rarely happen, if ever in TX, unless I had requested them like this) and maybe 3 bites at most each.  You want brisket tacos, go to Gloria's in DFW.  They should be grilled soft corn tortillas with juicy pulled beef brisket, melted from the grill shredded cheese and grilled marinated onions.  These were dry brisket, what felt like straight out of a bag soft corn tortillas, sliced and grilled onions/peppers (though I had requested this item with no onions.). There was a sauce on the side termed "jalapeño gravy," but I'd say it was far from that description.  It did have good flavor for my non salted tortilla chips though.

Since I was still hungry after having the brisket tacos....Now the puffy tacos, I should have ordered these from the start, but I was picturing them to be super greasy.  Well they aren't corn tortillas.  They are fried tortas - think 1/4 inch thick masa, fried and shaped like a taco.  Flavor of the pork was decent, again a bit dry, but I think the torta would have fallen apart is the meat were wet.  It was already falling apart from having been laid on guacamole and shredded iceberg lettuce.  So if you go, try this item first and according to the manager, have some queso.  

Doubt I'll come back.  It was super crowded, but I honestly don't suspect Javalina will make it in the long haul unless it steps up the game.  This is a foodie town with a serious lack of Tex Mex.  But imo it's still lacking.

I REALLY wanted to like this place as the menu looks fantastic (puffy tacos in NYC?!?), but sadly everything was bland and flavorless (the one exception being the guacamole which was actually quite tasty.) The queso, which I was looking forward to most of all, can't even compare with the likes of Moe's, much less the real stuff I miss so much (real Texas queso isn't just melted cheese - there needs to be some bite to cut through the creaminess.)

And if that weren't bad enough, the cost to portion size ratio is poor - everything is far too expensive for what you get, even by NYC standards. Which I might be willing to overlook if the quality was there, given the dearth of quality Mexican/Tex-Mex food up here, but it wasn't.

Service was decent and aside from the chips nothing tasted stale; it was just all so bland. Mexican food doesn't have to be excessively spicy, but it does need to be flavorful, and that just wasn't there. I'm hoping they can turn things around though - there is a severe lack of good Mexican and Tex-Mex options in this city, and if they would only bring some flavor to their food and cut the prices by $2 on everything on the menu this could be a great place.

A bunch of buzz right now for Javelina and their bringing "true Tex-Mex" to NYC.  The restaurant was packed on a Friday night, with the hostess quoting a 1.5 hour wait for people walking in without reservations.  Hope those people didn't wait.

The service was very prompt and the food was good.  We ordered the queso sampler with the Bob Armstrong, which is queso with guac and brisket mixed in.  That was a winner.  My friends had two types of fajitas -- steak and shrimp -- which got good reviews; tortillas received praise.  I ordered the West Texas Enchiladas with pork, which is basically a Tex-Mex lasagna -- cool concept and good execution.

Drinks were solid, and came quickly.  Dessert bites came compliments of the chef, if you have any room after the large portions.

Ended up being about $65 pp with a shared app, entree each and two rounds of drinks, which was very fair.  Overall, we were happy with the meal, but by no means is Javelina worthy of going out of your way for -- especially if you're planning on going out after (food babies aren't so sexy).  Seems destined to be a solid spot for locals planning to go crash back on their couch afterward.
I don't know what all the hype is about. This place has good atmo but average food at best. Sort of a waste of a meal.

IN SHORT: Is Tex-Mex better in Texas? Yes. Is Javelina still the closest thing the Big Apple has to the comfort food of the Lone Star state, full of cheap ground beef and yellow cheese product? Probably. Is it worth a visit for their Prickly Pear Margarita or Mexican Martini, if nothing else? Absolutely.

THE STORY: The day Javelina opened, I received a frantic email from my best Texas friend with the press release followed by a few simple words expressing the sheer magnitude of her euphoria that Shiner Bock was finally on tap at what claimed to be an unabashedly Tex-Mex restaurant filling a void in New York City's dining scene:

"Literally crying tears of joy right now."

This is exactly why Javelina is a success. It seems as if every Texas transplant to the city has embraced the laid-back space that promised to pay homage to the many cities and specialties of the Tex-Mex tradition, and they've all swarmed upon Javelina with a friend by their side.

On my first dinner here with my Texas expert (already on her third or fourth visit, I've lost count), our waiter immediately asked if we wanted to start with any queso or margaritas, immediately setting the tone and guiding us through the rest of our meal. I was dutifully instructed to begin with the best queso on the menu, the Bob Armstrong, a traditional yellow queso from Matt's El Rancho in Austin with guacamole, ground beef, pico de gallo, and sour cream that must then be stirred. The texture is lighter and thinner than I expected from my previous experiences with Velveeta and Rotel, but was so addictively good that I had to break up my tortilla chips into small pieces to maximize the chip to queso ratio. I guess my only other option was to drink it like a bowl of soup, but I'm telling myself I'm better than that.

From the recommendation of our waiter, I also tried the Prickly Pear Margarita, a sweet and sour concoction that hits all the right notes of a drink meant to accompany comfort food, and the Mexican Martini, with reposado tequila cointreau, olive juice, and fresh lime.

The Brisket tacos, while certainly true to Tex-Mex cuisine and topped with a jalapeno gravy that added the ideal spice and a fresh complexity to the dish, unfortunately suffered from beef brisket that was tough and overcooked. The Fish tacos fared a bit better, with lightly grilled mahi mahi, house pickled jalapenos for a bit of sweetness, guacamole, and queso fresco for a balance of salt and creaminess. Perhaps the food is better experienced by tastebuds numbed by a few too many margaritas.

The popularity of the sparsely decorated space also contributes to another classic feature of the Tex-Mex experience: a powerfully loud dining room with service that tries to turn tables over at least 3 times every night. It might be hard on the ears, but the excitement and rush on the space seems to have everyone eager to come back for more.

Yes, there are still inevitable flaws in food that tries to replicate a particular cuisine too closely while taking measured, restrained risks in innovation, but if this is the best New York can do with Tex-Mex and authentically unauthentic Mexican food, I'm sold.

I likely need to go again (I didn't eat much there), but based on what I did eat I'd say this is a pretty cool spot. I'm no Texan, therefore I have little to compare it to, but their queso trio was delicious to me. My favorite was the Bob Armstrong with the little ground beef pieces in it. My date got a steak taco and I got the House Salad with shrimp. It was very tasty and was one of those salads where you doubt it's "healthy" because it tastes so yummy. I also had two of the traditional margaritas on the rocks, both were delicioso! 

I'd love to return and try their guacamole and an entree. The atmosphere is casual, yet very cute and bright. The service was good. All in all a great experience. I will be back!

Sunday night dinner review:

I liked the fascade of this place but opened the door to a moderate sound assault, reminded me of the volume in the Smith UWS location which I also find unpleasant aurally.  We sat down in time but our waiter was not to be seen for about 15-20 minutes, another server seemed a little annoyed to be flagged down as we were attempting to obtain some beverages.

Upon his arrival he was pleasant and attentive. A shared order of guacamole was nicely prepared and flavored. Our server then went back to wherever he was hiding previously.

After another pause our food was brought to the table.  I had ordered the fish tacos.  They were fresh, tasty and overall pretty good. They don't quite have the snap of a good California taco but for the east coast it was a good performance. The brisket tacos were well received by others in my party and the chicken fajitas were on par.

Our server then once again retreated until well after the main courses had been removed from the table.  He returned well rested from his nap to offer a dessert menu but our party was ready to depart by that time.

Conclusion: good food, slow service, loud 3.5 stars

Being a native Texan, there was no way I could resist the temptations and praises of Javelina - one of New York's new Tex-Mex restaurants. 

I came here on a Sunday night and it was packed. My friend and I got right down to business. We ordered the queso sampler with the Bob Armstrong, white cheese and traditional cheese. We got a bowl of guacamole as well, and it tasted so fresh. You can also add jalapeños to it to add some hotness. We went for hot (not too hot at all). 

Queso, contrary to popular belief, is not just cheese dip. It achieves a silky, creamy consistency that is an art. I am a huge fan of the Bob Armstrong. We got the traditional cheese with beef, guac, & pico. Tastes just like I remember it from home. My friend loved the white cheese - claims it's like nothing she has ever had before. The guacamole was smooth and it had a nice spicy kick to it. We saved most of it for our entree!

By the time we were finished with the appetizer, we were honestly very close to being full, as we ate a lot of chips with the queso and salsa and guac. I ordered the skirt steak fajita and she ordered some steak quesadillas. Trust me - this is more than enough. The steak fajita was served on a sizzling hot skillet. There were red peppers, onions and queso (get the "sunset" style) and of course steak. The dish was accompanied by all the regular fajita fillings (sour cream, salsa, guacamole, tortillas). The quesadilla was less novel and also served with the three sides. Had sides of rice and beans as well.

Overall, I would give this restaurant a solid 4. It brings some great Tex-Mex food to the city, but it does come at a premium.

We were very excited to try Javelina as we had a reservation for several weeks. We finally dined there on a Sunday night. Sadly, it was very underwhelming. It was very crowded, but we got seated within a few minutes (oddly, the hostess at first declined to seat us because another party with a reservation 15 minutes before us was late and she wanted to wait for them to show up... is that our problem?)

The good: 
Puffy tacos ($18), loved the homemade corn tortillas and at least this was an interesting and unique dish. This came with two tacos but they seemed to be a better value than the brisket tacos (below) because they were larger.

Queso, for the brief moment in time that it was hot, I enjoyed this a lot. (But it got cold very very fast, maybe it should be served in something that retains heat better).

The bad:
Took 25+ minutes after we were seated for our waitress to acknowledge us and take our drinks order. Food was even longer! She was visibly annoyed when I stated we had been ready for a long time. Waitress was generally frazzled (she may have been training?) and extremely, painstakingly slow. Not sure if they are understaffed? 

Chips and salsa - while I appreciated that these were complimentary (that is actually the standard at any Mexican restaurant elsewhere but not always in NYC), the salsa had absolutely no kick to it and while it was fresh, it was not nearly flavorful enough.

My avocado-cilantro margarita  ($14) tasted creamy, but nothing like avocado OR cilantro. When I asked the waitress about this she said it varies batch to batch based on how it's made. Hmmm....not a good sign.

Jalapeno margarita ($12-$14?) was not spicy at all. Tasted 100% of margarita mix, no fresh lime or jalapeno flavor.

Queso ($8) - for the brief time it was hot, it was tasty, but it became cold quickly. Waitress did not bring us chips when the queso came out so we had to wait for a fresh basket which prolonged getting to eat it.

Brisket tacos ($16) - brisket was so dry, not tender at all, and dish was not hot when it arrived. Extremely small portion of two small tacos.

Overall:
I LOVE Mexican food and was surprised that all of the food we had at Javelina was not spicy at all. Maybe Tex-Mex is not supposed to be spicy? I've never been to Texas but am from California so am used to Mexican food and it's my favorite cuisine! Everything seemed fresh, but left a lot to be desired. It was just mediocre and almost flavorless. The service was the even bigger issue, but to be fair, the manager Elena was EXTREMELY apologetic and accommodating when I complained about all of the things listed above, and that is why they are getting 3 stars rather than 1-2. They will probably improve with time, or, we may have just had a terrible experience because I see lots of solidly good reviews here from other people!
I LOVE THIS PLACE! Happily greeting by a sweet hostess named Jenna and served by perfect bartender named Laci! Definitely returning for that delicious queso :)

So I wasn't planning on writing a review, but figured given my experience (and a review written recently here on Yelp by someone who was sitting right next to us, I would need to).

I made reservations around 3 weeks ago for this past Sunday at 6:30pm (it was the soonest I could get in at a convenient time, which was fine because I figured it'd be worth it). Also worth nothing I recently tried El Original, the other self-proclaimed "tex-mex" restaurant in Hell's Kitchen. Javelina easily wins round 1, but I'll be back to try both again.

First, my experience: 

Friendly staff, from top to bottom.

Very loud inside, not sure that's anything they can fix, but also goes to show how busy they are.

Queso - very good, originally ordered the queso sampler, but only the Bob Armstrong came out. That was the one I wanted to try the most and I knew if we sent it back or tried to get it corrected, it would probably go to waste (as a native Texan, you DO NOT waste queso). Honestly, I did not care about this and the right thing was on the check in the end anyways.

Meal - ordered the brisket tacos, which were good and no complaints.

Service - everyone was friendly and usually had someone come around every 10 minutes or so to check on us, so that was fine - we're not picky people. Furthermore, it was extremely busy and the place has been open for just a few weeks. If this is what they're putting forward at this point, I can't imagine how great it is going to be once the kinks get worked out - will DEFINITELY be going back and recommend everyone to do so.

Lastly, hands down, the worst part of my experience (along with my girlfriend's), was who we were sat down next to (which isn't the restaurant's fault). I can't imagine they sat down much more before we did and then we proceeded to have to spend the entire evening listening to this one woman complain - at one point calling the manager over and speaking for 5 minutes straight about every single thing she hated, the dirty looks she had been given (never saw), etc., etc. The manager handled it with grace and the boyfriend/husband was noticeably ashamed by his significant other's actions.

We made it a point to speak to the manager after they left and help correct some of the misinformation she had been given by the other woman. We would definitely be coming back and that if in fact the waitress that both of us had (we had the same waitress), had been training then she should be given a break - she is learning and was very nice. Maybe I'm just not that picky, but honestly having to listen and deal w/ that was not only uncomfortable, it was honestly the worst part of our night (but Javelina can't fix that).

Anyways, highly recommend and can't wait to visit again - next time, enchiladas!

After waiting nearly a month for a reservation at Javelina, we settled for a 6:00pm reservation on a Monday night.  One word describes our experience; disappointing!  The food was good but there are plenty of tex-mex place to choose from these days.  We came specifically for the chicken fried steak which had gotten rave reviews.  When asked, the waitress informed us that the chef took it off the menu because "he wasn't happy with the recipe."  Seriously???  In an attempt to drown our cholesterol-deprived sorrows we ordered margaritas.  What we were served could only aspire to be mediocre.  I'd be surprised if any limes were harmed in the making of that drink.  It was crowded and loud and disappointing but, hey, otherwise it was fine.  Won't be heading back there anytime soon.

I realize this is New York City and there is huge hype for this restaurant right now, however coming in as a party of 4 walk-in and waiting over 3 hours then still not being seated (we ended up leaving at 10pm)  is absolutely unacceptable. Either keep actual tables for walk-ins or don't take names down at all. Not only that, we were initially told it would be an hour and 45 minutes. And yes, I tried to make a reservation, but their phone number doesn't work and the options on Open Table were less than ideal. One of the bartenders was very nice, coming around and keeping our chips, salsa, and margaritas replenished. We had the queso sampler, which was ok, but not the best dip I've ever had. Definitely not as amazing as everyone has made it out to be. It was very frustrating to leave after 3 hours without really even trying the food and would have been nice if they had offered us something to make up for the poor experience. Don't even bother if you're going to try to walk in, unless you're a party of two and get lucky with seats at the bar. Not worth it to me and I doubt I'll be back.

The first time we wanted to try out this much-hyped restaurant, they had way over-booked and dropped the ball on our reservation.  Which was really annoying, but the owner made it right and invited us back for a meal on the house.  Every member of the staff the second time around were very friendly and we went into the meal wanting to love it.

I'll start by saying that the quesos are all fantastic.  They are more than merely watery velveeta blends like so many places in the city; they are dense, cheesy, and in the case of Bob Armstrong, loaded with well-seasoned meat and fresh guac.  The rest of our meal was OK, nothing incredible, but the prices are absolutely absurd. The chile relleno was interesting; the sauce was the bomb but the main dish itself was super doughy and deep fried and the filling was still cold in parts. 

I tried the avocado-cilantro margarita and wasn't overly impressed.  It is very filling as you would expect an avocado-based drink to be, but seemed to be lacking on the alcohol.  Ditto for the Mexican martini, which is nothing like the drinks of the same name in Texas -- this one was warm, strangely salty, and just not very drinkable.  These drinks are both like $13/piece, so I expect something strong and super delicious. 

The venue is also pretty teensy, so they ended up putting us at a "shared table" right between two other couples.  This is OK, but because the music is so loud, everyone ends up shouting and it was pretty distracting and made it hard to enjoy the meal.  Maybe they could try seating fewer folks at that table and leaving a little more room in between.

In sum, I'd add Javelina to the long list of overpriced, not-quite-there Tex Mex joints around town. I would return for a beer (not a cocktail, see above) and the divine queso, but until they work the rest of the kinks out, I think I'd give it a pass.

KenScale: 8.0/10

Lately, NYC has caught wind of booming Tex-Mex dining scene. Tex-Mex is a somewhat amorphous term referring to Mexican cuisine that supposedly originated in Texas after immigrants from Mexico started folowing into the Lone Star State. Javelina is at the forefront of this Tex-Mex boom in the city after it opened about a couple of months ago in Gramercy area. Ever since its opening, it has been one of the hottest tables in the city, so I was eager to check what all the hype was about. Overall, my impression was that Javelina certainly offers authentic and delicious Mexican cuisine that would mostly make for a satisfying meal. 

Any meal at Javelina must start with queso, basically a dish of decadent molten cheese dip. I went with the "Bob Armstrong" version that had guacamole, ground beef and sour cream, and had we not ordered other dishes, we might've just finished the meal dipping chips onto this rich and delicious bowl all night. Of the tacos, the stand-out was San Antonio puffy taco, with fried corn tortillas and spicy marinated pork shoulder that was definitely one of the better tacos in the city, and brisket taco was not bad either. I found Enchiladas de Tejas (with a combination of cheese, onions, red chili gravy, chili con carne and house-pickled jalapenos) to be overwhelmingly salty, but I enjoyed steak fajitas, with very nicely cooked meat and fresh vegetables that made for every pleasant bite on the flour tortillas. There is only single dessert of sopapillas (think fried pastry) that you can dip in honey, a simple yet surprisingly good dish to end the meal.

Getting a reservation could be a challenge so book early or show up early to try your luck at the bar area. I was initially quoted 2 hours wait time for a table of four people on a Saturday night, but was lucky to get the text message that my table was ready in about an hour. The restaurant has hip scene making it perfect for fun gatherings with friends, although the noise can be a bit overwhelming. There are a variety of tequila and mezcal based cocktails, so do try some to complement your meal. If you want to explore what Tex-Mex cuisine is all about in NYC, Javelina is probably the right place to start.

Wish I could write about the food and drinks but the hostess was so bad I did not get that far. I had 6:15 reservations and got there at 6. Place was mostly empty. Apparently when you make a reservation, there are different levels of reservations. Mine was the table in the dark corner against the wall. Asked to be moved but got more excuses than help, including that one of the tables was specifically reserved for the Chef's wife. No accommodation for three of the alternative two seater tables I inquired about. Won't be back and will advise friends to stay away.

They also cancelled my reservation on OpenTable immediately as I walked out so that I could not review them in OpenTable.

Let me start by saying, our food was really great- no complaint there. As an Oklahoma transplant, I was super excited for actual queso! HOWEVER.....the restaurant was so overcrowded, no one could enjoy their meals. They had chosen to participate in a some type of restaurant tour that had groups of 30+ people bombarding the place every 20-30 minutes. The dining area is already small, so you can imagine the disaster this was for those of us forced to sit in the middle of these rotating groups. One particular couple in the very middle of the chaos asked to be moved and was denied. Maybe post this info on your website so we can choose a different night to make a reservation? 
    I also spent a great deal of my time hugging the wall next to our table/dodging elbows because a member of the management staff happen to know the couple dining 12 inches from us and chose to hover over their/our table for a good 20 minutes while catching up. Not fun. 
    Maybe they offer food to go--I'd hate to miss out on great Tex-Mex because I dread the dining experience.

While my first trip to Javelina was less than desirable, I went back for seconds and I couldn't have been more pleased. The nachos were full of cheesy deliciousness and the steak fajitas with queso were unreal. They were actually mouth watering. The service was great this go-around, very attentive and accommodating. Drinks once again were delicious and strong :)

Javelina is the closest thing to authentic Tex-Mex in NYC. I appreciate the effort given this is the only cuisine I have not been able to find here. 

Pros: They make their own chips and flour tortillas (which are great) and offer queso which are key staples to good Tex-Mex and offer local Texas cocktails such as prickly pear margaritas and Shiner. 

Cons: EXTREMELY loud and I had to repeat everything i said to the wait staff, a group of people longing for their college days were chanting fight songs at the bar (which might be ok if the restaurant was not so small), the chicken fajitas were slightly overcooked and rubbery and it is a little pricey for the quality. 

Overall, I'd be willing to give it another go.
Skip the burger which was nothing to write home about and order the queso dip and huevos rancheros.

Lunch on a Saturday was a disappointment. We were a party of 6 plus a toddler and they seated us at a four top. No high chair. The 2 they had were in use. So we had to use an adult chair and our child went over backwards. Big bruise. Not child friendly nor do they care.
Service-- seems to be a problem between wait staff and kitchen. Orders were partially correct e.g. Burger ordered with bacon came without but we were charged. Bloody Maria mix had to be be made- took 30 minutes to get the drink which wasn't that good. 
In short- the staff has things to work out to become a great place. Potential is there.

In a city of limitless options this is not one of them. 
I dont get what all the fuss is about, we tried to get a reservation for a while and could never seem to connect so when we were nearby we just popped in and got lucky, or so we thought. Queso was the only bright spot, Tacos were and overly greasy ball of meat with almost no flavor, Fajitas came with a pile of greased out peppers that my 15 yr old son, who will eat anything, any everything, would not even touch. Enchilada was Ok but also flavorless.  After a weak flavorless, almost inedible meal, they attempted to send you home with a good taste in your mouth by giving you fried cinnamon covered doughnut like things. The highlight of the meal. 
So many great places to eat in NYC at a fraction of the overinflated prices and with much less attitude, take a pass.

My boyfriend and I waited two weeks to get a reservation and it was well worth it. I started off with the strawberry frozen margarita, which was excellent. Then we had the Bob Armstrong queso (traditional) which was amazing! I loved the flavor of the meat, sour cream and other garnishes. It was such a different twist on queso. We then split the fish tacos and brisket tacos. The fish tacos were good, a little more dry, but once I put some lime on there, it tasted better. Fish was very fresh as well. The brisket was good as well and came with a sauce that really highlighted the flavors. The atmosphere was nice, loud, but our waitress was great and was right there when we needed a re-fill of chips :)

This week's fashionplate features our new black sheer Georgette Natalie blouse at the new Tex-Mex spot Javelina in Gramercy.  It's located in the old Tommy Lasagna space so it's quite narrow and gets packed quickly, best bet is to make a res.  One weekday evening my dining companion and I decided to make a last minute res.  The turquoise tufted banquettes are fun and festive.  I tried the Mexican Martini which was yummy as well as a few margaritas on the rocks which were strong and tasty as well.  We decided to order the guacamole and the queso to start, both were very yummy.  Next time I want one of the specialty quesos, they looked super good. My friend got the veggie fajitas which were solid but nothing special.  I wanted to try the avocado tacos but they were out of it the night I went so I went with brisket tacos which was tasty especially the jalapeno gravy that comes with it.  We ended the night with complimentary churros which were delish.

The crowd was mixed between young professionals, older tourists and locals.

This is really good Tex Mex food - not great or amazing but really good.  Like too many eateries these days, the service is LOUSY!  The staff just aren't friendly or pleasant - that's unfortunate because I would have given them a 2nd chance.  Sadly, this is another place seemingly running on auto-pilot with no management.  And it's always over crowded and noisy.

Drinks extremely good the rest not so much. 

Food - I can best sum it up as mexican food for white people. A little bland, and lacked a unique or genuine flavor profile. I've had true tex-mex, SoCal Mex, and in-country Mex and it's not close 

Atmosphere - very standard and based upon the price point I was expecting more

Service - I will say my waiter was good and there was a solid team spirit towards picking up the slack on tables that weren't their own. 

Quick win - bring your own hot sauce if you go.

Javelina was great! We started out with some chips and salsa, queso trio, and guac. The queso is a must here and the portions were large. Also had the fried avocado taco and mushroom tacos which were good, but not amazing. 

The service was great- we got seated half an hour after our reservation so the manager gave our table one round of drinks (strong and tasty$ on the house and sopapillas for dessert as well.

Prefacing this with the fact that I'm from Vermont, not Texas - this place is awesome!  I typically don't care much about queso, but this is the best I've ever had (compared to trips to Austin and backyard bbqs with queso made by Texan friends).  

My enchiladas were delicious, and our party of 12 was well-cared for and content.  Cocktails and atmosphere are great too.  Highly recommended.
I went here for lunch on Monday.  It wasn't busy or loud.  I ordered the pork tamales and a side of rice.  It was just the right amount of food for me.  I would go there again.
Excellent Mexican Tex-Mex restaurant in Gramercy district. Food is so flavorful,authentic and originally fresh. I recommend everything on the menu. Best salsa and queso in NYC too.

It may take quite some time to get a reservation, so your best bet is to come early to the bar.  Or very late at night.  The food is fantastic and never disappoints. My favorites: queso blanco, shredded chicken tamales and chile relleno.

I was really looking forward to checking this place out--as an avid Mexican food enthusiast, I was excited to try some TexMex to switch things up.  My friend and I came in two weeks ago hungry for good food and good drinks.  Unfortunately, we didn't get much of either.  For cocktails, I started with the Texas Mule which was watery and rather boring, while my friend went for a classic Margarita, which she described as generic (but I guess she did order just a classic marg....).  

Next up--the queso, which was why we decided to check out the restaurant in the first place.  It was definitely good, but so is Velveeta + Rotel zapped in the microwave for a few minutes.  We had the trio sampler which, while not amazing, was our favorite part of the meal.  For our entrees, we split the fish and lamb tacos which were both filled with lettuce and pico, and rather skimpy on the protein.  Most disappointing was that the tacos were served on flour tortillas.  To be honest, I'm not sure if that is a TexMex tradition or an oversight on the restaurant, but it is keeping me from ordering them again.
