Overall, I would suggest stopping by for a drink (most likely a beer) and queso if you want to switch things up--it definitely beats the weak sports bars near by.

MAS TEX-MEX!!  Best I've ever tasted outside of my home town of Austin. BOB ARMSTRONG!! Both white and yellow quesos are top notch and fairly priced for the enormous bowl and unlimited hot and salty chips coming your way. Drinks from the bar are strong and taste totally authentic.  Everyone is FRIENDLY.  My server was awesome and also from Santa Barbara, which is where I went to graduate school, instant connection!  If you are missing Stellas and Magnolias COME IN ..... FEEL AT HOME!!

This place is ridiculously loud.  My ears were ringing most of the time and I could barely hear my tablemates.  I don't plan on coming back.

What we got:
Guacamole - Creamy but SALTY
Chile Relleno - This was okay but small portion size
San Antonio Puffy Taco - Eh.  This was whatever.  Pork was okay but surprisingly didn't enjoy the deep-fried corn taco.
Enchiladas de Tejas - This was absolutely terrible.  I had one bite and didn't touch the rest.  Gave it to my dining companions that also thought it was bad but didn't want to see it go to waste.
Complimentary Fried Dough with Honey - Pretty good

Service:
The hostess was really nice and accommodating and our waitress was great.
This place is amazing! They have the best food and margaritas and the new skark tacos are amazing I recommend coming here this is one of the best restaurants in NYC! The service is great!!

Great food but wish we had a different waitress.  Don't understand when you're in the service industry, why have an attitude!?  Since the salsa was really good and I had ordered some food to go as well, she only gave me the remaining salsa that was left over from our table!  Wow, definitely a stingy waitress.  

Another complaint is that when you call to make a reservation, their phone lines are ALWAYS down!!! And when you FINALLY get through, they are always booked for over a month!

I have had almost everything on the menu and you can tell this food is made with love. The drinks are great, the homemade chips and salsa are addictive as is the queso. My favorite queso was the white with chorizo. Yes it's busy, but when you are dining at one of the hottest new restaurants in NYC, what would you expect?? Be glad you get a seat here and order the parillada  mixed grill platter. It's unbelievable. You will not have anything like this in New York. Bring an appetite and expect to have fun. Everyone there from the servers to the management are on board:) can't wait to go back. Bravo

DEAR NYT: GO FUCK YOURSELF.

I am allowed to say that b/c I am a journalist who has actually worked
at the NYT.

Yes, the New York Times and that sarcastic Wells asshole who gave this place a bad review
just because of the service (and NOT the food, which he called
"outstanding") can go fuck themselves.

If you actually care about finding good Tex-Mex in Manhattan, then go here. 
There is no way any mildly intelligent person gives the food here and THOSE SCRATCH-MADE FLOUR TORTILLAS anything less than 5 stars.

Pro tip: Since the service at this place seems to blow, go at OFF-PEAK HOURS.
Which is what I do. I drag my ass to 18th Street at like 3 p.m. on a Sunday, 
when the restaurant is empty and I have had zero service issues.

What I have had instead is HEAVENLY flour tortillas and skirt steak fajitas and queso and guac. That is all that I have ordered each time and I recommend you stick to that.  
Not as good as Texas, but very very close. Good enough for any Texan living in NYC Metro.

Javelina's food gets 5 stars, the service gets 5 stars (again, I go at off-peak hours), 
the New York Times gets zero stars.

Yeah I'm basically taking the time to give this place five stars because of the nastiness of the NYT review. 

As a Texan, the queso is to die for (thin and sharp), the enchiladas taste like home, and the margaritas are strong. I likes the food better than El Original's by far, even though I'm a huge Homesick Texan fan.

Yeah there are kinks in the service. Go on off hours. And don't be a douche.

Enjoyed a lovely meal here Friday night with a group of boys from Texas...yum yum yum!  I really enjoyed the food and drinks.  I ordered this michelada / bloody mary type of drink that was super flavorful like tangy and spicy and all that goodness wrapped into one.

For din din I had the chicken enchiladas and the boy had the lamb with the egg which was legit.  The portion was good, I think the sauce was a little salty but I actually like it that way.  Nothing to complain about.  Lamb + eggs = Sign me up.  I tasted a bite of that and was smiling inside.  

Overall, service was terrible and by service I am referring to the 4G network not the waitstaff ; )  

I will be back and bringing more friends.

Very underwhelming spot.  The best thing about this place is the free chips they give you.  The fish tacos have no flavor and my friend ordered the hamburgasa which was over cooked and said he couldn't taste the egg he ordered with it.  The fries it came with were pretty good though.  This guacamole is horrible.  I know they said they didn't make to order (which I should've known from there not to order), but it came out cold and again lacked flavor...thank god for the salty chips.  I would definitely not come back here again.

Holy cow. This new tex-mex joint really blew me away. 
I was expecting to wait, as you should too- the hype they're getting is really drawing the crowd. 
If the margaritas weren't so strong I would have tried every single one. The traditional and avocado cilantro margs are spot on. 
If you don't order queso, come back to do just that. What is better than a bowl of spicy melted cheese? the answer is nothing. there's nothing better than queso. (Mag mud is my reccommendation)
Taco fanatic here: fish tacos- yes. puffy tacos- double yes. (Heads up, they come 2/order)
Also tried the cilantro pescado, a white flaky filet with light creamy lime-y sauce that I would just drink. *Comes with their homemade flour tortillas, so you don't actually HAVE to drink it.
Saw somebody order the pariallada- basically a giant man-size flaming fajita platter. Could feed a small army. (Next time... but just for me).
Our server was lovely, highly attentive, and super smiley (especially noting how obviously busy she was [the place was packed])
*Only negative comment: Don't come here with a sore throat. You may have to shout across the table over the crazy-loud [everything] happening around you.

I am from Texas so I know good TexMex.....I had the number 2 lunch special today.
The salsa was a little sweet to be considered true TexMex but it tasted really good so there u have it. The pork tamale was kinda small, but it was very very very tasty. The avocado thing was delicious..... I mean Really Really good! The cilantro was fresh. So were the avocados. The steak thing was a tad bland today but you could tell that the ingredients were fresh. Overall, I thought this restaurant was great. The atmosphere was wonderful and the service was even better! It is worth a visit if you are really craving Mexican in the Big City!!

So I'm really glad I ate here before all the terrible reviews came out, because I may have written Javelina off as another terrible Tex-Mex impression and never given it a shot.

I'm not a native Texan (born and raised in its pan-shaped northern neighbor), but it's pretty much exactly the same in OK as in Dallas. The San Antonio-style puffy tacos haven't migrated that far north, and we don't have quite the proliferation of breakfast taco options like Austin, but Tex Mex is still a staple. Like, eat at least twice a week. For lunch. Then 2-3x more for dinner. And people wonder why that part of the country is fat: TEX MEX! I even was a server at a Tex Mex restaurant in high school.

Anyway, now that I've explained my credentials: as I was leaving Javelina, full of queso and joy, the (exceptionally kind) hostess asked me about my experience and all I could say through my big smile was "a taste of home". 

The good: The queso was great. I don't get white queso, I've honestly never seen that in a Tex Mex restaurant other than as a special. But yellow queso: that's your standard. And Javelinas, in all iterations, was fantastic. We ordered the sampler and ended up with just one gigantic Bob Armstrong (just order it). The waiter, while very busy and confused, was kind and brought us two ramekins of the other ones, gratis. The chips were fantastic. Crispy, not greasy, but with enough heft to hold up the queso. Yes, queso gets a sort of weird layer on top when it sits...but it's melted cheese yall, what do you expect? When it cools it hardens up. SCIENCE. Salsa was good and on our night quite spicy for table-salsa. I love hot salsa and would have loved a spicer option, but it seems risky to auto-serve a salsa that hot to people whose dainty palates may get set on fire rather than one more mild. But it tasted and looked fresh and delicious. I had the chile relleno, because as far as I'm concerned if you can't make a good chile relleno and good fajitas, you ain't making good Tex Mex. lucky - it was great! The breading could have been thinner, but as a carb-lover I won't complain. The crust was crispy and the pepper firm, the filling was bursting out in all its delicious glory.

The room-for-improvement: service was hectic. We went not long after their opening, so I'm sure they will settle in, but it was a little slow and funky. Servers were very nice, but extremely busy, and part of the beauty of Tex Mex is the pace and the comfort. The smiling waiter that says yall and tells you to take your time, honey, and probably knows your mother from some Bunco group that his mother also goes to. Obviously: can't replicate it. But! They can try by maybe lessening the waiters load by getting the bussers and food runners to have a little more urgency, or just simply giving them an amount of tables they can actually handle. We felt awkwardly rushed at first but then practically had to beg to pay. Weird. Boy has brisket tacos - he said good but I don't think it was the best choice. I had a taste and they were very greasy, messy, and a bit boring for all that work. I don't think he would order it again. Get the puffy tacos if you are married to tacos. Drinks were..odd. I ordered a sangria swirl (!!!!!) and having served them for many months, I can say this was a great tasting swirl but the presentation of the swirl was pretty pathetic. It was all mushed together and turned a really funky color instead of looking like a pretty swirl. And especially considering how much they charge for tiny drinks, I would hope the presentation could be better. And my boy had a strawberry marg, and it was incredibly sweet, diabetes-in-a-cup sweet. Needs some work.



Overall: love this place. Ignore the nasty reviews, make a reservation, come in with an open mind, don't be a snob, don't order brisket tacos, and enjoy. You definitely will. 

In addition, we didn't have/couldn't get a reservation for the night we wanted. But we are very flexible on time, and I spoke with the owner (seriously, called one afternoon and he was the dude answering the phone) who basically told me to come when they opened and put my name on the list and that I should get a table by 10pm at the latest. They text you when your table is about to be ready (based on how far away you tell them you're going to be). We didn't get a table until 9:45, which was fine for us, and the process was very smooth and for a busy new restaurant, pretty gosh darn solid. I'll definitely go back! Thanks yall!

Cold Queso, Overpriced, Nothing Authentic about this place.
As a Texan I was truly looking forward to the Queso as its so hard to find in NYC. We ordered the sampler with "Mag Mud" I was hoping it would revival "Kerby Lane's " in Austin but it was cold and almost congealed. The flavor was there but cold Queso, is no bueno. Nothing on the menu looked like what I normally order at the mom and pop Tex Mex places in Houston I haunt when I visit my family. 

As a gluten free pescatarian for allergy reasons, navigating the menu was hard but they did have corn tortillas. The #1 combo plate was exactly what I wanted except no chicken but they don't do substitutions. The waiter recommended fish tacos not very Tex Mex to me and I was yearning for enchiladas but there were no meat free options there. So I ended up with veggie fajitas they were filling and when I slathered cold queso on my corn tortillas then layered with black beans, veggies, "mexican" rice and it was ok but the rice on its own was not at all good.

Basically the food isn't terrible but it's not authentic and not worth the price or the hype.

Also $14 Margaritas on the rocks is steep.

I know yelp is a place to get away from the big reviews, but I thought Pete Wells was pretty spot on:
http://www.nytimes.com/2015/05/20/dining/restaurant-review-javelina-in-gramercy-park.html?ref=dining

Went last night and really enjoyed it but similar to previous trips the loud and not enjoyable music was a bit of a buzzkill. The waitress let unknown that the owner chooses the music so maybe this is something they can look into.

Great food, drinks and service. 5 stars if they can choose any other music than what plays in there now.

Ok, so I'm from Texas, grew up on a ranch near a border town in West Texas, went to school in Austin, lived in Dallas and been everywhere from El Paso to Orange, Brownsville to Dalhart, so I think I know Texas cuisine and Tex-Mex, and would give Javelina:

4-stars in NYC compared to other places
3-stars if Javelina were in Texas

I do think Javelina is the best Tex-Mex in the city, however, it's tough for me to give it a full 5-stars, only cause it didn't necessarily blow me away.  But, it was very good.

I especially liked and recommend the following, which I think were probably the best thing on the menu:
- Avocado-Cilantro Margarita (not too sweet, not too tart, perfect)
- Tamales (green tomatillo ones are very authentic)
 
Followed closely by the:
- Brisket Tacos (although not as good as the inventor of this taco, Mia's in Dallas)
- Queso (almost as good as Matt's/Kerbey/Magnolia in Austin)

Things that were not good, in my opinion:
- San Antonio Puffy Tacos (not nearly as good as Henry's Puffy Taco in San Antonio...just tasted like the fried corn tortilla was retaining too much grease - I think they don't de-grease the tortillas on paper towels like Henry's does)

- "West Texas Stacked Enchiladas" (should actually be called "New Mexican Flat Enchiladas" cause that's what they're called in West Texas where I'm from...there's only like three places you can get them - Borunda's in Marfa, Abuelo's in Odessa and a lot places in El Paso, which might as well be NM)

- Sopapillas (was nice that they were free at the end of the meal, but they really shouldn't serve sugar on them - they should be served plain and let the honey be the only sweetener)

Service is excellent and fast and price is fair.

Overall, if you want as-close-to-authentic-Tex-Mex as you can get in NYC, then Javelina is the place.

This place does not honor reservations.

We had made plans to eat dinner at Javelina over a month in advance--arrived right on time and waited around for over 20 minutes for our 8pm reservation on a Tuesday night.Hostess/Manager did not seem to care about our displeasure, so we left....

I lived in Texas for 20 years so I know my Tex-Mex.  A fellow Texan told me about Javelina so I gave it a try.

PROS:
1) Queso is great - rivals any queso I have had in Texas
2) Tamales were delicious! 
3) Salsa had a great consistency and a nice kick to it
4) Sopapillas were fabulous and free - could have eaten lots more
5) The "wave" (Pappasito's fans know what I'm talking about) was perfect.
6) Great service.  Our waiter Scottie was great.

CONS:
1) Chips were too salty - I am a salt junkie so me saying something is too salty means something
2) The chili sauce on the Enchiladas de Tejas was too bitter.  I am used to a sweeter tasting chili sauce on my cheese enchiladas.  Sour cream may have helped take out some of the bitterness.  When I go back, I probably wouldn't order this dish again.
3) The restaurant is very loud once it gets filled up. 

I will definitely try Javelina again, but it is not yet my favorite Tex-Mex in the city.  That is still Ah Chihuahua's.

On a quest to find the best Mexican / Tex-Mex in NYC:  http://nycmexfoodquest.blogspot.com.  I tried this place in April and the service was poor, but the food was pretty good.  If you're craving queso and homemade flour tortillas, definitely try this place.

Ok let me start by saying that I'm not from Texas, so I can't really judge whether or not Javelina is "authentic" Tex Mex, but I could definitely tell you that IMHO Javelina did not live up to its hype.

I made a reservation 3 weeks in advance for a colleague's birthday, after readying all the various online foodie blogs/reviews about the restaurant.  Here is a summary of of our dishes . . . 

"Bob Armstrong" Queso - served lukewarm and borning, not much better than any other melted cheese I've had.  Plus, the chips were super salty.
Brisket Tacos - It was ok, nothing to rave about.  I've had better tacos at other Mexican restaurants in the city.
Enchiladas de Tejas - A hot mess!  I felt they really skimped on the ingredients and all I got was a plate full of cheese and gravy.  I'm pretty sure I got a heartburn after eating this.
Jalepeno Margarita - you can barely taste the jalepeno, at $13 I would have expected better!
Sopapillas (complimentary dessert) - yummy!  taste like churros!

I read a lot of the Yelp reviewers mention that the service was terrible, but fortunately we had a super sweet waitress that was very patient and upbeat.  Our dishes came out super quick and the hostess was also pleasant as well. 

All in all, I think it was a good experience just to try out what "true" Tex Mex really is, but honestly, I would probably not go back, it's just not worth the calories!

First, I have no idea if it's "authentic." I was born and raised in NYS, never been to Texas, and not much desire to go, but I do like Mexican food, and was curious about the long lines outside this place. When we scored a same-day reservation, we said OK, why not? 

For this neighborhood, the prices aren't bad. The complimentary chips and salsa are top-notch. The salsa's about a medium heat, but they have homemade red sauce that goes well with everything. When our nachos came without the pickled jalapenos, our waitress brought us both fresh and pickled. Nice. 

FYI, the tacos come 2 to an order. We tried the chili (OK), and I opted for chile relleno, one of my favorite Mexican dishes. This one had ground beef in the middle (because, Texas), and was served with raisins and pecans in the sauce, an unusual, but enjoyable, seasoning. 

Had some Shiner Bock beer (OK), and they surprised us with some sopapillas for dessert. We might go back, but we're not going to wait in any line to get in, that's for sure.

so I've been scouring the city for a place to host some parties for my firm, and Javelina might just be that place. the partners are from Texas, so Tex-Mex will definitely blow them away. I recently went to another "Tex-Mex" place in the city, and was blown away. not by the quality of food, but by the lack of professionalism from the management. but let's not go there. the queso at Javelina was enough to get me to keep coming back, but the cocktails put me over the top. avocado-cilantro margarita? who would've ever thought of such a thing!? absolutely phenomenal. if I could give this place more stars, I definitely would. I can't wait to throw a shindig or three here!

I have eaten at other Mexican spots, plus have had authentic Mexican/TexMex. Javelina is ok; nothing to write Texas about. Now don't get me wrong, you will like the food, I just didn't find it AMAZING.
I came here with a friend who heard about this place and wanted to try it. She ordered a drink that had Cilantro and she liked that as well. I ordered the fish of the day, and it was good, the sauce was really good. 
It's a small place and I found myself having to move every 5 minutes because the diners around me had to go the restroom, come back from the restroom, or the server had to get to the next table, then get out from where she was. That took away from my dining experience.
It was also very loud. My friend and I needed to yell at each other and yet we were trying to understand why people were talking loud when there wasn't any music on or anything. 
If someone plans a dinner here I would maybe come again, but I wouldn't go out of my way to come here. The popularity and hype this place received is confusing to me, as it's not all what it was hyped up to be.
Great margarita perfect taste delicious salsa guacamole and queso dip...chicken tacos were outstanding ...only complaint its extremely loud

I'm a native Texan and have not had any Tex-Mex in nearly a year since moving to the NYC area. This cuisine was a staple in my upbringing. I was extremely excited when I heard about Javelina and was eager to try it.

Is it 100% authentic? Not exactly, but it's also not far off. If it were in Texas, I agree with another review that it would only get 3 stars, but for NYC, where Tex-Mex is not easy to find, it's pretty good. The drinks, while overpriced, are very good! I had the Texas Mule and Jalapeno Margarita. The Bob Armstrong white queso was superb! 

The only areas I would say could use improvement are the service and the decor. What I mean by service is that we were told we could not make a reservation since they book out quickly, and when we got there, we were told they were booked out with reservations. A part of me suspects that they say that as a marketing strategy, but saying one thing and then doing the opposite does not make good business. The decor does not have a Tex-Mex vibe either. Other than that, the food was good, and I will return.

Finally, enjoyable Tex-Mex has arrived in NYC!  It took hundreds of years for some unknown reason, but Matt Post has come to save the day!  Last night we (a San Antonian, an Austinite and a Houstonian) went to check Javelina out for ourselves, after waiting anxiously for our reservation (made a month ago) to arrive.  We were happy to discover that the food lived up to the hype.  To start the salsa was legitimate and tasty and made with real tomatoes (nothing worse than NYC salsa made from canned Italian tomatoes!).  The queso, pico de gallo, the black [refried] beans, and the guacamole were also awesome.  My favorite thing, however, were the flour tortillas.  These were the first good flour tortillas I have eaten in NYC.  They are handmade in the restaurant and the real deal!  Our fajitas and chile relleno were all crowd pleasers as well.  Service is friendly and the sopapillas to close were a nice sweet treat at the end of our meal.  It was so good we ate way too much and left there stuffed, with leftovers in hand.  We'll definitely be back.  No other place in NYC attempting to serve Tex-Mex is remotely this good.

if you are looking for the best enchiladas in NY you  will find them here.  i have lived in the city for 10 years and his place makes them be right way.  perfect amount of  cheese and the sauce will make you want to defend the Alamo.  fantastic ambience and strong Margaritas make this a must visit.  stop reading this and go already.

Best Tex-Mex North of Texas! I started with three kinds
of flavorful queso (the white cheese was my favorite!), while sipping on a perfectly tart Paloma made with blanca tequila. As a vegetarian, I usually have to settle for tortillas and cheese but at Javelina, I got to eat not just an amazing dish....it was an amazing VEGETARIAN dish. Fried avocado tacos. Let me repeat: fried avocado tacos.  Complete with the perfect amount of beans, little sprinkle of cheese and crunchy lettuce and pico...it was super filling as well as tasty. The dinner ended with sopaipillas (just a little sweet) that reminded me of the Tex-Mex I had growing up.  
The atmosphere was fun and felt like we traveled into another city by walking downstairs...and the staff were all very attentive and on point.  
I can't wait to go back!

Great. Great. Great.

1. Great Atmosphere: Cool, yet comfortable modern decor with a Tex-Mex twist. Beautiful, graphic tile throughout, refreshing pops of turquoise accents and even a gorgeous turquoise, cow-hide booth (very nice!). Lively chatter, lots of laughter and a genuinely happy environment. It's like it's (Javelina) is excited to have you there and everyone feels it and reciprocates. 

2. Great Service: Everyone was super friendly, we were seated immediately and were tended to 100% throughout our meal. The owner even spoke to us and made sure we were enjoying our meal (Spoiler: we were!!), which made it feel like southern hospitality had shown up right in the middle of New York City. 

3. GREAT FOOD: Queso Sampler. Enchiladas de Tejas. Fried Avocado Tacos (yes, you read that right). Each dish was exactly what I wanted and yet each dish surprised me in a way I didn't think was possible. If you know queso and like queso, you will love this queso. The enchiladas are among best I have found in the city thus far (and actually cheaper than the others). And the Fried Avocado Tacos...I almost don't want to ruin them with words, but I will try: extremely light, flavorful, genius.

I walk in - I have a reservation but I still have to wait for my table (already feels like Austin). I go to the bar and say we'll take 2 mexi-marts. The guy says what? I assume he doesn't hear me so I repeat myself. Really he just didn't know what a mexi-mart was so I clarified that it was a Mexican martini. Understandable mistake, though the Mexican martinis are based on Trudy's. He made it. It came in an 8 oz glass and was about halfway full. It tasted like juice and I remained sober. 

We decided to get the queso sampler. This was the best part of the meal. Their salsa was also pretty good and the chips were obviously fresh.

I decided to give another drink a try so I ordered the jalapeño margarita. I think they just cut up jalapeños and put them in a margarita. All the spice none of the smoke, and too sweet for my taste.

For dinner I ordered the puffy pork tacos. The pork is apparently slow roasted for 12 hours or something like that that makes it sound delicious. The pork I make in my crockpot is juicier and more flavorful. There was no sauce or salsa on them either. I only ate one. My friend said her enchiladas were mediocre and that the Mexican place across the street from her house makes them just as good. 

We spent half of our meal listing the tex-mex restaurants we missed in Austin.

Javelina was good. It was one of the best Mexican places I've been to. It was hidden in a quiet street but the atmosphere, service and the food was exceptional. They had a range of food options. I had a #2 combination platter pork tamale, guacamole chalupa and steak enchilada with rice, which was great to be able to try different foods. The complimentary chips were good and I definitely recommend getting the white queso. It had a bit of a kick but it was good.

Came here for brunch with a small group of friends. Overall, I'd say everything was mediocre... I started with a regular Bloody Mary... It tasted fine, but not great. Once we sat down at the table, we were brought chips and salsa quickly. The salsa was probably my favorite thing I ate at the meal. The table ordered the queso sampler. All of the quesos were like the Bloody Mary, fine but nothing special. For my entree I ordered huevos rancheros... The eggs were well cooked and the portion was large, but the ranchero sauce was lacking both in amount (there wasn't much of it) and in flavor. For the same price at a different place, I'd be able to get better food and "bottomless" brunch drinks for the same price I paid here.

Brunch was totally and SO disappointing. I've ben wanting to try Javelina for so long and to say that this was upsetting is actually upsetting. Eggs were really cold, service was very very below average, the hostess didn't want to sit us even though it was totally empty on a Saturday. My boyfriend actually had no idea what was in his eggs, it seemed like something was just splattered onto his plate. The drinks were extremely average and the atmosphere was overall dark. I had the breakfast tacos for brunch, again I think it was really rushed when it was put together and nothing special about them at all. Overall experience was upsetting and would definitely not recommend for brunch! Hopefully dinner is a little better.......

My first impression is that Javelina is totally overrated!

First I should note that my favorite cuisine is Tex Mex. I really liked the food at Javelina. Wanted to eat more but was just too full. 

We started with the queso sampler which was really good but a lot of cheese for two people. 

Next course was steak nachos. Really enjoyed these. Even though the nachos had plenty of toppings I also added some of the queso.  

Next we had the fried avocado tacos. The flour tortillas here are amazing. The avocado was so creamy!

Last we had the chile rellano. This they put a nice spin on. It had pecans and raisins and a green sauce. Plus lots of cheese. Really good!

They do not have a dessert menu which in some cases might be a big issue. But here they give you complementary sopapillas. And they were good too. 

For drinks we tried avocado and jalapeño margaritas and also mexican martini. All were good. The avocado one was filling though. 

The only negative was it is a little loud there. But I will definitely be back to try more of the menu.

The queso dip tasted great my sister and I both got sick after dinner and that's the only thing we both eat so I suspect it was to blame. The rest of the food was very mediocre and the ambience was nothing to write home about. And it was expensive. The only decent thing was the service.

Giving 5 stars because the staff was amazing.  The waiter was very attentive and the manager stopped by the table multiple times.  Their drinks were delicious, and food was good not great. Only real complaint is the noise. They need to figure out the acoustic situation soon, because you can't hear the waiter, your friend, whoever!

Really enjoyed my meal here! Was here with a group of 5, we shared the traditional queso and then I had the crispy beef tacos with a prickly pear margarita. Everything was absolutely delicious! It was a little dark inside but otherwise was very happy with this restaurant.

A friend recommended Javelina, and we were nearby, so we decided to give it a try for lunch. We arrived around 1pm on Friday, and they had plenty of open tables. They host seated us right away, and chips and salsa were brought to our table. We enjoyed the chips and salsa for sure!

I ordered fish tacos for my meal. They were super tasty, and I loved them! What I didn't love was the fifteen dollar price for two friggin' tacos. My boyfriend got the Roosevelt special, and I had some of his rice and beans. It was more reasonably priced than my tacos, but the super cheap neighborhood Mexican place around the corner is just as good. 

I think you may pay for the trendy atmosphere at Javelina, so if you're fine with that, then go ahead and try it.
Decently priced drinks, amazing queso, and a cool spin on some enchiladas. Definitely had a good experience and will be back.

Amazing Tex Mex! I felt like I was back home in Texas! The queso was excellent, the servings were more than we could eat. By the breakfast tacos were loaded with eggs that were cooked perfectly and wrapped in homemade flour tortillas.  It was obvious that the food was fresh and made to order.  The service was exceptional which was a welcome change from the lack luster service we received elsewhere while spending a week in NYC.
The atmosphere was reminiscent of the WestTexas cafes I've been to and was very nicely done!
This will be a regular stop for us every time we visit!
Worse than Taco Bell. The queso is all that is good. Bad service, extremely loud, slow cooked food and overall bad environment.

Worst margarita I ever had
Worst fish taco I ever had

Very noisy

Liked the tortilla soup
My husband thought his fajita was average

Will not be going back.

Comments from a native Texan:

1) White queso was delicious, perhaps the best item on the menu. 
2) Chips were hot, fresh and salsa had the perfect amount of spice.  
3) Noise level on a Saturday night at 9 pm in the restaurant was nearly unbearable. Waitress had to scream to take our order. 
4) Decor is cute, but simple. 
5) Service was prompt and friendly. 
6) Fish with lime cilantro sauce was excellent, although not really Tex-Mex.
7) Puffy tacos were mediocre. Small, unseasoned, and the pork wasn't very tender. 
8) Refried beans were cold and tasted canned. Rice was decent. 
9) Avocado Cilantro Frozen Margarita was unusual and surprisingly tasty although not very strong. I'd have it for dessert next time. Or breakfast! 
10) Classic margarita on rocks wasn't mixed well, but Classic frozen was excellent. 
11) Our free sopapillas never arrived. 
12) Flour tortillas were above average. 

All in all, I prefer El Original in terms of newly opened Tex Mex restaurants in New York.

My server Hailee was the best. She was knowledgeable about all the tequila - friendly and very attentive. The food was delish although the free dessert wasn't great - we had the cheese sampler and it was some of the best queso I've had. I had the chicken tacos and was apprehensive when only two tacos showed up - I was sure I would be left hungry after but it was so loaded with lettuce tomato cilantro etc that I found myself pleasantly full. I tried to continue eating my cheese sampler and Guacamole but I just couldn't. All in all a great place.

I grew up in Texas and, what I had at Javelina, was the real deal Tex-Mex.  Devoured the Bob Armstrong, which is my favorite queso and I'm so happy to see it on their menu.  Also had the cheese and red chili gravy enchiladas and they were awesome.  I had a frozen margarita, which was perfect, and a jalapeno margarita - could have been spicier.  My boyfriend had the shiner Ruby Redbird from their tap and he said it was flat.  So that's a bummer.  Also, I didn't have the sopaipillas, but from the pictures I've seen, they are not doing these right and maybe they'll see this and fix that.  It's just fried dough with honey on the side.  Please do not coat them in sugar with chocolate on the side for dipping...  Other than that, the service was great, the music was great.  Loved it and I'll be back!

After giving Javelina a second try, the margaritas and food were up to Texas standards. We had wonderful customer service, the food was delivered promptly, and the queso was not cold! I definitely suggest trying the sunrise fajitas (fajitas smothered in queso - the more queso the better). Will definitely be back again soon!

Seriously great queso and frozen margarita! I'm a native Texan desperate for a Tex-Mex fix after two months In NYC. I kept hearing about this place from fellow Texans, but reservations are hard to come by. I dropped by at 4pm and was quickly seated at bar. A few minutes later, I was in Tex-Mx heaven! I'll be back for the perfectly-spiced, smoky- flavored queso and the smooth, "I can taste the tequila,"margaritas. Great service, too!Don't miss this awesome spot!
For NYC tex-mex, definitely the best I've had... Nothing will ever compare to my beloved Houston tex-mex, but the queso is ON POINT!

The trio queso dip was definitely amazing, would go  back just for that, We got it with the beef. Also we got the shrimp quesdilla it was really good and we also got fish tacos, to me it fish tacos could have been fresher, still ate it though. The wait was a hour, so its highly recommend to make reservations. The service was on point, fast, and she was really friendly. The place is super loud from people taking, and there isn't no music. For sure its a must go for those delicious queso dips.

I had a friend who was a kleptomaniac. Spoons were his favorite, and he had an impressive collection from various restaurants. 

There's no chance he would have had a spoon from Javelina. Impossible! The waiters here are so quick to swoop down on your plates and cutlery that you would wonder how they let you have a bite of your food in the first place. 

All that is quite unfortunate because the food ain't bad at all. If you're a queso fan, Javelina has plenty of interesting variations to choose from. The drinks are creative, and the entrees are quite decent: I thought my breakfast tacos were flavorful, but could have been better with a little less cheese.

Thus, aside from the overly swift clearance of dishes, the only other shortfall of this restaurant is it's slightly spartan and dark interior, which almost made me wish I hadn't left the sunny sidewalk to walk in here in the first place.

The only things bigger than the portions at Javelina were the hype and the disappointment. We went with high expectations, and while the nachos were huge and really very good, the rest of the experience was dismal. We waited over 1/2 hour for a 2nd glass of wine, (only to be finally told that they were out of it), and the table next to us waited just as long for cocktails, got their dinner before their drinks, had the wrong entree, and walked out. (We were still waiting for our drink.) We then ordered the fish tacos, which were fine, but were mostly greens. The rice was ice cold. We thought that the black beans were a mistake...that we'd gotten cold black bean soup instead. At that point we gave up, paid and left.

Amazing service! One of my favorite neighborhood restaurants. As a native Texan, I know Tex-Mex and the Tex-Mex here is amazing. So amazing that I often order it and pick it up. Recently, they accidentally goofed on my order and hand delivered the correct order to my apartment.  Looove Javelina!!

Solid drinks. 

First time I went was opening week and there were some hiccups. Restaurant was proactive in inviting us back. Return trip was excellent. Spoke with tables around us and confirmed that it was not just us getting special treatment, everyone was being treated very well. 

Looking forward to returning soon.

Went for some drinks and dinner with a friend recently on a Tuesday night.  Environment is small and lively.  Were able to sit at bar before table was ready and had quick service.  We both had traditional margaritas and they were just as expected.

Our server Scott was fabulous - friendly, high-energy and attentive.  I tried tamales and the tortilla soup and enjoyed both.  

We already have plans to go back next month.

Great casual spot for tex-mex.
Have to say the con queso is really good.  The service is good and the staff is really nice.
The Queso....oh the queso. Go here for margs, chips and salsa and the queso sampler. Skip everything else. Old school, original tex mex. Delicious.

Been here a few times.   The place is a Tex-Mex joint and is exactly that, so don't go expecting white table cloth fine dinning.    Free chips and salsa to start!!! and The Queso is maybe the greatest thing ever.   I have only had the Fajitas which are great.  You get a bunch of stuff (refried beans, guac, pico, sour cream, rice, onions and peppers, i usually get shrimp which they skimp on a little but fresh flour tortilla is fantastic)  all in all pretty dam delicious .   The drinks are solid (I get standard margaritas, the frozen ones are too sweet for me) and the service is great.  The manager there, cute little blonde was at our table all the time making sure we were good and the server which was one of the guys was very pro and on the ball.  Really just can't think of bad thing to say.

Not worth all the hype! Staff is from
Texas and can rattle off restaurant names and famous margaritas however it was mediocre at best! Extremely disappointed with atmosphere. Guacamole was not fresh and brown chunks through out.  Queso typical for any Taco Bell. Do not go!

Excellent!!! Coming from someone who lived in Dallas for 15 years, this place hands down was as close to Texas Tex-Mex as it gets. Queso and steak fajitas were perfect. Will go back before we leave. A must try!!!

*** Extremely delicious, Very filling, Highly recommend ***

Came here on a whim. I was so impressed by the service. The food was SO delicious compared to other Mexican restaurants I've been to in NYC. The service was beyond excellent and overall, the price is decently priced for the amount that you get. You'll definitely walk away full!
The food was mediocre.  They took a very long time to serve us even though the place was not busy.  The waitress that served us was very unpleasant.  This place is overrated.

Great food, fun atmosphere, friendly service, love this place!  A big thumbs up.  We ordered a bunch of things to share and everything was delicious.  Great drinks too!  So many neat choices as well.  This a wonderful choice for friends...casual, hip, cool spot with yummy food.  Can't go wrong here!

First off, this Tex Mex restaurant delivers what it claims, and more: authentic Tex Mex in NYC. As other reviewers note, this is close to the real thing, and most true Texans (I am half Texan) won't be disappointed by the food. White queso in NYC has been missing for too long, and it's now here, Bob Armstrong style with ground beef in the middle. I tried a couple of others on repeat visits, but I will have to say that the white queso is my favorite.

On my second visit we tried the new brunch menu. It was delicious. We chose to split a queso, the steak fajitas with eggs and the biscuits with jalapeño sausage gravy. The steak was, hands down, our favorite. We all agreed that it was the best steak fajita we have ever had. It was juicy, deliciously grilled, and served with perfectly scrambled eggs. The tortillas were fresh and warm, and the fajitas were accompanied with refried beans and rice. We enjoyed the biscuits and gravy too, but my Tennessee self is probably a bit picky about those. It's hard to satisfy me in NYC on those grounds, but this restaurant certainly hits the target on Texas cuisine.

I enjoyed the tomatillo Blood Mary, which is a distinctive way of making the Bloody Mary that seemed a bit suspect to me but turned out to be a great drink. I think my favorite drink here though is the swirl margarita. I would encourage the restaurant to consider the size and price point on the margaritas, but there is no doubt as to their quality and their strength. :)

What I love most about Javelina is the people. The owner Matt, the managers and our server Scotty all were gracious, generous and dedicated to making the experience a great one for their guests. I have been twice since the opening, and my second experience revealed a great deal of improvement that make them the clear stand out in NYC for the increasingly popular Tex Mex cuisine. Hats and sombreros off to them for a great time and for good food.

After writing my last review I was informed they changed the acoustics and made the noise level better.  We tried it and they did well.  Great food, great margaritas and excellent well-run restaurant.  This will be our new neighborhood spot

Margaritas and tortilla chips are among my favorite foods, so Tex Mex is usually a win in my book.  The frozen margaritas - with an exciting option to add an extra shot of tequila for $2 extra (yes, of course, thank you, I love you).  The only downside was that it was so loud in the restaurant that it was nearly impossible to carry on a conversation without shouting.  Overall though, delicious tacos + friendly servers + trendy tacos + great margaritas = a second visit some time very soon.

The owner contacted me directly and invited me back to try it out.  I have to say the service, food, and atmosphere are leaps and bounds better than when it first opened.  Our waiter was knowledgable and attentive and the manager was eager to explain and offer different tequilas that we may like for our margaritas.  

We had the queso dip and tamales, very yummy!  I believe we got the spicy chicken, as recommended by our waiter.  We split the San Antonio Puffy Tacos and Brisket Tacos, both were amazing and very filling!  You really can't go wrong with the tacos there.  The drinks were spicy enough for me and the tequila was great.  

I am happy I tried this place out again and am looking forward to going back!

I've been here a few times since they've opened.  Really great Tex-Mex food, the best I've ever had in NYC.  They are famous for their queso and for good reason, it's completely addicting.  My favorite is the Bob Armstrong.  The fajitas are also my go to dish and the steak is amazing tasting.  Great service and great margaritas (avocado cilantro) make this probably my favorite place to eat in the area!
Food was okay but the service was really annoying, from calling to try and schedule a reservation to the actual waiters inside. They have way too inflated an opinion of themselves!

Get the queso, get the cocktails (if you get the negroni, ask them to hold the campari - it's too heavy on the bitters otherwise - but sans campari you've got yourself a winner). 

The food was fine, but the winner here is the queso.

Seated a half hour after our reservation at a table that was too small to accommodate our party, by a hostess/manager that couldn't have portrayed more apathy had she tried. The space is loud and uncomfortable and the food mediocre. Far, far better options exist in this neighborhood

Finally... This Dallas girl has found real Tex mex and queso here in NYC. My hubby and I had a delish dinner here on Sunday. He tried the puffy and brisket tacos. The brisket tacos were maybe the best tacos ever. I had the Enchiladas de Tejas which really hit the spot and reminded me of my favorite Papasitos enchiladas back home. Make sure you get the queso sampler, I liked the Bob Armstrong queso the best and he loved the white queso. I can't vouch for the cocktails because I'm 9 months pregnant, but I will be back to try the margaritas soon!

Javelina did an amazing job catering my party in West Village! They had an excellent off-site catering menu and the food was more than enough for everyone there!

A couple folks from the restaurant came to my apartment to setup the food and burners. It was a huge hit at the party and everyone loved it (especially the queso!!)

The brisket was good but the other toppings didn't go. The fish taco was a huge disappointment. one finger sized piece of fish in each taco, buried in iceberg lettuce. Good guacamole w bottomless chips.

Having lived in Dallas, I was so excited to have Bob Armstrong dip close to home. Overall great quality. It does not come with a spoon to stir all the ingredients, so you'll need to use a chip. They also did not provide any plates before our main course arrived (and not sure how you'd scoop it out without a spoon anyway). The meat is a little different -- it's darker than what I'm used to. Bob Armstrong was also a little on the spicier side. And free chips and salsa as every legit TexMex place should have.

We shared the chicken and steak fajitas mixtas. There was still plenty of meat and veggies left to make a little fajita salad, so this is definitely shareable.

1) Long Wait
2) Food poisoning
3) Shitty management


Came here with a very large group based off a recommendation, but was disappointed throughout the entire time. 

They made us wait in the narrow front area for half an hour before seating us. It was super fun dodging people and squishing together. The manager assured us our table would be ready 'soon.'  A bunch of us came from out of the city and one of the girls was pregnant, but by all means keep your guests waiting and shoved around when the reservation was made and confirmed well ahead of time. The restaurant is incredibly loud, we couldn't even hear the person next to us.

Nobody was impressed by the food or the watered down drinks. The queso sampler thing was glorified Taco bell cheese sauce, and my dish in particular gave me food poisoning well into the next day. I contacted the manager via email recapping the entire night and got no response. Definitely not coming back.

We had a reservation and were seated right away.  Took a minute or two to get a menu, but other than that the service was great.

The food.  Amazing.  Unlimited chip is all I ask for.  We ordered guacamole and the white cheese dip to share both were great and the chicken enchiladas (with green sauce) was the best.

Deducting one star for the loudness factor, but the restaurant was packed.

As a Texas native, I'm always weary when I come across a spot claiming to have real Tex Mex in a city that probably knows little about it. However Javelina was absolutely delicious. I ordered the Habanero and White Peach Margarita, on the rocks, which was spicy and sweet. The bartender, Walter, made it just right. If you can't handle a little heat then try the Prickly Pear which is also very good. I started with the Traditional Queso, and it was tasty, again with a good kick to it. The cheese is rich and creamy and the homemade chips scoop up the thick queso perfectly. For my main I ordered the Chicken Fajitas which came out on a sizzling platter with all the sides and fresh homemade tortillas, another good sign that this place is following Tex Mex traditions. All in all it was a solid meal. There's no fuss to this food, it is abundant and delicious. So come with an empty stomach!

The free chips & salsa and the free bootleg doughnuts for dessert are a nice touch. The ambience wasn't bad either. I got the chicken fried steak, and my friends got the relleno, fajitas, and tacos. Everything was fine, but nothing was great. Its worth checking out if you're in the area, and the price point and portions are pretty good.

Bob Armstrong queso.  It fills one of the few gaps in the otherwise crowded NY restaurant market (as least to an occasionally homesick Texan).  Nice service, good drinks, and crowded in a way that reassures you that it's as delicious as the margaritas make you think.
Been here before and the food is great and so is the service. Yummy margaritas!!! Definitely worth the visit for the queso dips.

I just don't get this place.  Food is totally mediocre.  Queso dip fine,  but nothing special.  Most other fish tacos better,  and the server actually told us the guacamole is nothing special. Are two tacos really a dinner? The free giveaway dessert was also poor,  almost stale.  If it's not going to blow you away,  why bother serving? 
Good luck!
Eh the food was okay.  From NC so we CRAVE queso dip- and being that this is one of the only places in the city that makes it.  It was okay- kindof pricey, but the service was great!

Ordered fajitas delivery the other day they forgot the tortillas. Honest mistake. I call, and they immediately send someone back out and even offer me something comped from their menu (which I appreciated but declined). The owner himself actually brought the tortillas to my place, and then called a half hour later and said they'd comp the meal. Unbelievable service. The staff is unquestionably the friendliest I've ever experienced in New York.

We stopped in to sit down and watch a football game in the late afternoon. The ambiance was great, and the GM was very nice. We only had the white queso and a couple drinks, but will be back for dinner soon. The queso is outstanding, and rivals anything I had in Texas and Oklahoma growing up. They also have a good selection of Shiner.

Tex mex is hard to find in NYC so this was an exciting night. We had dinner for a girlfriends birthday on a Thursday night. Note: they will not seat you until your whole party is present. We had a reservation and there wasn't a table right at the reservation time. Expect to be seated 10 min or so after. If it's cold out there isn't a large space to wait inside, but would suggest trying to squeeze in at the bar to pass the time.

One of the most sought after dishes is the queso. Go with the Bob Armstrong version of queso with ground beef, pico, and sour cream. You won't be disappointed. For my entree I ordered the chicken fajitas and they were delicious. It's a big portion with rice and beans (refried or black) that comes with it. Everything was a little over salted though. Ordered their version of a Moscow mule to go along with it, but I heard the margarita would've been a better choice. 

The service was mediocre. Something that would've made my rating a 4 star rating if it were just a little better. 

Overall I would like to go back and try some other stuff on the menu. I enjoyed the atmosphere and is a good dinner spot in the Flatiron area.

We had a reservation for 7:30PM and weren't sat until 8:20PM on a week night.  The hostess half heartedly apologized about our wait, said the manager was going to come over to apologize, but he never did.  The waitress was sweet when we sat down and offered us a round of free drinks for our patience, but we felt like it wasn't enough for the wait (and one of us wasn't drinking) and for basically being ignored for 50 minutes.  I realize they often can't control when people stay longer than planned, but they should have asked if we wanted a drink 15 minutes into the wait or comped an appetizer or something.    The food was decent, but nothing special.  The ambiance was also okay, but nothing spectacular.

5 stars simply because the tortillas are freshly made on site and are amazing.  Had steak fajitas for my dinner - excellent.  Queso dip sampler was devoured.  Guacamole great.  Unlimited tortilla chips.  
Just as a tip, people at my table with big appetites didn't find the tacos to be enough food.  The fajitas were more than enough, so luckily we all just shared and everyone was happy.  
No dessert menu, but you do get the "churros" (ie donuts covered in cinnamon and sugar) which were great.

I popped in here with a girlfriend after ABC kitchen was too busy. I am glad! The food was delicious, the staff was excellent! We especially loved our bartender Walter. Jolly, friendly and full of suggestions. Will definitely come back!

I live in the area and enjoy many local restaurants - this is not one of them. The very first time I came to the restaurant to pick up an order of chicken tacos , rice and beans and chile relleno and it took ONE HOUR. The order was also wrong - tacos were not correct. The food was so so, but doesn't compare to many other options in the area , especially at this price point. 

Clearly others enjoy this place, but I'm more then happy to go elsewhere

Great new Mexican restaurant. Fun and trendy vibe. Walked in with 2 friends without a reservation. Unfortunately, the whole place was booked but was able to sit at the bar. We originally just went for drinks, but decided to eat dinner as well after being tempted by the menu. The drinks were great - highly recommend the prickly pear margarita. Also great service. The waiter was very helpful in recommending drinks to our liking. Will definitely be back and plan to make a reservation next time. Bathroom décor was also a cute touch - there is a picture of Matthew McConaughey and Beyoncé to denote mens vs. womens.

Can't say enough great things about this place. As long as you're in the mood for tex mex, you're going to love this place. Food, atmosphere, and service was wonderful. To start we got the queso sampler and guacamole which were excellent. No going wrong with the mains. All are great!

This restaurant definitely deserves 4 stars, and not only because it is almost named after me ;)

My three girlfriends and I went to dinner at Javelina last night, and were beyond impressed by their customer service. A round of margaritas on the house to make up for the seating delay, energetic/friendly bartenders that actually made great mean suggestions. The manager stopped by a few times to see how our dinner was going. 

It was simply a great dinner, not easy to find such friendly staff in NY.

Jim Bob's Breakfast Tacos.. excellent.

Bob Armstrong - queso dip.. excellent.

Service.. excellent.

What else could you ask from a restaurant?  Went on a Saturday afternoon and found that they had a special brunch menu.  I love breakfast food, but I was hoping to have some authentic Mexican or TexMex.  As it turned out, the breakfast tacos were really good and filling.  The queso dip that I ordered was also excellent, although I could slowly feel my arteries becoming clogged and my butt cheeks sinking into the seat from the weight.

The service was also excellent, although the place wasn't full.  The servers really made sure that you were taken care of by providing their recommendations and refilling my water.

Overall, I'm very pleased and this will be my go-to Mexican place when I'm in the area.
Great food great service. Very high energy place. Will come every time we are in NYC!! Wonderful margaritas.

I was in Houston earlier this year but apparently failed to have proper Tex Mex there.  In an effort to right that wrong I came to Javelina but probably should have just waited for my next trip to Texas.

In any case, the meal was decent but nothing was spectacular.  I will admit the Queso was VERY good, but it's literally just melted cheese so I don't know how that could be not good?  Who doesn't like melted cheese?  

By the time mains rolled around I had effectively gorged myself on half a cup of cheese so wasn't too hungry but probably lucky for me.  We shared a bunch of items at the table - fish tacos, pork tacos, DIY fajitas, enchiladas and nothing really stood out...of those items my favorite is probably the fajitas, which come with warm tortillas and a sizzling platter of veggies and meat (we chose half and half shrimp and beef).  Ironically our first container of tortillas arrived EMPTY (what a tease) but this was quickly rectified by our waitress who was super sweet and attentive.

Drinks were pretty strong and even though we skipped dessert, they brought out some fried donuts on the house.  Maybe to make up for the missing fajitas?  In any case, a worthy trade since the fried donuts were delicious.

This place is pretty good for groups though, and the cuisine is neutral enough that everyone can find something to eat here.

On my third visit, I left before I was seated. Since it was clear my reservation was not going to be honored.

First visit, server got the order wrong. Food was good if not overwhelmingly so. 
Second visit, waited 20 minutes for a reservation but the service and food were much better, so I figured the first time was an anomaly. Friends I had brought from Texas enjoyed it.

Third visit, it's clear that an older couple is not welcome. We had planned a special evening and arrived 5 minutes before our reservation, only to watch  others who had later reservations seated before us. We watched other parties that were similarly unable to be seated offered and served comp drinks with the manager making a great deal of fuss over them. We were ignored and certainly not offered comp drinks. 35 minutes after the reservation time when it was clear that they were not going to seat us at any time in the near future, we left. The hostess was increasingly hostile when we asked about the disparity in service and accommodation. Of course, you have to stand there right in front of her in a narrow chute. Beware of the cactus that lean into the waiting area and may snag your coat. We had made the reservation through Open Table, but the hostess cancelled it when we complained of the wait. (You get an alert on your phone right away.) 
 
Silly us, thinking that discriminatory door policies went out in the 80s. They're alive and well. So, if you don't fit the white 20-something demographic Javenlina seems to want (at least for the minute-and-a-half while they're hot and popular), you may be treated with a level of dismissive hostility that achieves their objective of getting you to leave, which we ultimately did.

So much for Texas hospitality. Of course, given some of the current political climate in Texas, discrimination and hostility to the "other" is an authentic Texas experience. However, that is not one I need to have or expose my guests to again.

Meh. Completely overpriced for what it has to offer. "Bob Armstrong" queso tastes like Velveeta dip with a bit of flavor (but not much more). It arrives to your table lukewarm. Brisket tacos have no flavor whatsoever (brisket tastes like boiled pork). Not sure where "26" rating for food from Zagat is coming from.

We arrived 8pm on a Monday night and sat at the bar, the bartender was friendly but definitely try to oversell on the menu. We he died to go with his "best picks", the Queso and the combo fajita. 20 minutes later the food arrived, the Queso was extremely salty and flavorless, the taste was one dimension and very heavy on the salt, was this intentional? We did not like it. Fajita has a good presentation, but again it was tasteless. We have read great review about this place but we were extremely disappointed, this is just another overhyped Downtown food joint that is overpriced, underwhelmed and soon to be gone Restaurant. Take your money elsewhere.

We came for a fam dinner because my sister loves the queso. It was clearly company Xmas party season and the staff was overwhelmed. The waitress was doing the best she could, brought us extra chips, warned me to not get certain drinks but they forgot about my drink order and all our apps and brought the entrees out. She had already comped my drink at this point but our mom was very unhappy about the forgotten queso - it's definitely not a mom restaurant!- but the manager immediately came over and was so nice about it and comped the queso which did eventually come out, comped another round of drinks - just went out of his way to apologize for the mistakes. 
Our mom couldn't be appeased but we probably shouldn't have brought her to this kind of boozy after work spot anyway. As for us, we were taken aback by the lengths they went to on a busy night to make things right, so props where props are due!

This place is one of my favorites in the city. It's real authentic texmex that one usually can only find in Texas. The quesos are perfection and the drinks are delicious with nice heavy pours. Every meal I've had is on par. It took me a year to find a texmex oasis in NYC, but now that I've found it I'm in heaven!

I was looking forward to trying this place, but overall I was unimpressed.  The drinks were excellent, the service was terrific, the food - just OK. Everything just seemed average and underwhelming. It's too bad, because there isn't a whole lot of this type of cuisine in the area and I would have liked to have a go-to spot.
Margaritas and taquitos during happy hour were on the money. Bartenders were extremely hospitable and weren't too pushy to get us out of our seats once the place started filling up.
Great food and great drinks! Love the dip options, have had dinner and lunch here, all excellent.  Tacos are great and salads are great. Get the Bob Armstrong!
queso is good. drinks weren't bad either. the rest will probably taste better after a few margaritas.

It's hard to find decent Tex-Mex in NYC. My husband and I were really excited when Javelina opened up. Their cheese dips are delicious. I will say the portions are gigantic so if you order a cheese dip for the table, a smaller appetizer choice or even their soups is more than enough food. Each time we go, we end up over ordering! Their margaritas are tasty frozen or on the rocks.

Being one of the hottest reservations in NYC at the moment, I was thrilled to be able to come to the super-hyped Tex Mex joint. This sort of cuisine is very hard to come by in the city, which justifies the hype. We called on a Friday and got a reservation at 6 for the same day, guess it's easier if you're just 2 people. 

Anyway, we started with the infamous queso. There are many different choices, but we went with the white option that had jalapeños. Let me tell you, it was addictive. Its creamy, well seasoned, and has just the right amount of heat. It's a perfect marriage with the salty and crunchy tortilla chips. We seriously couldn't stop eating it! For entrees, we went with the skirt steak fajitas and their famous "puffy tacos". The steak was cooked perfectly, and had a great marinade on it. The flour tortillas were also excellent. The puffy tacos were very interesting. The sides of the shells were puffed up and crispy, but somehow the whole thing didn't fall apart once you bit into it, which amazed me. The meat inside was also tender and delicious. The guacamole is excellent, and is a perfect condiment (along with that epic queso) for any of the dishes. 

When you get the check, they also bring you a complementary plate of sopapillas, which are pieces of fried dough sprinkled with cinnamon sugar, churro style. 

Overall, I have to say that it is definitely worth the hype. The food is delicious, really the only high quality Mexican/Tex Mex I've had in the city. As long as you can get a table, I highly recommend.

Don't buy into the incredibly snarky review in the Times, this place it delicious and seems to have come leaps and bounds from when the review came out. Made a reservation for 8 and were sat just after. The margaritas were just right as was the queso. Listen when I say this: get the puffy tacos. As a member of Taco Enthusiasts United, these were incredible. I wanted to try my boyfriends meal but when I looked up he'd already devoured the whole thing. Make yourself a reservation and enjoy.

Holy hot sauce Batman!  A Tex-Mex place in New York...  With Rita's, Mexican beers and chips and salsa that didn't taste like cardboard and ketchup...  This place has all the hallmarks of a great Tex-Mex Joint in the Lone Star State.  Margaritas were great...  Ask them to add jalapenos for a kick.  Salsa was old school, but the queso was the surprise of the night.  The sampler brings you 3 takes on the cheese dish.  All were excellent.  Tacos were very good, maybe needed a little more spice, but definitely solid.  The prodominantlyTexan staff was as friendly as the state.  It's not the best Tex-Mex in the world, but definitely an upgrade in Manhattan.

Tried this place bc it's in my hood. It started off good and then ended up being a horrible experience.  The one pro: Place was packed which created a good vibe. Cons: Food was ok. After getting our food, all went to shit - during our meal, the bus boy took away ALL our food. After telling them they brought back exactly what they took. Then we left thinking this was an unlikely place we would revisit. THEN to top it all off I got food poisoning and have been sick all day!!! Not worth it for sure now!!

having grown up in Austin I was excited to try Tex-Mex in NYC and Javelina did not disappoint. service was easily a 5 - so friendly and attentive, food was a 4 for NYC and a 3 by Texas standards. 

chips and salsa were tasty, and that can set the tone for tex-mex really, bad chips and salsa and you might as well resign yourself to a night of disappointing tex-mex to follow. We ordered the white queso and it was really really good, comparable (but not quite as delicious) to Matt's El Rancho. I ordered the Enchiladas de Tejas and it was good. my only complaint was that the enchiladas were quite stuffed, and sort of resembled burritos almost, rather than the typical flatter enchiladas, and because of that the cheese in the middle was kind of unmelted and slightly lukewarm. but...the right flavors were pretty much there. not sure how I feel about jalapeños as a topping for them though. my mom ordered the mushroom and corn quesadilla and she loved them. I was overall very happy and will definitely be coming back to get my queso fix!

I really loved this place. My sister brought me here for lunch because they have chips and queso which, while a staple in the south, is not so easy to find in NYC. The chips were crispy and the white queso dip was the right amount of spicy. We had the pork enchiladas and we really enjoyed them. Very good flavor. It was definitely enough food for both between the queso and the enchiladas. The service was outstanding and the restaurant and bathrooms were extremely clean. I want to come back for more delicious food and to have drinks!

This place deserves four stars for the queso alone. I haven't found many reasonably priced but good Tex mex / Mexican in the city, but this place was solid. I'll be back. The Migas was an interesting dish that I probably wouldn't get next time, but it was tasty and the whole experience convinced me I need to come back
If you're a native texan or just a fan of tex mex you will be very happy w Javelina as they've finally filled a longstanding void in NYC dining. Viva Tex Mex in NYC!

Came here for lunch once as this place is around the corner from my office. The decor is nice and place is clean. Three (3) because the food here is overpriced and there is nothing special to it. So many mexican reataurants around Union Square, why choose this one. My co-worker actually got food-sick eating at this place. They should also have a lunch special. I have mix feeling about this place.
Hallelujah, we found good queso in New York City!! Hallelujah!! Staff is super friendly - great environment - good Tex-Mex... and did I mention QUESO and margaritas?!

It's a mantra that New York City has every type of food, but it lacks great Tex-Mex. Not Mexican food--Tex-Mex. Javelina, has real queso dip, nachos, and Shiner on draft like you would get in Dallas. Of course it's not just the sides that make it authentic. The service was friendly and attentive. My bartender was a cheerful blond from Austin.

Enchiladas, burritos, and margaritas are all up to Texas standards. Just be warned that the place is small and pretty tight.

After all the hype and impossibly long waits after they opened, I finally got to check this place out.  And it absolutely lives up to the hype.  Everything was on point.  Quesos were all great, chips and salsa were solid, tacos and enchiladas were done right.  They appear to have ironed out any prior kinks and have things running strong.  Service was very good - prompt and attentive.  We went on a Wednesday night so maybe that's how to play it and avoid the weekend rush.  NYC isn't exactly a tex-mex mecca but this is the best in town by far.

First let me say that I lived in Texas for 4 years so I know good Tex-Mex when I taste it. This place is great! The key to good Tex-Mex is to have the right amount of "heat" in every dish otherwise it's just bland. The queso is fantastic and has the appropriate amount of jalapenos, the flour tortillas are made fresh which is extremely hard to find in NYC, and San Antonio puffy taco's are to die for! Plus this place has very friendly waitstaff and is easy on the wallet!! I don't know why I waited so long to come here but I'll definitely be back soon.

My wife and I went to Javelina last Thursday during their busiest time. The bartender noticed we had been waiting an hour and bought us a round of drinks. After we sat down the manager came to our table and profusely apologized for the wait and offered us appetizers gratis. This is the first time in years that I have experienced this kind of customer service in NYC. The food was awesome as well.
Good cocktails and Mexican food. More of a lunch atmosphere, not dinner. Great service. Would go again.

This place tastes like home. The chili relleno is perfectly fried, and the queso is the perfect texture. My roommate swears by the enchilada sauce, and I liked the avocado tacos, but they aren't a Tex-Mex Classic in my mind. The chips are thin and crisp and the salsa that comes out with them when you sit down is delicious. I've had great service here, and I'll keep coming back! I read the NYT review, and I think they fundamentally misunderstand Tex-Mex as a dining genre. If you want subtlety and delicate balances pick one of the city's posh eateries. If you want cheesy goodness with a side of rice and refried beans when you are missing those starry Texas nights, eat here. My two complaints--while I appreciate that they know what a sopaipilla is, I think they do it wrong. It should be hollow inside, not dense. And when I told my dad how much I paid for the chili relleno, he almost made me move back home. But what do I know? I'm just a small town Texas girl.

After desperately searching for a good Mexican restaurant in New York City I was really happy when this place opened up. Everybody was talking about it and we decided to give it a chance. It was so hard to get a reservation here in the beginning when it first opened. And it's still kind of hard so definitely call in advance if you're going on a busy night.

I think the main thing I have to say here is that the queso here is life changing --it is so freaking good! We got the queso sampler which includes the choice of three different quesos. Each and every single one of them was so good. There is one that was my favorite I think it's called the mad mug. It includes guacamole pico de gallo and black beans. It is amazing.

Normally I would give it a 4-star rating because the rest of the food on the menu is just OK and they don't heat up the cheese when it gets cold BUT the cheese is so amazing and my mouth is watering even thinking about it that I'm forced to give a 5-star rating. 

We also got the enchiladas which were decent nothing to write home about. The avocado tacos I would recommend though it was pretty delicious. I often visit this restaurant and usually just get the queso sampler and the tacos and I am a happy girl.
Now that things have slowed down here, this is far and away the best tex-mex option in the city

Recommended to me as the most authentic Tex-Mex you'll get in NY. 

The queso sampler is the highlight of their menu. Everything else tasted like pretty basic Tex-Mex. 

If you like to top off meals with desserts like me, you'll need to go somewhere else. No dessert menu here but really nice staff.

Disappointing. Annoyingly would not seat us when majority of party was there. Queso turned to rubber 5 min after arrival - inedible. Rest of meal generally unremarkable. Obnoxious waitress. Go to Mole instead.

Stumbled past this place after work and decided to stop in. The interior is adorable, especially the lighting! We were told we had an hour to sit at the table since after that time all of them were taken by reservations, which was fine. We sat down just to find out that happy hour specials were only at the bar, so we moved to the bar.

We each got a frozen margarita ($6), and some guac/salsa to split. The chips and guac were $14 for happy hour, which is high in my opinion...

Service was prompt, but the food was mediocre. Nothing special.
Lived in Texas for ten years and think this is a very solid option for queso, which is nearly impossible to find in this city. Margs and food are also good, but a little pricey.

Their cheese dip and nachos are good - but $9-15 for these things - even in NYC - is a bit much. They aren't that good. 

The avocado tacos we tried were pretty boring and without much taste. 

Won't be going back.
Real Tex-Mex, yum. Gets super loud though, which is unfortunate. The queso is amazing. The mushroom quesadilla is delicious and creamy.

Queso is the ultimate!!! 
Professional hospitality always provided by Samantha T. - She is a beacon of light!!!

Avocado margarita was great !
Enchiladas (brisket?) was yummy~
Tamales (chicken) was okay.
Waitress was energetic and attentive.
Scored their chicken taco, which came with a good # of chips and some nice spice to their guac & queso (MealPass 4/4/16). This tex-mex place was dead at lunch, and FYI NYT gave them no stars.

Best Tex-Mex in Manhattan, hands down. 

Try:
Queso (ask for flour tortillas to accompany)
Fajitas (says they feed two, but can easily feed 4-6 marketing girls)
Margaritas - delicious and lethal
Enchiliadas

basically you cant go wrong with anything here. give it a go!

Best Mexican food in the city- like, wow! Also loved the frozen margs. And you absolutely must order the queso sampler- it's life changing. Always busy but not impossible to get a table- I've gotten seated twice without reservations at peak times, once at a table and once at the bar.

Good place for Tex-mex! Came here for brunch on a Saturday. They give you free chips and salsa right off the bat which was pretty good. I got the breakfast taco with eggs and chorizo which was cheesy and filling. A little too greasy but good otherwise. When they got busier, service was a little slow in terms of checking on is for the check but we ordered and got our food in a timely manner.

Good if you are looking for a restaurant to go to with a young crowd before you go out. The food is like every other descent Mexican spot in NYC. I think the best thing was the queso dish. It had a little kick to it. The drinks were good as well. It was extremely busy on a Friday night around 830 with a young crowd, mixed with groups and people on dates. It's very loud inside so not sure how a date would be.

This was my first time at Javelina and it was really good. We made a reservation but had to wait about 25 min to get seated. Once we sat down, the staff promptly placed down complimentary chips and salsa. We started off our meal with some white queso with carnitas and the taquitos appetizer. The queso was extremely heavy but totally worth it. Taquitos were pretty good as well. I was almost full by the time our mains came out between all the chips and our appetizers. My group ordered the brisket tacos and the carne asada and I had the steak/chicken fajitas. Everyone seemed to really enjoy their meal. My fajitas had a tiny bit too much pepper on them, but between the homemade tortilla, amazing pico de gallo, and some perfectly cooked meat, I was pretty content. Definitely recommend this place!

This review was not a rating of the food but the service.

My girlfriend was craving nachos so we decided to try the nachos at Javelina, which received great reviews from the Gothamist & other papers. We got at the restaurant a little before 6. The hostess did not acknowledge us when we first entered the restaurant. After what seemed to be a 5 minute wait, the hostess made eye contact with us & told us to come back at 7pm, without any explanation or anything. (mind you there were still empty tables there). 

I know this place might have customers call in for reservations however the way & the matter in which my girlfriend and I were treated was not appreciated. We did not give the hostess any attitude nor were we rude & nosiy when we arrived into the restaurant. Although this place will still receive customers, we will not be one of them.

First time at Javelina the other day with another couple.  One of them was running late for our reservation so we bellied up to the bar for a few margaritas.  My girlfriend was excited about the prickly pear which was really good as was the spicy.  We were especially fond of the bartender who was alot of fun..the service overall was very good all night.  When we sat down we went for the queso which was awesome.  The rest of the food was average but good....enchiladas, steak & fajitas.  The room busy but comfortable.  We'll go back again for sure.
