Great staff, dip was amazing, drinks and tacos were good but the portions overall were not worth the price. Needless to say I can't come here when I'm hungry but if I need a snack while I'm in the union square area I know where to go.

Came here with a reservation for 4 on a Monday night. Let's start with the good. Frozen classic margaritas: phenomenal. Queso sampler: excellent. Bartender (Oscar): lovely. Host (didn't catch his name unfortunately): funny and did plenty to try and make the evening right after we had one of the worst servers I've ever experienced. Great segue into the bad. 

Everyone gets a bad day, but this woman seemed to be really unamused with our party.  After grabbing us 2 rounds of their free chips and salsa she seemed to think we were taking too long and came to our table several times asking if we were ready to order with exasperation. Everyone at the table noticed it and weren't sure what we had done, but after watching her interact with other tables, her attitude seemed present at different levels for all of her tables. 

Bad service kills me, but bad service on a $21 shrimp entree that arrives with 5 shrimp?  I ordered a dish I believe was called the Sam Houston. Gets to the table with only 5 shrimp and the rice and beans it comes with were forgotten (though they brought it to me after I reminded them).

Also be sure to check your bill. It was minor but ours was incorrect. There were certainly redeeming elements to Javelina but unfortunately, not much makes up for bad service (and inflated pricing).

The restaurant is small but atmosphere was great. Wasn't a fan of the avocado Margarita or Swirl but food was good. Bob Armstrong white queso was delicious! Just like in Texas. Beef fajitas were really good, chicken fajitas were ok. Overall great experience if you want TEX MEX in NYC!

Came here a few weeks ago and got a solid Tex-Mex meal. We started with the queso which was loaded with beans, cheese and a bit of guac. It was delicious, gotta love a good queso. We also started with the chips, salsa and guac which was also a hit. As an entree, I got the fish tacos which were very yummy. Not the absolute best tacos I've ever had, but a very solid meal. The fish was well seasoned and the taco shells were soft with lots of corn flavor. Definitely would love to come back here, I'd like to try some of the drinks as well.

Food is pretty standard Mexican - a little overpriced in my opinion for what it was ($26 for shrimp fajitas). The margherita was fine, nothing particularly memorable in either a good or bad way here. Would probably come again if I was hungry in the area and craving Mexican. 

Honestly the worst part about the experience was the service. Our waitress was very nice but we had to flag her down every time we wanted something - it took us probably an hour to even order our dinner. It was nice that they did not rush us out at the end, but when we literally opened the bill with the credit cards we still had to flag her down to charge them (and at this point there were only a few other people in the restaurant). We still left a good tip because she was nice about it and kept apologizing, but note to the restaurant - the staff needs to be more proactive about checking up on the tables!

The queso!!!! It is, by far, the best queso in New York City and on par with queso from Texas. They have different variations of it and they all taste amazing. Do yourself a favor and get the sampler to try them out. 

The brisket tacos were really good, but the brisket could have been more tender. Relatively speaking though, it is the best brisket tacos I've had in New York in terms of taste and texture. 

My friend got the fajitas and they were spot on! The meat was tender and cooked perfectly.  

Will definitely go back to get brunch and some Mexican margs.

Excellent attempt at TexMex. Most of the entrees are authentic, although too pricey by Texas standards  (what can you do, it's Manhattan). I recommend this place both for homesick Texans and those looking to try TexMex without traveling to the Lone Star State.

Really unfortunate that I'm writing such a review, as my boyfriend and I came here after disregarding a terrible Times review last year and really enjoyed ourselves. Working in the industry, we know how a bad review can really suck, so we made Javelina our go-to Tex-Mex spot. Tonight, a Tuesday, happily we decided to return at 9:01PM, only to be told by the seemingly clueless maitre'd that they wouldn't have room to seat the two of us as their kitchen was closing soon. Eyebrows raised, we commented online they claim to close at 10. The girl responded that "yeah, but their hours vary from night to night and that a manager had informed her 9:15 would be tonight's closing time for the kitchen."

??? Unless there was an incident in BOH she wasn't informed of, or that she was more clueless than originally perceived, that's utter bull shit. Not cool javelina - especially from two optimistic, in-your-corner industry professionals.

Just walked in to Javelina at 9:01 pm on a Tuesday evening and was told that there was no possibility of sitting because the kitchen was closing at 9:15. When we asked why considering that the restaurant was full and the kitchen was scheduled to be open until 10:00 on Tuesdays the host explained that "the kitchen closing time varies all the time. The manager just decides and then we stop seating". I have been a restaurant manager for ten years in NYC and I've rarely, if ever, encountered this practice to say nothing of such a terrible approach to hospitality by both FOH staff and management. It's sad too because we really loved coming to Javelina and frequently ordered delivery as well. You have lost two loyal customers and succumbed to the worst kind of amateurism. I've opened restaurants and I've closed them... guess which one this place now feels like??

My friend and I only sat at the bar - so this review is really for the bar experience. Our female bartender (I'm forgetting her name!!) was so fun and attentive while we enjoyed frozen margaritas, queso, and fish tacos. I expressed my anguish over having a laughably low tolerance of alcohol (I was tipsy after 1 of those strong margs!!), and she told me she'd make me a special gin drink the next time I was there. I'm looking forward to going back for that! Overall had a great time, mostly thanks to that cool bartender.

Good Mexican restaurant, with plenty of options to choose from and complimentary chips (at least for lunch). The enchiladas were delicious. The food was a bit long to come but it might be because we arrived during rush time.

Finally! I decent Tex-Mex place that's actually TRUE Tex-Mex! I looked everywhere for a place like this when I lived here over a year ago (Texan born and raised) and couldn't find anything close to what true Tex-Mex actually is. This place opened right when I moved so I wasn't able to try it until I moved back recently. 

The queso is a requirement to order. It has all the required elements: thick gooey cheese, tomatoes/peppers, guac, and chorizo if you're up for it. Best queso I've had outside of Texas.

My mom ordered the cheese enchiladas, which were on par and I had the brisket tacos. The tacos were closer to being California style (smaller and over stuffed) but the tortillas and brisket were cooked perfectly. 

We ended our meal with complimentary sopapillas, which were delicious and small, so it wasn't overwhelming. 

We had the traditional margarita, which was good because it didn't have the sweet and sour mix, it was a true marg. 

The less positive reviews of this place seemed to mostly cite bad service. We actually had really good service! Got our food fast and our waiter was super friendly.

Mandy is an amazing bartender!! Taught us all about tequila & was super cool!! Their queso was incredible!! Everyone is super nice!! Their food is amazing!! I would def recommend this place to my friends!

AWESOME!  We ate at the bar and at 45 were probably the oldest people there. Talk about beautiful people!  Everyone had a romper on. But a it the food, we had the chips with guacamole medium, the steak quesadilla and the brisket nachos. Innovative and the nachos had a great taste as they picked up the brisket flavor. Brilliant. The steak quesadilla also had high quality meat. Again the taste of the meat was picked up by the tomatillo salsa and the just right amount of sour cream.  All came with guacamole. The portions were not as big as at brother jimmy's (down the block) but they were of higher quality we were full. They do not need to be huge. For drinks we had the margaritas (sangria and strawberry) and both were great, true to flavor. Very clever to do a sangria margarita. Fruity but not too sweet with strong alcohol. Then when I inquired about the avocado margarita the waitress let me try it for free. Not a familiar taste but very good.

I've been to Javelina three times since it opened and it keeps getting better! Most recently I went on Friday with my wife. For background I go to Texas quite often for work and always eat some of the best Tex Mex the state has to offer (my current favorite is El Tiempo Cantina). I've lived in NYC for over 16 years and have yet to find a place with authentic Tex Mex. That is, until Javelina opened a few years back.

You'll see a ton of reviews referring to their queso, specifically the Bob Armstrong. It is not over hyped, this is simply the best queso in the Northeastern United States! Get it and the brisket tacos, then wash it down with a jalapeno margarita. Thank me later!!

I celebrated my birthday at Javelina and I am so glad I did! A friend of mine had been there once and suggested it. Their menu is big, but not overwhelming. Our server, Scotty was 100% on it. He was so personable and attentive! He had great suggestions and took care of us all night. I had the steak & chicken fajitas. They were absolutely scrumptious- I will say that for the price, there probably should have been a little more meat. But that's truly my only criticism! The Bob Armstrong queso was insane and the prickly pear margarita was like a sunny summer day in a cup. Thanks to Scotty for a spectacular experience at Javelina!!

Eaten here three times already, once on a weeknight date dinner before a show at Webster Hall and twice for business lunch. We've always had a reservation and been seated promptly. Service sometimes take a while to get to the table in between visits, but they come often, so no real complaints; it's not fast food. Queso & margaritas are not to be missed - all flavors are phenomenal. Enough veggie options to suit me; I've enjoyed the salad, mushroom tacos, and avocado tacos. Husband & friends all eat meat and have never been disappointed. Today, we went during the lunch rush and had to wait a while between queso appetizer and mains arriving. Didn't complain, but did make eye contact with the server who apologized twice and then COMPED ALL FIVE OF OUR MARGARITAS. Damn. Will always return & recommend. Best sit-down Tex Mex I've had in the city. Did I mention they comped our drinks? Nom.

First time here. Honestly, this place could get 5 stars on the service alone. While waiting for our table, the bartender actually acknowledged our presence and despite it being crowded and loud, managed to offer us a cocktail menu and turn around a fabulous frozen margarita-sangria swirl in just a few minutes. We were escorted to our table quickly and were immediately presented with ice waters and a bowl of warm chips and really yummy salsa (always a good sign!). Our waiter Scotty was exceptional. His smile and positive attitude was contagious and really put us in a good mood. He was the perfect amount of attentive and it made our experience even better. The food was delicious. THE QUESO was soooooo good.  My boyfriend had the chicken fried steak, which was awesome and I had the skirt steak fajitas, which were also delicious. The portions were huge and I had no choice but to take home my leftovers because everything was that good. Shoutout to the containers they use to thoughtfully pack your leftovers; they are compartmentalized so you don't go home with a big container of mush. So thoughtful and I love it.

At the end of the meal, you're served complementary fried dough puffs with cinnamon and sugar. My ONLY callout would be that these guys would be amazing served with chocolate sauce instead of honey/syrup because they were a bit dry.

Love this place. Can't wait to come back.

Somewhat of a biased review because I had a great time and my friend knew the (wonderful and amazing) bartender - but it is legitimately a solid spot. 

The queso - OMG. We shared the mag mud quest and it was amazing. 

Warning: The spicy margarita will leave your lips numb. 

The very friendly, down to earth and attentive staff is what pushed the place over the top. I look forward to visiting again.

Fabulous! We ate there tonight, maybe our fourth or fifth visit. Brisket tacos are to die for, smoky Negroni is a lovely cocktail, and our waiter Scotty was THE BEST! We had a large-ish party and a few of us showed up late, but they were so accommodating and just nice!!!

Met up with a girlfriend for catch up dinner - wasn't particularly hungry so we decided on getting some tacos! 

After reviewing the menu however, I decided to give their signature chilli relleno a try while my friend stuck with the brisket tacos. My chilli relleno which was served with rice and beans (black or refried) - came burning hot on skillet straight from oven. I felt the burn alright. The busboy didn't give me any warning and I leaned my arm right on the handle - ouch. 

Was my dish worth the scorching hot mark? Not one bit - The dish, although very cheesy and saucy - was disappointingly bland and lacked the needed contrasting textures. It felt as if I was eating this giant pool of goo. In addition, the chilli relleno was not plump as one should be - where was the stuffing? Might as well have ordered a grilled while pepper instead. Even with side order of rice and beans - I was still hungry! 

Even though the tacos come in an order of two, my friend barely finished her first. The brisket was closer to beef jerky. The toppings and salsa didn't do much to bring the tacos back to death -There was zero flavors. 

Overall - poor quality and quantity of food, lack of communication and customer service (our waitress gave me an extremely hard time on bringing in outside coffee which I told her I wasn't going to drink in the restaurant - forced me to pour it into a glass, told me to hide in a paper bag, then spilled most of the content on the floor). The manager later came over to apologize for the miscommunication -  but of course our waitress followed up with major cold shoulder for our entire meal. Many great taco/tex mex options in the area - won't be coming back.

I had the fajitas with skirt steak and they were amazing! Though it's pretty difficult to screw up fajitas! I also has the frozen sangria margarita...it was AMAZING! Really great drink, and unique! The service was great as well. Our waitress was friendly, quick, and she checked on our table often. The place is small and intimate with a fun vibe!

Pretty disappointing and overpriced. 
We went here thinking it would be something like DOS MOLINOS which was in this spot before. 
Sadly not, the best part of the night was the chips and queso (i'm looking to say something nice here....). 

Everything else was less than basic.

Ambience: bright and loud
Food: ok, but not at that price ($16 for 2 so so tacos doesn't come with beans & rice)
Service: decent

I've been walking past Javelina for a few months and it's always brimming with patrons. Finally got to eat dinner here with a friend who also works in the area. We got there at a great time and didn't need to wait for a table. We started with the complimentary chips and dip and topped that off with an order of queso. I'm a New Yorker and can't say I'm much of a queso connoisseur, but if you're into fancier nacho cheese than what you'll find at your local Cineplex, this is for you. 

We missed HH, but ordered two drinks each. The jalapeño prickly pear was definitely the standout. As for food, my friend ordered the brisket quesadilla. It looked okay. At the suggestion of the waitress I ordered the shrimp tacos. The shrimp were of high quality but with just two shrimp per taco I would have enjoyed the chicken or steak much more. The complimentary mini donuts were a nice way to close out our meal. 

I would return to Javelina for HH and chips. The food was too expensive. In total we paid $70 each for two drinks, queso and an entree. Nope.

Amazing food and drinks. The atmosphere is lively but not obnoxiously loud. The white bob armstrong is literally heaven!  

They also were super great at hosting my birthday dinner here and gave us more than enough food. 

Love the staff and the food is delicious! I definitely suggest it if you are craving or wanting to try TexMex. It's the closest NYC has gotten.

Delicious margaritas and tacos! I loved the cactus fries, though would have never tried them had they not been suggested.  I would like to shoutout to our AWESOME waitress Elena! She was so sweet and helpful and FUN! It was my friend's birthday, and she made sure there was no shortage of drinks or snacks on our table, and even tried to help us out when we asked for coffee! Highly recommend this place ESP if you have Elena as your waitress!
First bowl of Queso was cold, and drink order was wrong. Good food, but an "eh" experience.

One of my FAVORITE meals to date in the city!  

I am from the Midwest and recently relocated from Denver.  I've never had an issue finding Queso at Mexican restaurants until moving to New York.  After many, many failed attempts, we finally caved and tried a Tex-Mex eatery... and BOOM!  Issue resolved!  

Reasons to go:
- Queso with cheese only
- Cute decor
- Queso with meat
- Sweet servers
- Queso on burgers
- Location 
- Queso on chicken sammies
- Mac & Cheese 

They do not allow you to box leftovers, they do it for you. I stressed the importance of getting every drop of Queso and the server not only didnt judge, she did a fantastic job!!

This place is awesome and needs to open a location near Turtle Bay!  I promise I would frequent the establishment weekly!

Two words: cheese dip.  Best cheese dip ever!

One of my favorites in the city, being from the south I have been in search of good tex-mex for years.  Javelina is the absolute best!

Is this a fast food place? Horrible lighting and fast food type Mexican food. The only good item is their queso. How is this place still around? The quesadilla they serve is something you would find at a food court in a mall and everything was served at room temperature and brought out all at once. This place is underwhelming and bland!

Very good Mexican food that features lots of pork dishes. I had the chicken so I can't tell you about the pork, but the chicken was very good. The chips were good and so were the sides. They have some good lunch combinations that let you try different things on the menu. I would definitely go back.

Food? Good. Jalapeño margaritas? Delicious. The service? Incredible. We spent most of the night having two different servers coming around and they were both fantastic. They even brought us around free desserts and shots because they liked us so much. I would come back for the service alone; but it didn't hurt that everything else was good as well.

Probably the blandest fish tacos I've ever had. I had to ask for salt just to make it edible. The salsa on top of the fish tacos was good, so maybe I just needed a lot more of that, the fish itself just didn't have any good flavor. My friend had a quesadilla, she also wasn't feeling it. The salsa provided at the beginning was okay, and the chips were good. Service was good. Cute interior. Overall I expected more, and know I can get good Mexican elsewhere without having to bring my own Lawry's.
The manager at this restaurant is reason enough to come here.  He is a great person who has defended women from harassment. Also, the guacamole is great :)

Haven't been here yet, but will be going for sure. Just read a great account about how the manager followed up on reports that someone associated indirectly with the restaurant had seriously harassed a woman.  He did the right thing and that's enough for me to give them a try. And I've heard the guacamole is fantastic!

Great queso and amazing service. They give you free chips as soon as you sit down and although they are delicious DO NOT fill your stomach with them as you won't have space to enjoy all the delicious food they have.

I have lived in Texas my entire life before moving to NY. This is as close as I've ever gotten to real Tex-mex since I left. I had an itch I couldn't scratch until I tried Javelina. 
Free chips and salsa... a Tex-Mex must. Queso... which if done right should be hot melty goodness made of barely-recognizable cheese varieties... check. I ordered the regular traditional yellow queso which really brought me back to home. Yum! And the chips kept coming. Dinner was steak fajitas which came on a sizzling cast iron skillet dripping with oil, onions and peppers. No, this is not a bad thing as you might expect in other restaurants. Dripping with oil is EXACTLY as it should be. It was perfect. One order was enough to serve 2. 
Washed it down with shiner bock and jalapeño margaritas... perfection
Free sopapillas for desert, dusted with cinnamon-sugar and dipped in honey. Yes!

Wednesday at 7pm. We put our name down and was told around one hour. At 9 pm, we finish our second beer at a nearby bar (where we purposefully didn't order apps to save room for queso), and we stop by to check in. Not only did the hostess know us by name, but she also unapologetically told us they stopped seating 15 min ago and "'meant to call us and cancel" never coming back.
Drinks were good. Food was not exceptional, but not bad. May be one of those one time place. Sraff/service was good

It's been two years since Pete Wells infamous review of this place, its still popular so figured it had worked out the kinks.  Kinda. Almost turned around and went somewhere else when we arrived and saw it. Atmosphere is weird, the restaurant is super bright, like fast food chain mobbed with self-conscious 20-somethings.

Food was ok, not great. First drink was great, second (same exact order) was much worse.  Both food and drinks were way overpriced for the quality. Service was good, not great. You had the sense that overall they just wanted to turn your table, for good reason, there were people lined up out the door waiting.  So many people, in fact, that it was hard to exit the restaurant as the bar/stairs/hostess stand left only a small space, which those waiting for a table completely occupied.  No one wanted to move out of the way to let people leave.  Fitting that it was necessary to push past hella rude people as the final insult of this place.

Who: Locals, families, dates, buzzed sports fans wandering out of SideBar seeking nachos

What: High quality, large portioned Mexican food. Standard Mexican menu. Very high quality ingredients. Emphasis on presentation. Very clean restaurant. Terrific waiters and busboys, trained to cater our needs before we think of them. 

When: I fell into the SideBar sports fan guest category, so I was here for an early dinner. I suspect anytime of the day will bring you a consistently fantastic meal.

Where: Gramercy/ Flatiron

Why: Very high quality Mexican food without the Dos Toros prices. Fantastic service and a suitable environment to bring anyone to. Will come back!

Having lived in Dallas for a couple years before returning to the city, I had experienced some seriously amazing tex-mex. I was on the hunt for a place in the city and came across Javelinas. Amazing margaritas, cactus fries are awesome, and cheese dip is a winner. Would highly recommend but do make reservations because they get super slammed during dinner time.

I was planning a night out for four and of course was in the mood for Mexican. I was searching on Yelp for that cuisine but also needed a certain location to properly accommodate everyone. This restaurant was a great find. Located in Flatiron it was perfectly positioned for all of us.

Now onto the experience. Two of us got there a bit early so we grabbed a drink at the bar. There was no happy hour at this time, which was fine. Not sure if they offer one. The margaritas were a bit expensive in my opinion, about $14 a piece. I just went with a cider for $8. It was my first time trying that brand, it was a recommendation from the bartender, very good.

The other two showed up and we were able to be seated right away. Once we sat down we were given chips and salsa that were so so so good! Big fan of the salsa. We ordered guacamole (medium). I am a big gauc person. This was not the best. It definitely didn't taste hot enough for me. Also the advocating was not chopped up enough in my opinion. Lastly portion seemed a bit small for $14.

We actually all ended up with the enchiladas. Two finished their plates and loved it. I loved it just couldn't finish it all. Very good meal. Also came with beans and rice where were good side portions.

Overall, it was great Mexican. Need a reservation, gets pretty crowded.

Javelina is perfect for cheese dip (as they say in the south) or queso as they say here and margaritas. It's not a fancy sit down restaurant or, in my opinion, a good first date place, but for happy hour and brunch I recommend it. It's really easy to get to and we didn't have to wait for a table for brunch, which is always a plus. The original margarita was $13 - which I did find a little pricey for the size, but it was delicious. The queso is $9 and they have multiple types to choose from. I got the breakfast tacos (2) and they were fresh, warm, but not anything spectacular. I can get the same thing in the East Village for half the price. I would definitely try it if you're craving margaritas and queso, but I would say it's a little pricey - I only went for brunch and I'll be back to try dinner!
I need the nacho cheese dip about every 2 weeks. The other dishes are pretty standard but not many dishes can compare to nacho cheese dip.

I was expecting greatness and a taste of Texas when I came but the cheese wasn't as warm as I'd hoped. We have come for dinner and brunch. The interior is cute. The restroom signs are fitting. Customer service is great but the food wasn't what I was expecting. It wasn't as flavorful as the Tex mex I'm used to, but I appreciate the effort. It's more of a cleaner version of Tex mex without that greasy flavorful kick you get back home. I still go here when I need a good batch of Queso and chips.

Really don't understand the hype about this place. The food was bland and forgettable, the prices don't match the portion size (food and drinks), not to mention the staff was completely inattentive. Don't bother to ask for a plate or utensils either because those are impossible to get, even when you ask multiple people.

Upon receiving the check our waitress gave the table a "dessert on the house" which were three little doughnut-type fried pillows. A nice little touch which lessens the blow when you see the total, but don't be fooled. These cute little treasures covered in sugar which comes with a side of honey to dip in are the shitty ending to a mediocre meal.

Oh yeah, it's impossible to even get out of the place because of the other suckers waiting to eat there are blocking the steps and exit.
Great atmosphere, amazing customer service. Loved the Bob Armstrong dip and fajitas were delicious!

I'm a girl who loves Mexican food in a city where good Mexican food is hard to find-- but this place has been my favorite since I moved here over 2 years ago! Everything on the menu is fantastic, the drinks are delicious, and it's just about the only place you can get good queso in NYC! But better than the food is the service! Everyone is so friendly, and the manager Rae is the epitome of great customer service. She goes above and beyond to be accommodating and does everything in her power to make sure every guest has a positive experience. Haven't witnessed such great service or commitment to customer satisfaction anywhere in the city whether fine dining or casual dining! My only complaint: you need more locations!!!

Really great brunch. The Mimosas were great but the best part was the queso. We split 2 different orders and we loved both of them. Service was great and fast. Overall it was a very enjoyable and we were allowed to sit for 4 hours without being rushed out.
Pricey tacos but oh soooo good and fresh, especially the beef tacos. Bill was about $60-70 for one drink, and two plates of tacos (3 each), but comes with free chips and salsa

I order Javelina through seamless and my order was a joke. I ordered 2 Chicken Tortilla Soup Dinners and I was delivered 2 tiny, half filled, cold cups of soup. The portion in the restaurant is totally different. I called to ask if this was the right order and the employee assured me that her manager packed the bag himself and those are the right portion sizes. Never ordering here again.

Food was decent, though nothing too memorable. I enjoyed the queso dip appetizer, but there was a little too much acid on my chile relleno dish, and the walnuts that came sprinkled on it were an odd choice of garnish. Good margaritas, however, and fast service.

Ambience set by teal and wood, soft lighting. Perfect spot for Valentine's night dinner with my mama. Staff were welcoming. Margaritas on-point, especially jalapeño. Tasty salad, tex-mex queso, and mushroom tacos, carried by pervasive Austin, tx spirit.

Scotty is THE MAN. Will come back just to hang and talk to this legend behind the bar. He makes a mean jalapeño marg and his energy is ON POINT. If ya don't know, now ya know. Happy Birthday Scotty!!!

Hands down, one of the best places in New York to get true Texan queso. The Bob Armstrong is delicious and paired with the Shiners on the menu makes you think you've stepped in to the Lone Star State. 

The wait staff is friendly and attentive. The rest of the menu is filled with solid Mexican dishes.

As a former Texas resident missing their queso very much, I couldn't be happier about finding javelinas. Their Bob Armstrong dip is hands down the best queso in the city, and their margaritas are amazing as well. Bonus points for having Shiner on tap. I have brought several non-Texans here who have said they now won't do any other Mexican food in the city!  One of my favorites!
There's always a wait so make a reservation. The best white queso ever and margaritas that would make the non-spanish speaking speak Spanish.
Overpriced and underwhelmed. The food was bland and not good quality. I love Tex-mex and I would advise people to skip this place.
Cheese sauce tasted like melted rubber but the margaritas were perfectly syrupy and completely masked the taste of the tequila, so that was nice. Service was good but no Ruby Tuesday's
Food was unoriginal and very expensive for what it is. The waiter was nice and they have shiner on tap. While that's all good, im still not sure I would recommend.

My boyfriend and I sat at the bar and ordered the nachos with beef, a skinny margarita, and tacos. The tacos and margarita were recommended by the bar tender who was super helpful and friendly. All was delicious Tex mex fare.

ive wanted to try this spot forever and mistakenly read reviews before i went. someone compared the vibe to the dating app tinder and that really grossed me out. needless to say, i was pleasantly surprised when i finally went. yah, the crowd is young, but thats because of the neighborhood - duh. service was on point and i had a great time soo whatever. bomb armstrong dip and fajitas for the win y'all.

Great authentic Tex Mex place in a great location. Casual place with colorful decor. Queso trio is ah-mazing. Careful not to down too much of it before your entree comes so you'll still have room in your stomach, but it'll be hard to restrain yourself.

GREAT! I have been looking for real queso in New York for awhile now. This is the place to get it! Also the atmosphere is great! People actually talk to each other which is rare for New Yorkers. Ask for Hallie. Best waitress I've had in a long time! She knows the menu and how to have a good time. 10/10 would recommend.

This was a great Tex Mex place. I couldn't resist eating the warm nacho chips that came before ordering, but it's better to save your appetite for the  actual meal. The house salad with shrimp was good and the chili lime pecans really complimented the salad with jalapeño ranch dressing. The queso sampler dip, after a bit became too cheesy, which was expected! The fish tacos portion was very tiny and there was nothing on the side either so it's good if you filled yourself with those nachos. 

The service was not great, servers forgot we were there, someone took our order someone else brought our food, so the person didn't know who ordered what. After ordering there was a long wait before the food came. And some people on the table received food others had to wait 5 minutes before their food came.

White Tex mex queso for the WIN!  Along with the habenero margarita. Granted it's super spicy but totally good and worth it. I would definitely order it again. They also seamless, it's never a disappointment if you are craving some good ole Tex mex!
Queso was good. Cheese enchiladas were truly terrible and rice and beans came out cold.

This is my go-to Mexican spot. I'm from Dallas, and Javelina's is by far the best tex-mex I have found in the city. Service is always great, drinks are reasonable priced, and you get free chips and salsa! Best thing on the menu: Bob Armstrong queso!!!

I walked in knowing it was TexMex, but expecting good TexMex. The food was beyond mediocre. The queso which everybody raves about is unfortunately subpar. The TGIFridays down the street has better Fajitas. It can be fun inside and they have a great tequilla list, but don't go expecting good food.

Fantastic experience at Javelina! Was here with a group of 10 on Cinco de Mayo, a notoriously busy day for Mexican restaurants. Javelina was extremely accommodating and friendly. The drinks were strong and the queso delicious, what more could you ask for?! I will definitely be back.
This place is perfect for southern Tex Mex. it's the only place in the city that has real southern white queso dip.

Alright guys- brace yourselves. I am about to school you on what could possibly be one of the best Tex mex joints in town. No really, they just won an award for THE BEST MARGARITA IN NY. What?! There's even a huge trophy by the bar to prove it. The queso and taquitos were beyond- the decor is amazing but best of all- were the staff, nay, ANGELS who will take care of you and brighten your day like rays of Texmex sunshine dripping with the trifecta of salsa, queso and damn good guacamole. SHOUT OUT to Samantha and Chris who were the folks that keep the wheels turning around here. Great for friends to catch up, families and couples looking for some good grub.

While there are no shortage of taquerias in the city Javelina stands to be one of the few that has been around awhile and for good reason, billing itself as the first Tex-Mex in the city. We had to put that to the test. 3.5/5.0

While for many, fajitas are a great go-to, the most exciting thing on the menu to me were the puffy tacos, which we had to order!  They arrived freshly fried and puffy just how I'd imagine them but the meat was sadly dry.

 Complimentary chips and salsa to start was great, definitely a nice perk.  The queso trio we ordered definitely hit the spot, but noticeably they do not come with enough chips and not enough staff came around to check on us. Flagging down the waiter was a chore. Lastly, the cactus fries were a nice oddity to order but as tasteless as biting into battered fried pepper.

I guess the hurt came when the bill arrived, to the tune of $70 after two beers, two puffy tacos, queso trio and cactus fries.  While I'm optimistic my feedback will help them improve, I'll still have them on my radar if I'm feeling spendy again. 3.5/5.0

This place serves truly excellent chilaquiles. They are just perfect and remind me of the ones I have eaten in Mexico. Additionally -- you cannot go wrong w the selection of different quesos. They even serve veggies to dip so you don't totally fill yourself up w tortilla chips before the main meal. The quesadilla was also good my only gripe was not enough guacamole (then again is there even such a thing as *enough* guacamole....).
Their margaritas are AMAZING! And so are the fajitas. It's a great spot for happy hour but otherwise way too expensive

Really had high hopes for this place but it wasn't a big hit for me.  The queso, which is what I came for was too salted and heavy specifically on garlic salt I believe.  The chips were thick and it just made everything too heavy between the extra salt and thick chips.  The queso looks so good but falls short on flavor.  :-( the margaritas were ok but I enjoy other places more, sad to say, and the fajitas were also just ok.  I added a star though because service was so friendly from the hostess to the bar tender to the waitress.  Perhaps there are other menu items that are better!

Ambiance was great! Margaritas were amazing (I got the avocado one). Food wasn't anything too memorable. We had a reservation but had to wait 30 mins to sit because they had some big parties. They were very attentive and courteous about it though. Great place to grab drinks and snacks with friends.
Best queso I have had in New York City. Solid guac and enchiladas. I took off a star because the service was not great.

UPDATE: went back to javelina and last night and wow, 180 experience there from my first review. I think we had just ordered wrong the first time around. Last night, we got the frozen margs instead of skinny, and boy was there a major improvement. Then our queso with chorizo came, which, as the server put it, was stupid good. I got the tortilla soup and the house salad for my mains which both tasted fresh and well seasoned, and my friend got the puffy tacos which she highly recommended afterwards. 

I will certainly be making room on my regular restaurant roster for javelina. It's a fun spot with good food and drinks and awesome service.

This place is delightful. Staff is prompt. Lots of different varieties of foods. The only issue would be the hefty price tag. But it makes sense being everything around Union Square is pricey.

We both had the chicken soup which was hearty and filling. He got the guacamole and chips. I'm not a huge fan of guac. Next came the fajitas. You know at one point, you need to sit and reevaluate your life then ask wtf are you paying nearly $30 for fajitas? That didn't come till months later. The regret takes times to marinate then hit your smack in the face months down the road. Lmfao. 

Our bill was nearly $100. Which at the moment, didn't seem bad because we left there full and happy. It's certainly a pricey place with great food. I'd come back for special occasions.

Just got off the phone with whomever was hostessing tonight. Ordered through seamless over two hours ago (nachos) and it still is not here at my place in the west village...when I expressed the fact that my food is going to be cold the hostess said "I don't know what to tell you..." extremely poor customer service and rude. I will not be ordering from here again

As a native Texan living in NYC for about 12 years now I'm always on the look for good authentic tex-mex. Javelina doesn't disappoint! They bring you fresh hot chips and salsa when you sit down. Their tortillas are homemade and the queso might be the best I've had in the city. They used to call the puffy tacos the "San Antonio Puffy Taco" and I wish they would change back the name back because Puffy Tacos come from San Antonio. If your looking for some good Tex-mex Javelina is worth trying.

Really awesome margaritas!!! However there is super limited space at the bar and no one bothered to indicate to those taking multiple chairs that it wasn't ok. (Hence the 4 stars) However the host did get my friend and I a table for a short duration so we could grab our drinks and catch up a bit. I'd love to try it out again with actual bar service next time I'm in town.

I really wanted to give this 5 stars until I bit into my chicken taquito & hit something hard.  It was either cartilage or bone & I immediately spit it out & could not make myself eat the rest.  

However, my experience prior to the taquito chicken bone was 5 stars.  I ordered thru mealpal and this place did not disappoint.  I had to wait 5 min for the additional queso I ordered to be prepped ($13 woah expensive, but worth it) so the bartender offered me some ice water.  Super nice girl, we chatted & she even gave me a reco to go to Brooklyn sometime.  Super sweet gal.  The queso was delicious, I started eating it on my walk back to work and A made a mess but B it was worth it.  Queso was spicy & savory & all the cheesy goodness you would want from a queso.  I ordered the "BOB ARMSTRONG"
that has guacamole, ground beef, pico de gallo & sour cream all mixed in.  So noms.  Recommend but probably won't order anything else on the menu other than the queso next time I go.

Looks like a fun bar so maybe margz & queso?

Had dinner at Javelina on a weekday and it was packed. We sat at the bar and shared the chicken fajitas, good quantity for two if not too hungry (plus we had a good amount of chips).

 Quality of the food was food, except for the avocado, which as someone else noted, was a bit dark. I guess maybe they peel them early and that's why they oxidize. In any case, that wouldn't deter me from coming back.

The best part of the dinner was the skinny margarita : ) I asked the bartender for a margarita, not too sweet, and he made a perfect limey marg. No wonder they have a trophy for margaritas. Will be back just for that!

Follow for more cool spot alerts: instagram.com/danapgreco

We've been in NYC for five days and we needed a taste of home... we're from Laporte, Texas.  First off Oscars knows his margaritas.... go with Heradura Repasado and you can't go wrong... splurge and have a shot of Clase Azul Repasado or Herradura Especial and start/finish the night off right.  The chile Carne asada  was perfect.  If your from Texas and missing home you can't go wrong.

Great for the cheese lover. Pretty standard tex-mex offerings. 

Otherwise, a lot loud and a lot cramped.

The food here was not good. Service slightly redeems the restaurant. Our server was fun and her recommendations were helpful but overall I wouldn't recommend this restaurant for a meal. The food is really not great and there is much better Mexican to be had in the area.

Could be fun for drinks only.

I don't typically write Yelp reviews - but I love Javelina, so I feel I must make an exception.

I'm giving Javelina a rating of 5 stars based solely on one thing: queso. Now - you may think that it is ridiculous to base an entire review on an appetizer.  First off, I would challenge your assertion that queso is an appetizer. To me, queso is a meal. QUESO IS LIFE. Second, I would tell you that as a former Texan (born and raised), I have conducted an exhaustive (nearly 6 year) quest for queso in NYC. Queso is critical to me and my pursuit of happiness. (For non-Texans, when I say 'queso' - I am referring to the magical goodness that is a cheese concoction of joy which usually has a liquid-esque consistency, and is often mixed with meat. 'Queso,' 'queso dip,' or 'chili con queso' are not to be confused with 'queso fundido.' Queso fundido is a more traditional, baked cheese dip. And while queso fundido can be found at many Mexican establishments around town, true 'chili con queso' is a Tex-Mex dish which is hard to come by in NYC).

All that said - the queso at Javelina is SPOT. ON. Having tried multiple varieties and combinations - I strongly recommend the white queso with chorizo. 

The rest of the food is just fine - good even. The stacked enchiladas are nice. 

But again - I come to this place multiple times a year (including every year on my birthday) because of my addiction to and affinity for queso (and the fact that Javelina is the ONLY place in the NYC area I have found to do it justice). At the end of the day - take it from a former Texan - if you head to Javelina, order the queso. And if you don't? Well. I don't want to know you. Who would do that? A terrible person, that's who (or a lactose-intolerant one, I suppose).

This place is where the decibel level shatters the roof. Not fun when the cacophony is too much that you cannot enjoy your food...perhaps it's a young people's place. Overall food was below average as well and service slow. Do not recommend this place.
We went there for the first time and while the food is tasty the portions are really not large enough for the prices charged,So, definitely go there but order appetizers.

Fantastic margaritas! Delicious queso! Yummy shrimp quesadillas! Excellent service! Being from Louisiana, I was skeptical finding good Tex-Mex/Cajun/Southern food in NYC! Javelina hit the spot! I highly recommend this spot if you are in the mood for Tex-Mex/Mexican food! Check Javelina out! So good!

It's not terrible! And for reasons, that's a pretty good review. I'm from Texas, I've been wanting Tex-Mex, and some friends recommended Javelina. The space is lovely and comfortable. I had the regular queso, frozen sangria swirl margarita, and huevos rancheros. Everything tasted fine, and the service was pretty good. Nothing there is amazing, but it's also not bad, so for Tex-Mex in NY, I'd recommend it. It's not Mexican food, it's its own thing, and it was pretty good.

I hail from Texas the land of Tex-Mex and I was surprisingly pleased with Javelina. The margaritas were spot on and were delivered to our specifications. The food itself was pretty good. I had the crispy beef tacos and my friend had the avocado tacos. Since he's vegan the waitress went out of her way to accommodate him. Now to the queso. The reason why I went. Not my all time favorite but a decent attempt in the Big Apple. I will say that I walked away stuffed and happy. I'm definitely going back to try the tamales. I'll skip the queso next time. But my search continues for authentic queso in NYC.

It's a real shame that this restaurant is as poorly organized and devoid of service as it is.  Even if you have a reservation, expect to wait 45 minutes to an hour to be seated. And once you are, expect the same long waits in the minimal service that you'll receive.  

Oh! And should you be interested in partaking in the catering offerings they advertise on their website, you might as well forget about it.  You can call and email and call and email and when you finally at least get the name of the manager responsible for this piece of the restaurant (Chris) he'll shirk you off, apparently not invested in gleaning any additional business from what another manager admitted to as being "a part of our offerings that isn't really set up."  

I loved the food, but after enough times being completely spurned by their customer service, I will not be patronizing this establishment again. That's how bad it is.

This may have been one of the most disappointing experiences of my life.  The food was super bland. The tacos are $7 each and we're just soggy messes. I may have not even bothered to post a review but for two people the bill before tip was $60. Please save your money!!

One of my favorite restaurants in the city. As other people have mentioned, the queso here is out of this world. We get the "Bob Armstrong" white queso. It's a huge portion and always satisfying. 

Normally I get the enchiladas which are solid but tonight we split the mixed (chicken, shrimp, steak) fajitas. It blew me away. Great flavor, huge portion and came out on a sizzling plate with a burner under it so it stays hot. It's definitely a solid choice for dinner. 

We also ordered the brisket tacos, which I thought were ok but for 16 dollars for 2, it didn't seem worth it. 

For drinks I got the smokey negrani, which was delicious. I've also had their frozen margaritas which are excellent. 

Overall a great place and always packed.

Javelina is basically like a fancier, sit-down version of Chipotle. Sure, the food is good, but it's pretty overpriced. $19 for 3 vegetarian tacos with a side of rice and beans? Please. Anyway, the servers were notably friendly and the place was packed on a weekday. It was pretty noisy and filled with a younger, trendier crowd. Not sure if I would come back here- some of my friends really enjoy it though. Also, what alarmed me was what happened after we left. There were two or three cockroaches strolling around on the sidewalk outside the restaurant. Eek.

Awful experience here.  If I could give zero stars I would.    Had the guacamole and chips that tasted like nothing.  We ordered spicy and it was bland bland bland.   
For dinner we had the brisket enchilada.  Was ok. Except for waking up at 3 am with the worst stomach pains and food poisoning.  
Both me and my friend have been sick since.   Never again....

Would give this place 0 stars if it was possible. Came in around 6 on a Sunday...the place was nearly empty. Sat down and ordered margaritas and guac. The guac was tasteless and we told the waitress, as we looked at the menu and realized she never asked if we wanted it mild, medium or spicy. We asked if we could get more spice and she looked at us as though we just committed a crime. She brought our food and was rude throughout the meal. Was conveniently nice when the check came though! We tipped and finished and my friend had a foot on the empty chair next to her. She came up and whispered in her ear to get her foot off the chair. My friend moved it and was done with the attitude of the waitress, and took her+20% tip down a dollar. The waitress ran over and grabbed the check and gave a rude look. Staff is catty, management doesn't try to understand that they should please customers and instead go talk in the kitchen and exchange glares to tables. Highschool cafeteria vibes at a place that should be a little more high end. Would not recommend eating somewhere where management can't handle criticism.

I was disappointed after hearing good things. The queso was good, however it was not very hot- it came out a little above room temperature. The crispy beef tacos had no flavor- they were like Taco Bell tacos but the meat was not even seasoned. The stacked pork enchiladas were dry- minimal sauce, also with very little spice or seasoning. The plate was hot, but the enchiladas themselves were barely above room temp. Everything here is just OK, I will not be returning.

I LOVE this place.

The drinks!!!! They have the most amazing tequila selection. I'm obsessed with the white peach margarita. It's to die for!

The food is amazing!! I recommend the white queso as an appetizer- it's packed with flavor without being too spicy. Perfect for sharing.

As a vegetarian, I'm always impressed when a restaurant has more than one option for my kind on their menu. This place will not let you down! My personal favorite is the avocado taco. It's unreal.

The service is spectacular. Our waitress, Jessica, could not have been more attentive. She was bubbly, sweet, and made wonderful recommendations. The bar staff and management are extremely friendly and accommodating.

Can't wait to come back!!

I was in the neighborhood downtown and had a wanting of some Mexican for lunch one day a week or so ago. The negatives first so that I can get out of the way - the wait was long like it takes a while because it is crowded. The staff tries their hardest and in my view they were all super friendly and tried to be courteous. Also the price tag do not expect just a quick cheap lunch this place the prices are one thing and that is high slightly overpriced.   
That said my food was good they give complimentary chips and salsa which were really delish and then I had the queso trio and the cactus fries both were really tasty wish I could say best I ever ate to honor the price tag but I can't. My friend had the Queso Trio and still raves about it.
All in all this was a good experience however not guaranteeing I will go back because of the price tag though so I have to give my experience like average somewhere in the middle.

I was super excited to try this place out with a friend since I had good things about it and I had passed it several times. We made a reservation for 9pm on a Friday and upon arrival, we were told that they were very behind. We were probably seated around 9:30 and we were starving. The host graciously told us we could go to the bar and get a round for free, which is why I am giving this restaurant three stars. I ordered quesadillas and my friend ordered fajitas, both of which took so long that we asked for them to be put in to go boxes because we were tired and ready to head home. We filled up on chips and queso, both of which were pretty good. I would really love to give this place another try in the future, perhaps on a weekday at 5pm when there is no rush and hopes for better service.

Best queso!! Also very delicious frozen strawberry margarita. My friend got a jalapeño and the bartender was able to make it just as spicy as she wanted it. We came for lunch and it was packed so we sat at the bar and had a great time. Super friendly staff. Will be coming back!

The only thing that kept this review from being five stars was the service.  The food was delicious, but overall service was incredibly slow and that seems to be a common theme from other reviews.  We shared the queso sampler and it was delicious, I honestly could not decide which one was my favorite they were all so good.  I also had the chicken and beef fajitas which was large enough to share.  The staff was friendly, but slow moving and unattentive.  Expect to pay new york prices ($$$) but that's the norm and the food was good enough to not make you feel too bad about it.  Overall I would recommend, but make sure you're not on a timeline when you show up!

I live right by here and had heard it was overrated but wanted to try it.  I made a reservation for my brother's birthday and from the moment we sat down, the server was rushing through everything.  He came up to us 3 times in under 5 minutes of sitting to order.... the food came out so fast that almost everything was undercooked - especially the steak which was ordered medium rare - it was completely red and bloody throughout.  The server made no attempt to fix or help when he noticed.  

After sitting for 50 minutes total, about to pay the check a heavy set woman with way too much clown makeup on, who is one of the managers, came over and was like, I really need you to leave so I can turn over the table.  I've never experienced that at restaurant - maybe very politely after sitting for 2 hours - but certainly not the second the food is cleared and being there under an hour.  I would say this place has problems from the management down.  

The food overall tasted like Chipotle, nothing special tex mex.  I'd save your money on this one.

We were greeted at the door by a friendly smile and seated promptly. After ordering, the food came quickly. Great food. The manager, a lovely young lady, came personally to check on our table. We will definitely be back. This place gets a thumbs up.

With so many TexMex Restaurants they not only caught my attention but I will be returning and highly recommending Javelina. 

As we walking down the street we noticed one word on a sign, 'Tequila', simple and straight to the point creative advertising at it's best (pic included). How can you walk by that? So we went inside and were quickly greeted and seated. The decor was simply minimalistic 70's with just enough accents to remind you that you in a TexMex restaurant, think guacamole and jalapeños. Shortly after our waiter Scotty arrived and asked if we needed any help or wanted to order. I explained that I have a rare allergy and usually not able to enjoy the menu without fear of visiting the nearest ER. I was presently surprised that Scotty not only was accommodating but knew what 'Carmine' was. So I ordered the cactus fruit Margarita that was the most beautiful shade of purple, a first for me(pic). Normal I do not drink anything pink purple or red because of my allergy. I felt like I was living on the edge and it was sweet with a touch of jalapeño. We continued to order with Scotty's assistance and we had the 'white queso' OMG it was heaven. The Excecutive Chef Lawrence stopped by our table to say hello and to see that everything was to our liking (great touch). We told him everything was great the only problem was we didn't have enough room to try more.

The food was delicious, ample and a great value. Scotty's personally, energy, knowledge of menu and service was top notch. We look forward to returning soon to continue working our way through the menu.

We were told they are also due to open a new location on the upper east side around East 72 and 2nd Ave. I can't wait. 
. 

When we left... I noticed the  backside of the board (or front) and it was the as clever as the front and how I was feeling (pic included).

I highly recommended. If you visit Javelina and please send Scotty and Lawrence all the best from Rose and Rocco. We hope to see them soon.

This place has a great Tex-Mex theme. They have good margaritas, but happy hour prices are more reasonable. If you are from Texas, you will find peace at this place! I moved to NYC from Texas 7 months ago. It was great to see Shiner beer on tap. Also, they serve delicious queso that will take you back to Texas for sure!!!

Pretty good hole in the wall Mexican restaurant in the Gramercy area. Would recommend any of the margaritas (avocado was my favorite!) and the queso - it's what make this place worth it. All the dishes were pretty standard, but tasted pretty good. Gets crowded and is a small spot, good for small groups not larger than four people.
The margaritas are strong. The environment is lively. But really it's all about the queso. There are five options, I have tried them all and they are all delicious.

Good guacamole. Great queso. Good food. Good drinks. What else is there to say? Plenty of Mexican/Tex-Mex places in NY and this one is a good choice. Seriously the queso is great make sure you get it here.

How have I not written a review about this place before?!?! 

Having lived in Texas for a few years there are some foods that I miss desperately and queso is my main one! The second is a prickly pear margarita, Luckily Javelina has both! 

I will say as a warning to those thinking of bringing a large party here... don't! The host staff is not great at keeping a reservation and I have had to wait many times over an hour past my reservation times even though my entire party was present. 

But as I said the queso and margs keep me coming back time and time again!
Had a great new years brunch! The food was amazing as was our server/bartender Jessica , very friendly and accommodating,  I would highly recommend Javelina

I think its the best Tex-Mex (therefore Mexican) in the city. Bob armstrong, fajitas and shiner bocks, what more could you want? I hope it stays open forever as I know this is a tough rent here. Go early or its crowded.

Normally love this place, however today's brunch has been very disappointing. Servers claimed we never asked for bottomless brunch, and the  we had the slowest service of all time. Have been here two to three hours and have been waiting 20 minutes for the next round of drinks. Will be taking our brunches elsewhere in the future.

Come for the queso and margaritas but stay for the tacos! Javelina has managed to carve itself out a nice niche in the Tex Mex market. 

Their margaritas are strong and artfully crafted and the best part: they don't get a watered down taste/flavor even after the ice has melted a little. They've also introduced this concept called a "Floater" to their margaritas in which roughly a half shot extra of tequila is added (for $2/3 more) to help supplement the margarita. Excellent bang for your buck in terms of getting a tasty and well-loaded drink. The bar area is a little crowded and there isn't a ton of space for customers waiting for a table to stand given it's the main walkway in and out as well. 

The queso dips are the next major highlights on the menu. We picked the white cheese over traditional yellow cheese. We didn't add any extra meat given their queso is already loaded a few toppings. It's no fondue but the queso pairs extremely well with their margaritas and is light years better than the complimentary salsa that is initially served with the chips. 

The rest of the menu is fairly predictable as far as mexican food goes. Fajitas, enchiladas, tacos, rice and beans etc. We opted for several of the tacos in which we were able to mix and match depending on the price. The tacos are fully loaded to the brim and most come with guacamole. The grilled shrimp was by far our favorite taco! Just the right amount of spicy texture but still very sweet!

I was definitely impressed by the portion sizes! Queso dip was a huge bowl and two tacos was absolutely more than filling. 

Food itself was good and drinks were good. If you are in the mood for Tex Mex and are in the area, worth stopping in. Javelina totally fits the bill. 

The place gets crowded - make a reservation if you can!

One of my favorite Mexican spots in the city. I come here at least once a month and typically sit at the bar. Although the bar isn't too big they manage to always make room.  The bartenders are all super nice and the drinks are great. I love them all, especially the frozen prickly pear. Not to mention they will always give you complimentary chips and salsa and the queso is the best.  Can't go wrong w the Bob Armstrong, its queso, guac and ground beef!  So goooood

Just took my wife here while we celebrated our anniversary. Their staff was super friendly and the food was great. Our favorites were the traditional queso dip and the brisket tacos! I definitely intend to check their new location on the Upper East Side.

It took 20+ minutes to even get a menu to our table.  Food was splilled on my bag and scarf while bringing it to our table which also took a long time.  Our server was delightful, but the service overall was horrid.  Even when I asked a different server for a menu, he said snarkily, yea, um gimme a few minutes... never to be seen with our menus again.  It wasnt the servers faults at all I imagine, It had to be that they were busy and completely understaffed but I would never come back.  The food was good, but for what looks like a casual place, the prices are steep and the service is poor because they need more servers.  SO Dissapointed

Do not go to this place.  One waitress waiting on tables and bartending.  20 min to get cut veggies and when the manager was asked what up she was obnoxious about it. 

Will never go back.

This is hands down the most authentic queso I have tasted in New York City. As an former resident of Austin who fell deeply in love with Bob Armstrong Queso at Matt's Famous El Rnacho (they even have a bob sticker from Austin), it is understandably challenging to find a restaurant in NYC that even comes close. Javelina's nailed it and then some. Their yellow bob queso hangs with the best queso's from Texas, their homemade tortillas put other tortillas to shame, and their service/management is full of life and excitement for the food they serve. In addition, I had their brisket tacos and a side of pickled red onions - they were excellent. As an aside, I would strongly recommend you stop by on your birthday (21+) for your complimentary raw rice birthday cake and tequila shot desert. This place is fun, honest, and will bring you back to your queso roots for anyone feeling homesick.

I came here with a friend from college on Tuesday and I have to say the queso was bomb! We didn't have a reservation so were told it would be a 2 hour wait. Luckily we were able to snag seats at the bar after about 10 minutes of hovering. But back to the queso... we got the Bob Armstrong with traditional cheese and it was definitely the highlight of the meal. It has guac and ground beef in it, as well as sour cream which I usually don't like but in this case didn't mind at all. I got the enchiladas de tejas which was highly recommended on Yelp for good reason and my friend got the tacos (which she said were pretty good) but they did look quite small. TLDR: Awesome queso with wonderful Cali ambience.
Good food, good service. prices aren't that bad either for NYC. Very fun vibes in the restaurant however can be a little loud if you are looking for somewhere quieter.

Once you go, you'll go back again. 

Margaritas that you can drink - try the spicier one (forget the name). 

Queso - best in nyc partially bc it's terrific while it isn't a common menu item. 

Steak dishes are terrific. 

Becoming a staple.

Horrible experience. Waitress got upset when I changed my queso Order a minute after placing the order. Rolled her eyes at me. As we wrapped up our dinner, she asked us if we wanted another drink, we said no thanks. She proceeds to bring us another round. I politely let her know we did not order another round. She angrily grabbed our drinks shook her head and walked away. When I asked for the bill she threw it on our table. Never ever ever coming back. Horrible service.

Has a great experience here. Came here on a busy Friday night and the noise level was pretty loud but it made our evening fun. Reservations are a must unless you're fine waiting for the bar seats or waiting it out for a table. The quest platter is a must as well as a fajita dish. Overall awesome experience here with great service and good.
Amazing food and amazing crowd. Chill place. You can come in for just a casual hangout to eat before heading out!

Seriously good Tex-Mex food and drinks. Stopped in during the afternoon, before the kitchen opened again for dinner service and stayed for a while. Wine, beer, two bowls of queso, two baskets of chips, one guacamole (yummy!) and one salsa later, we decided to wait for the kitchen to open and try their tacos and elote. Brisket and avocado tacos - both for sharing, and delicious Mexican street corn made us feel even better. Be sure to check out this unassuming, modern, spare, yet comfortable place while in the area. I know that we will be back.

Greatness comes in many forms.  Javelina is perhaps the best modern Mexican restaurant in the city.

With some of the best margaritas and queso you'll find anywhere, this is a spot you must check out if you're in the area.

Make a reservation ahead of time if you can as they tend to get packed!

I had lunch there today (brisket tacos) very good, the jalapeno gravy was amazing. Service at the bar was good ...however I was pretty put off by the server was yelling a conversation to his buddy at the opposite end of the bar about politically devisive topic.....really unprofessional. This is Manhattan...we pay alot of money to enjoy the great food and expect to be able to relax and enjoy it, thanks again for the tacos.

place is packed and lively! got a late dinner and drinks here with my friend and we had a good time. food was tasty and very filling, service was very nice as well. however, it does get quite crowded and if you don't have a reservation in advance for more popular times, you may be out of luck on getting seats.

Guac, queso, prickly pear margs, bar seating with super friendly and nice bartenders.

No complaints.

Javelina is a hip little Tex mex joint. The decor and ambiance of the place is warm and chill, making it the perfect spot for dinner with friends this last Saturday night.

We started off with a round of drinks (duh) and apps.  We ordered the guacamole and the queso, both of which received rave reviews from the entire table. Don't even think twice about ordering either of them. Just do it and thank me later. 

I ordered a glass of wine while my friends all ordered margaritas, some blended and others on the rocks. Nobody complained about their margaritas being watered down or too sweet so I would say that's a win.

As for entrees -- I ordered the vegetable fajitas which came with an amazing mix of sautéed veggies: zucchini, eggplant, bell peppers, onions, and a perfectly charred jalapeño pepper. It also came with rice, beans, and all the other normal fixings. Nothing was missed!

My friends ordered a mix of different dishes and no one had complaints but one friend -- she felt the brisket in her tacos was dry.

With that said, I give this place a solid 4 stars. Most of the dishes weren't mind blowing but none of them were terrible, and nearly all were very good. The service was alright. We all wished our server would have checked in/refilled water more often but when he did check in, he was very enjoyable. Lastly, the prices are totally fair, especially considering the large portions. 

All in all, we will be back!

Hands down, the best queso in town. If you are new to the menu, check out their queso sampler so you can find your favorite go-to. The mud gets my vote.
The tacos and nachos are really good, too. I really can't think of anything I've tried so far that wasn't exceptional. This place is all-around a top option for good Mexican in the city. It can be a little pricier than what you'd expect, but this is no run-of-the-mill food option. It's well-worth your time to stop in for dinner or brunch. Highly, highly recommend a reservation. The place is small and fill up fast. If you walk in when it's busy, expect to wait quite a while without a res (and there really isn't much room to wait in). The staff is hit or miss - some are quicker or more attentive than others, but everyone I've been served by has been very nice. Give it a shot and if nothing else, satiate your craving for queso.

If you're looking for loaded queso and some good Tex Mex, definitely check this place out. The quesadillas and tacos are tasty and the queso I'd BOMB. 

A huge reason I like this place is that it's available on open table and usually has availability for dinner on busy nights, or just a short wait. 

Also amazing margaritas. A variety of flavors and just a great place to meet up with friends for food and some boozin. Definitely recommend this place!

I met a friend for an early dinner on Tuesday night. We were seated very promptly and had water and a drink order placed veey quickly. We chatted for a little and our waiter was back in a few minutes to ask if we had questions. We did and asked for a few minutes to decide. He came for our order, I placed mine and he preceeded to run to another table without taking my friend's ordee. Well from that point on our waiter was back every few minutes asking questions. It really made us feel like he was rushing us. He slammed into my chair at one point getting to the table next to us, dropping my jacket to the floor. He kept coming to clear dishes and ask us if we wanted anything, which is good normally, but not when he's at our table every few minutes. We had the corn and shrimp tacos. Which were all good and a few rounds of drinks. But, felt so rushed.

This food was so amazing. They have this delicious white sauce that is to die for. If you like Tex-mex you will love this place and the service is good the bathrooms is clean. We had the chicken fajita with thee most aaaamazing flour tortilla I have ever tasted. They come in cute little Mexican box
This is a great Tex-Mex restaurant. The chips and salsa were awesome. The nachos and the enchiladas were our favorites.

Amazing Tex Mex! I'm from Dallas and they nail it here every time. My saving grace in nyc! 

Bartender in Sunday's is great too -knows her tequilas!!

Expect to be rushed out.  We were told they needed the table in 10-15 minutes while we were still having wine. Not what I expected after we had dinner and a bill of over $200. Waiter even took my glass of wine and I was not done. I actually saw this women (part of management) tell another guest that they had 10-15 minutes to finish up because they needed the table.. so this is the norm for them. Eat and get out!! Food.. just ok. I do not recommend.

Great food. Strong drinks. Good service. 


10/10 will come back

So. Damn. Good!

Yes guacamole 
Yes queso
Yes margaritas 
Yes beans
Yes salsa

What else do you want in life?! Goooooooo! 

Really. This is the best in the hood by far.

Tonight was my first night at Javelina and I must say, the cocktails were delightful and the queso was the best I've had in New York City! Our bartender Elizabeth was amazing! She was quick, friendly, and made our drinks perfectly! Can't wait to come back and try more if the food!

what a fantastic little gem! i came into javelina tonight with some friends as a going away dinner and i cannot say enough good things about my experience. our server, jillian, took fantastic care of us. she was so charming, offered multiple suggestions, and gave her honest opinion about interesting menu items (i.e the avocado and cilantro margarita, which IS an unusual texture for a margarita, but is EXCELLENT and very refreshing). the service was very well-paced and it never felt like we were waiting too long for anything. one of the managers, maggie, came to the table to check on us and seemed genuinely invested in whether we were having a good experience or not. everything we ordered was delicious and spot on for the tex-mex flavor profile. we tried 5 of their unique margaritas which were all very tasty! (prickly pear was my overall favorite, but honorable mention goes to the peach and habanero). you can't go wrong starting with ANY of their various queso dips or the guacamole! if you're open to venturing beyond tacos, splurge for the steak and sour cream enchiladas :) among its competitors in the area, javelina holds its own with well executed fare and cocktails and a strong service staff. thank you, jillian & maggie!

Ordered this for delivery so I can't speak for the eat-in experience, but I was very happy with my food. I got the avocado tacos and an order of nachos not expecting too much, but I was really surprised at how good the flavors were. Tacos don't always deliver the best but I wanted to take a chance and am very glad I did. Even though the tortillas had gone fairly soft and the fried avocado had lost some crispiness, the flavors and textures were still spot on. I ordered two but wished I had gotten three. The nachos were solid as well but probably much better in-house. I was a bit disappointed at the very small amount of refried beans and cheese on them. Overall very happy with my experience, especially with delivery, and would definitely go to the restaurant itself to eat!

We're BIG fans of block-heads frozen margs and have been religiously hitting that NYC chain for years on our visits. However a friend pushed us to Javelina this year and we're never looking back.

Highly reccomend giving Javelina a shot!

If you're looking for authentic Tex mex queso in NY, this is it. I'm from Austin and we were craving really good queso. We had the queso sampler and beer. The chips were thin and crunchy. Excellent texture with good snap to them. The bob Armstrong queso was the best of the 3. The complimentary salsa is also good. 

That's pretty much all we had here. Will try some other options next time. 

---------
Visited the place yesterday for the first time in awhile. Queso, guacamole and chips are fantastic. 

Enchiladas Tejanas are exceptional.  Lots of cheese, thin corn tortillas and plenty of chili sauce. 

Veggies enchiladas were good.

Went for dinner on a Saturday night,  pretty busy and had no reservations so had drinks and chips/salsa at the bar while waiting. Everything went well till we asked for to go boxes and they sent someone to get our dishes to box up.  The waiter began to pile the dishes of beans and rice on top of the main dishes,  like right on top of the food.  And we all had different rice and beans so I was interested to see how he would remember who had what. Also,  how clean are the bottom of those dishes that you just stacked right on top of my food! 
Well this morning when I opened my to go box,  surprise (not surprised) I have the wrong food. I guess I could have checked but like that was your one job! Really? Super annoyed and kinda grossed out about the way they pile on the dishes.

I've spent 15 years living in Texas and Arizona and this place has legit TexMex, Mexican that you'd expect in the Southwest. I was surprised how good it was honestly. Service was quick and friendly, chips and salsa on point and the #2 combo was very tasty. Some other items on the menu seemed a bit pricey for what they were but other than that this is a winner for me.

Real reason for the review is how great of a waitress Jilly was. The most friendly & helpful, she was a sweetheart. The margs are fantastic and the Bob Armstrong queso is too good. Definitely will be back because of Jilly!

Any Texan that leaves a good review of this place is out of their mind.  Horrible chunky salsa (like Chevy's) stale chips, margaritas too sweet and fishy tasting for some reason.  Queso far from legit- too salty and buttery ( all Texans agree queso is velveta and Rotel why try to trick it up?! I'll still pay my $10!).  Cheese Enchiladas- their "Chile con carne" was a sprinkling of taco meat on top. I can go on and on.  If you are a Texan in NYC and find hope in this place- don't.  I don't want to hurt a small business and never leave reviews but this lack of Tex-mex integrity in NYC has to end.
Not impressed ... pretty good food but terrible service unfortunately ruined my first and only experience. and really lacking in atmosphere . i miss tommy lasagna !!

I have mixed feelings about Javelina. Actually, scratch that--I have mostly negative feelings that are offset by the fact that this place has the best queso in the city.

Having moved here about a year ago from Austin, I constantly find myself having panicky moments as I realize that good queso really just doesn't exist outside of Texas. I've tried the queso at Jalapa Jar. I've tried it at Avenida Cantina. I've tried it at probably six or seven different places that I've heard have authentic queso. Until Javelina, every experience has only made me lose faith.

The queso here could be served at a Tex-Mex restaurant in Austin and I wouldn't question it. Yes, I've definitely had better, but for New York this is pretty much it. I've had both the white queso and the yellow queso (personally think the yellow is better) and they both managed to taste like more than just plain Velveeta. The chips were crunchy and salted perfectly, and the salsa wasn't too bad either.

Now onto the negatives.

Javelina has a happy hour until 6pm, but only at the bar. This wouldn't be problematic except for the fact that the bar can only seat about 6 people tops. Standing room? Forget about it. You're squished against a single wall and even when I came by myself I felt like an imposition. Want to order queso or a margarita at your table? Sorry, full price.
