This pricing model is ridiculous to me and I actually ordered my margarita at the bar the other day, brought it back to my table, and got a dirty look from our waiter. Not sorry, though. I don't make enough to pay double the price because I ordered at a table 15 feet away from the bar.

I've never actually tried the food here. Why? Because the last time I came in my friend wanted to order the tamales. They come in two options - shredded chipotle chicken with tomatillo sauce or pork with tres chiles sauce. My friend has a low spice tolerance and asked if she could get hers without sauce and with queso instead. Waiter told us it would be a $2 OR $4 surcharge. Excuse me? The queso bowl is only $10--why would $4 ever be acceptable. Also, 2 and 4 aren't really in the same ballpark. After checking, and confirming that it was in fact FOUR dollars more, my friend asked if she could just sub the tres chiles sauce with the chipotle chicken. Was told she couldn't do that because they're pre-made. Okaaaay. Then how would she have substituted the $4 queso?

I understand that this is New York and substitutions are frowned upon. But I don't think that asking for a different sauce, or no sauce at all (which she requested at one point), should be impossible. As a result she declined to order, and I followed suit. Waiter looked pissed at this point, but I'm not about to make my friend watch as I eat because you couldn't accommodate her.

The service here just feels so sub-par that I wouldn't recommend this place unless you're just coming for queso/margs and eating at the bar. Pop in, get your Tex-Mex fix, but stay far, far away from the real dining area.

If you are from Texas and need a fix of home this is the place to go. The queso is really good and they even have magmud and bob Armstrong on the menu. The best queso in nyc for sure. The margaritas are also delicious. In addition, the restaurant is so cute with upscale decorations.
Food is good but there was one waiter working the entire restaurant. I used an opentable gift card and the woman laughed at me when I told her to take 20.00 off the bill first. Very rude

I had a long, boozy weekday lunch at Javelina with my agent last month. His office was closed thanks to a water issue, and he ended up coming into Manhattan just to meet me, so we had several drinks on the company card. A great treat, as we're also long-time friends at this point, and I see him maybe once a year.

Javelina is a Tex-Mex spot near Union Square, cute and casual and pretty empty on a Thursday afternoon (we met on the late side, around 1:30). It was thinly staffed--the same guy greeted us, made our drinks, and waited our table. Service was on the hands-off side as a result, but the dude was friendly.

He also made solid drinks. I started with a Smokey Negroni, a mix of mezcal, Campari, sweet vermouth, orange peel, and habanero peach purée (it's usually made with habanero bitters, but they were out, and the substitution worked for me). I got a jalapeño margarita next, which was pleasantly spicy, then a frozen margarita once happy hour kicked in at 3:00. It was exactly what I wanted, slushy and refreshing. I also tried some of my agent's Michelada and prickly pear margarita, and they were both pretty good.

The food was solid Tex-Mex fare, nothing exceptional but mostly satisfying. The best thing was the white queso, a goopy, melty bowl of white cheese dip with jalapeños, roasted poblanos, and pico de gallo. We added chorizo, and this was a great choice. It took us a few minutes to flag down our helper and get chips to go with the queso. Queso with no chips--that's like a Gift of the Magi situation. The tortilla chips were good, golden and crunchy, as was the house salsa.

I got one of the combination plates for my lunch--a chicken taco, a brisket taco, and a pork tamale, served with jalapeño rice and black beans (you can also go with Mexican rice or refried beans). I liked the tacos fine. The chicken came with grilled chicken, guacamole, lettuce, pico de gallo, cilantro, and cotija; the brisket with slow-cooked beef brisket, jalapeño gravy, onions, mixed peppers, cilantro, and cotija. Nothing special, but sometimes a cheesy Tex-Mex taco can hit the spot. The tamale was the weak link here. The mole-like tres chiles sauce was nice, but the tamale and pork were bland and dry. The sides were decent, particularly the fluffy jalapeño rice.

This was a fun lunch that transitioned nicely into happy hour. I had to cut it short at 4:00 to meet another friend for drinks (I was a little late and a little tipsy), but would've loved to stay otherwise for another round. Javelina is a great place to get buzzed while indulging in large amounts of queso. Would highly recommend for a three-margarita lunch.

Javelina comes as close as any restaurant in NYC to offering authentic Tex-Mex cuisine. Both their queso and puffy tacos could pass for legitimate in San Antonio, as would their margaritas. I've eaten here numerous times and the staff is always very pleasant and efficient. Recommend making a reservation Thursday-Sunday as it tends to be packed on those evenings.

LOVE this place! As someone from Texas, it's hard to find good "texmex" up here in New York. However, this place hits the spot. Over the years I've referred so many friends to this place that they should have a referral program of some kind! :)

The staff is very friendly and management is all Texans...so you know its legitimate Texmex. Have come here for brithdays, drinks, my company even catered them for work lunches. I'd recommend for any meal!

Great spot for Tex mex. no reservations so definitely make one if you know you are coming here in advance. You can sit and eat at the bar (first comes first serve).  Services is kind of slow, but the food is really really good. The queso is a must try!

Came here on a Thursday night with a reservation. The ambience felt like any other nyc restaurant: loud and upbeat. Started off with the avocado margarita. It was refreshing and creamy. Had the yellow queso dip. On the saltier side. The chips were also salty. The shrimp entree was tasty along witchy the carne asada entree. The carne came out a little on the rarer side which was surprising but I like it red. Most places over cook a medium rare so I appreciated that. The food overall was good but not amazing. The service was slow and price is high but that is to be expected for a Tex mex spot. I would come back to try the other margaritas.

Seated at our reservation time..  good.  Asked for a booth table against the wall instead of a middle table, we were 3.  Host told us they had many reservations and full.  Not 10 minutes later, a party of 3 was seated at the table I asked for.  Our reservation must not have been worthy of that same table?  

3 white wines by the glass on menu.  On a Saturday evening, they were out of 2 out of the 3 whites??  No thanks to a margarita, the cheap, sweet bottle mix does not cut it for me.  

Salad was wilted and brown.  Fajita was okay, steak pieces under cooked, chicken and shrimp fine.  Queso was no better than what I could have made at home.  Oh well, gave you a try.  Disappointed and will not be returning.

We originally went to celebrate a friends birthday. I suggested this restaurant having been once before and made a reservation and we arrived on time. We had to wait a bit to be greeted and once brought over to our table, we were told our server will be with us shortly. 

When our server arrived, we ordered drinks and a starter, which arrived quickly. Our drinks however sat at the bar for quite some time. While waiting for our food, I noticed that our server was very attentive to her other tables; checking in quite often, which wasn't the case with our table. In noticing this treatment, I also realized that we were the only Black patrons of the restaurant at the time. 

When our food finally arrived, the server came over after about five minutes to ask if we'd like another round of drinks; we said sure and she quickly went to put in the order. We wanted to change one drink, however, our server was tending to other tables.  I got the attention of the bartender and let him know we'd like to change the order. Our server was standing nearby, talking to another table and when I had tried to get her attention, she didn't respond nor followup. 

During our dining experience, it felt like our server only gave the bare minimum in serving our table. Once we received  the check, we decided that the service was not worthy of 18% gratuity and decided to tip approximately 9% and when we settled the check,  the manager came over and asked about our experience due to the gratuity we left on the bill being "pretty low".  After hearing our grievances with the service, all she had to offer was an apology that felt insincere, however we said thank you. We were so appalled at the exchange we had with the manager, that we decided to leave.

This experience was cringe-worthy and embarrassing to say the least. While I cannot say that my experience earlier tonight had anything to do with the fact that we were the only Black patrons at the time, however, I can't say that it didn't either.

I am from Dallas, Texas so I'm pretttty confident in my Tex-mex taste and I liked Javelina! I've found that NYC really doesn't do texmex/mexican well at all and that it's kind of hard to find a place that is up to my standards haha. Javelina hit the spot though! Esp with the queso yum!

We ordered the guac and white queso to start. The queso is totally worth it--it's only $10 and you can add things inside of it for a surcharge. We decided to go bare and it was still so delicious. They give you such a huge portion too. This queso literally brought me back to austin/dallas and did not disappoint!!

I ordered the puffy pork tacos for my main. These were pretty good, not outstanding. The shells were fried and tasted authentic with the masa/corn flavors. The tacos were loaded, they put a ton of meat in each one. Still think they were waay over priced though at essentially $8/taco. Not used to paying this much for tacos, but they were good nevertheless. The tacos also came with rice/beans. I decided to get double rice--the spanish and the jalapeno. They gave me soooo much rice. I thought that they were both a little dry for my taste buds and flavored just ok. The jalapeno had a bit of a kick to it. 

Overall, it's a cute restaurant. It's oddly bright inside, compared to other nicer mexican places. I thought that the queso was pretty fairly priced, but everything else was a littttle more expensive than what I would've liked. I think I would be back just for the queso in the future, not sure if the food was 100% worth the price!

I was extremely impressed with Javelina and cannot wait to return.

Came with two of my girlfriends on a Saturday night, and our reservation was 8:30. Upon arrival we were told our table wasn't ready but we were given complimentary drinks (anything of our choice from the menu) due to the inconvenience, so points for service! We all chose the jalapeño margarita...it wasn't too spicy but flavorful and fresh. We loved it so much we each had 3 through the duration of the dinner!

The queso was some of the BEST I've ever had in my life- highly recommend the "mud" which mixes beans guacamole and pico de Gallo in the queso- I will be dreaming about the rich creamy consistency. The guacamole was also fresh and delicious.

For food, I had one chicken and one shrimp taco. The shrimp was cooked to perfection and the tacos were extremely fresh, and large enough to be filling with just 2! I liked both, the chicken had guacamole on it which was a nice touch. 

My friend has some allergies and Javelina was more than accommodating as well!

5 stars for service, 5 stars for food, 4 stars for ambiance (oddly was very cold inside the restaurant...) but I can't wait to return!

Great food, but questionable management and BS happy hour.

Happy hour is from 3-6pm*
*but you can only get happy hour prices if you sit at the bar or at one of the designated tables close to the bar. If you sit anywhere else in the restaurant, you cannot get happy hour prices. How weird is that!? 

Also, happy hour prices only apply to specific drinks - no specialty margaritas, and no QUESO! Genuinely confused by their happy hour policies...

Aside from that, the queso and puffy pork tacos were absolutely delicious. I would come back for the food but definitely not for "happy hour."
Great Tex-Mex, and more than that, when PostMates messed up the delivery the restaurant sent someone over themselves to make sure it was all right. Stand up people with amazing queso

I came with a group of 6 on a Thursday night and it was packed! Luckily we had a reservation and they allowed us to sit even though a member of our party was running late. The ambiance was lively and fun! We started with the Queso sampler and it did not disappoint. I tried the jalapeno margarita and it was very good, not too spicy. I had the texan cesar salad which was nice but a little overdressed. Overall, good experience and would go back, especially to try the boozy brunch!

I was so happy with my experience here! 

I came here a few weeks ago with two friends and we had a reservation. Upon arriving, the hostess said our table wasn't ready yet but if we wanted to grab a drink while we waited, it was on the house. It was really great service and the staff was super friendly and helpful.

Additionally, I have a lot of dietary restrictions and they were extremely accommodating in making sure the dishes were altered to not include gluten or dairy. I recommend the guac and the brisket tacos! Both were delicious, as was the jalapeno margarita.
The food and service were great, but there were FLIES everywhere.  IN OCTOBER.  Super gross.  I wouldnt go back.

Came here with a group of 5 and we had a res. Service is honestly very mediocre at best. The queso is the bomb & guac is very good also. I also loved the beef tacos. Didn't love the carne asada & it came at a steep price of $25. Jalapeno margs were ok - too sugary and not spicy enough.

Good Mexican food and good margarita spot. 

Ambiance: Nice heated area with traditional upscale decor. Looks like what you'd expect from a Mexican place in New York. Loud but not too bad. A bit tight in there but it's New York. 

The order: Free chips and salsa, queso sampler (white, yellow, and bob), chicken tacos with jalapeño rice, margaritas. 

Taste: So the free chips and salsa is very good and easy to fill up on. The queso dips are super good but heavy and rich. We almost didn't get the queso but very glad we did, make sure you get at least one. The chicken tacos weren't the best choice on my end. The tacos are hard to eat, it's more of a deconstructed taco because you won't be able to pick them up. They were alright but I can't recall them, if that makes sense. The jalapeño rice was good but not spicy or anything. The margaritas are good but very small for the price. 

Service: Great service, our sever was very friendly, very nice, really enjoyed her service to our loud and rowdy table. 

Overall: It was good, not the best place but solid food and solid times. The drinks are overpriced for the size, the food is alright nothing special. Very average place and good if you need a spot.

Having moved to NYC from Texas, I'm always on the hunt for flavors of home. Queso is one of those things I have missed. But not anymore! Javelina has filled that cheese shaped hole and is my new favorite Tex-Mex place in the city. 

First, start with a Mexican Martini (it's the gift that keeps on giving because you get to keep pouring the shaker yourself), or a prickly pear margarita. They also have good jalapeño ritas if you're feeling a little spicy. 

Then go for the queso sampler, because who can choose between white and yellow queso when you can just have them both! Between the "Bob Armstrong" and "Mag Mud", I go for the "Mag Mud" with beans on the side. I'm not into beans, but I don't fault my friends who are into them. You'll also get a smaller side of the yellow and white quesos by themselves. I'm more partial to white queso myself but I still love to eat both. I mean TBH I've been known to finish a whole full-size Mag Mud by myself. But don't tell anyone. ;o) 

Of course they have their complementary salsa and chips which is great on flavor, and just that they have it in general. It baffles me when I go to other NYC Mexican restaurants and they charge for chips and salsa. Come onnnn.

Guac has been hit or miss here. One time the avocados weren't quite been ripe enough so it made it hard to scoop with the chips. But other times it was spot on. 

I've had a friend get the tamales as her main and she enjoyed them a lot.  Twice now, I've gotten the chicken tacos and really enjoyed them. Really good flavor with the citrus marinade combined with guac, pico, and cotija cheese.

I have yet to try brunch here but after checking out the menu, I think it's about time. Although, one thing that I think they need on all the menus (lunch & dinner) is breakfast tacos. Don't limit breakfast tacos just to brunch! Breakfast tacos all day every day, y'all!!

They also opened another location on the upper east side earlier this year. A group of us went there for Texas Independence Day, of course, and had a blast. 

And lastly, one of the bartenders at this location is a fellow Texas State alum! Go Bobcats!

Javelina is a GREAT find in the city. Their drinks and food are amazing, and the best part about this place is COMPLIMENTARY chips and salsa. Being a recent college grad, anything I can get on the house is a huge plus for me. They may also have the best refried beans in the lower east side.

I'm in love with this place! Their salsa is soooo fresh and awesome, their black beans and rice are well-cooked and really tasty. And the salad - I don't know how they came up with such unique and fabulous recipe, but I couldn't stop eating it because it was so good! And if you like enchiladas, you have to try their enchiladas with steak and sour cream sauce - it is out of this world! (I ordered it due to my affinity for both enchiladas and sour cream.) The steak was cooked perfectly, and the sour cream sauce had the perfect balance of sour cream and spices; simply amazing! Not to mention, their service is EXCELLENTE! The host squeezed us in without a reservation on a Thursday night, and the energy of the staff was so warm and down to earth. Oh, can't forget about the big portions, reasonable prices, and did I mention excellent service?

I am from a small town near San Antonio, TX, and I have lived in NYC for a little over two years. I learned about Javelina at one of the UT alumni group's chili cook-offs a few months in. Since then, I've gone to Javelina for countless dinners and several summer Friday happy hours with coworkers, including for my birthday. My work team had our holiday dinner at Javelina last year. I live basically across the street from the newer UES location and was there on opening night (of course!), plus several other occasions. Though it is my belief that Javelina has the best Tex-Mex-style queso and margaritas in the city, they have finally disappointed me for the last time. 

INEXCUSABLY POOR SERVICE: My one-star rating is 100% reflective of their complete lack of customer service. It's just so, so horrible! Every single time. I've always left pissed off or, at the very least, just sort of bummed. The hosts are the worst offenders. They are in no way hospitable or welcoming. They act like they're doing customers a favor by allowing them to pay for food. The bartenders are usually nice. I like one Nick better than the other, and you'll soon learn my feelings toward host Nick. I think servers are hit or miss. One of the owners stopped by our table at the UES opening, and I enthusiastically told him I was from Texas and loved their food and drinks. He was completely uninterested and discourteous. So why was he even there? 

On my most recent visit, I missed my reservation by two minutes and had already been marked as a no-show. Fine. That's my fault. My out-of-town friends were running even later, so I waited for a seat at the bar and asked the host to let me know if a table came up or if there was a no-show. He seemed very unwilling to fulfill that request, and that was an accurate assumption. I spent $200 at the bar that night, while dining room tables sat empty the entire time. On the way out I sassed the host and said we would have spent more money if we had a table (at least double, I'm sure) but he just replied with "be on time." Not a hint of benevolence. No "I'm sorry we didn't get to seat you this time" or, "come back soon." Yeah, I'm never going back there. They didn't care about my business, so they lost a loyal customer and all of her queso converts. I never would have written this negative review if it weren't for his attitude. 

SO-SO FOOD: The Bob Armstrong dip is the star of the app menu, and borrowed from its namesake and Matt's el Rancho in Austin, TX. The Mexican martinis can be very good but don't truly compare to home (Trudy's, Chuy's, Baby A's and on and on). And it's not like they're trying to put their own spin on it or anything, they're just missing the mark. I think the rest of the menu is underwhelming, especially the very dry brisket tacos. I like that Union Square has Shiner Light Blonde on draft. It's my fave; my dad and his family are from Shiner, TX.

To sum up, it really does pain me to give up on Javelina. But I'm done. I guess my friends and I will have to get our fix at el Original or elsewhere from now on.

Met up with a friend here just to catch up. We had the most FABULOUS waitress (Angeliea!) She was a doll and super accommodating... we will definitely be back cause she was an absolute delight! (ps the spicy margaritas rule.. would definitely recommend! )

As someone that moved up to NYC from Austin, the ONLY cuisine this city doesn't know how to do correctly is Tex-Mex food. Thank god I found Javelina to fill the void. Great queso (what else do you need really) along with fantastic service and margs of course. Can't recommend it enough.

Hm. I was looking for a place to eat, and this place looked poppin around the bar, so went inside and there was luckily a table open.  Then it kind of went downhill from there. 

Took forever to have someone come for our drink orders.  Then forever for someone to come take our food order - we were already ready for our second round of drinks too.   Then, it was like another 30 minutes for our food to come out - and sadly, it wasn't amazing.  The puffy pork taco looked great, but in practice the taco shell totally could not handle the stuff inside and sort of disintegrated before hitting my mouth.  Really messy and I didn't understand the puffiness of the shell.  Elotes were bland and overcooked.  Enchilada was decent.  Best thing was the shrimp sam Houston though - that was tasty and I would recommend.   The jalepeno margarita I ordered was just okay and not very spicy - tasted like they were pre-made and was not comprised of fresh ingredients (mix maybe?).  

Sad experience for a Mexican restaurant.  But I liked the funny artwork on the walls!

We just came back from a meal here and the best word I could say is MEDIOCRE (and even that is being generous). 

The chips and salsa, sadly, were the highlight of the meal. We suspect that they were Costco brand (no slight to Costco). We then ordered the guacamole and I can say, without question, this was the WORST guacamole I have ever tasted. Not to mention, it costs $14! It came in a small bowl with two giant lime slices but the one thing it lacked was FLAVOR. I did not know it was possible to serve a guacamole this bland.... until tonight.

The meal came and I had the "specialty" which was the slow cooked beef brisket tacos
The brisket was tough and the tacos were lathered in sauce that made it almost impossible to hold and eat. 

Finally, our bill came. This would have been an expensive meal at a five-star Mexican restaurant, let alone here. Did I mention our waitress was rude, discourteous and unhelpful? Just shameful. 

Recommendation: Go for a drink and some chips and salsa, then walk down the street to Dos Toros for a cheap, delicious Mexican meal.

Great Tex-Mex spot with good food and friendly staff. I had the Combination plate and it is definitely the way to go. It comes with an enchilada, a taco and a tostada. It's a great way to try everything out. My favorite was the Veggie Enchilada- I loved the vegetables as well as the sauce. 

They've got a happy hour too ! The jalapeño rice was a nice surprise as well. The only let down was the guac - kind of mediocre. 

Overall, I would head there again, I liked the dishes!

Good food, meh service.

The unlimited chips and salsa that come comp are delicious.

We also ordered the queso samplier. It's good with randomly sized little containers of queso. eat quick or it solidifies as with any cheese.

The tacos are small and pricey. You do get a lot of meat though. I ordered the 2 Brisket and it came with a good amount of meat. 

I think the reason the service is so bad is because they want you to fill up on free chips to the point you aren't upset or hungry from the small portions.

I came with coworkers after a work day to get some drinks and appetizers. We got some margaritas, chicken quesadillas, and queso dip. You also get complimentary chips and salsa. The food was mediocre, but I think what was really unsettling to me was the service. 

We chose to get the queso sampler. You get three different types of queso, served in separate bowls. I know this may be petty or small to comment on but when he dropped it off on our table, he didn't arrange the dishes side by side. They were all randomly placed on our table, initially making us feel that we each would get an individual queso dish or something. By the time, he got to the third sampler, he literally dropped it in front of us or on someone's menu. Everything that was served, whether that was a margarita, a new bowl of chips, or the queso, were dropped sloppily on top of my coworker's menu. It was just weird to me and I felt like there could be more care in how you place the dishes on the table.  

Based on the service and that the food wasn't outstanding to absolve the service, I don't recommend coming here.

My go-to tex-mex spot with kind staff and delicious food. For a good price, you can get amazing jalapeno margaritas, their incredible trio queso and good entrees. Their queso is a must have when they combine the cheese with guac and beans in there. The staff is also very friendly and accomodating!

Along with all my fellow Texan reviews, I too, am a huge fan of Javelina. Growing up in the heart of Tex-Mex, you get to know good food when you taste it, which we CRAVE it like no other. 

Thankfully, Javelina delivers a VARIETY of queso dips, unlike ANY OTHER place in this city. At least, none to our knowledge. Queso isn't a thing up here, which is a damn shame. 

Yes, Javelina does miss the customer service mark, at times. Yes, the frozen margarita machine may not produce the most frozen consistency. Yes, you might get one tortilla chip with wayyy too much salt. However, the food is on point and outweighs some of the negatives. 

Suck it up people and queso-on. All in the name of Queso. 

#QuesoFoLife

Only vegan option is a rather terrible vegetable fajita. Veggies are unseasoned. They'll still give you sour cream even if you tell them not to. Guacamole is more like a garnish. I've never had a bad tortilla with a fajita until I came here...
COME EAT HERE! Andres is the nicest man to exist he chased us down the street with a bag we forgot he is the greatest man 10/10 would recommend!

I will come back here everytime I am in New York. Bob Armstrong dip, brisket tacos, and enchiladas were all great. Definitely one of my favorite meals during our trip. It is nice to find Tex-Mex this good in a place a didn't I expect to find it.

Update: The owner Matt reached out to me via Yelp to clarify the confusion. He was so professional, and I more than appreciate the customer service I received from him! Thanks!

It is with regret I am writing such a bad review. I have recently moved to Texas, but I lived in NY for college. We returned to the city earlier this week & were so excited to eat at one of our favorite New York restaurants! I usually eat at the UES location, which was closed temporarily to a fire. I've been to the union location before, and differed we would return since we love eating at Javelina so much. I made a reservation on open table to make sure we got a table for happy hour, which on the website is advertised 3-6 on weekdays. When we arrived at 5, the hostess was not there & the bartender welcomed us with a smiling face and asked us to join him at the bar for happy hour. I gladly told him, we're here for happy hour, but we made a reservation and would prefer a table for our group of 4. He sat us, admitting he didn't know what he was doing, and gladly sat us. Our waitress was so sweet and had great service! My review is solely based off the attitude of the manager and the false advertising on the menu- so beware! My group of 4 ordered a couple rounds of margaritas, queso & guac. Since it was happy hour, our menu said that our normally priced $14 margs would only be $6! Which is the whole reason we came to the restaurant when we did, for the great deal. When we got our check, I noticed we did not get happy hour prices, no big deal I thought! I let our sweet waitress know and she told us that the happy hour prices only apply to the bar. What??? There was only two other tables taken at this restaurant & 90% of the bar was empty. What difference does it make if we order 5 feet from the bar at our reserved table?? The manager came over very defensive. We explained to her that we let the man who sat us know we were here for happy hour. If the deal only applied to the bar- we would have liked to know & would have gladly sat there. I also explained to her that the menu we were given did not specify BAR ONLY. she immediately told me I was wrong (I've worked in customer service, the customer is always right.) and she brought over a menu (one we were NOT given) that said happy hour is bar only. I proceeded to tell her that this is not the menu we were given when we sat down.  She took our bill angrily and changed our bill. Thank God! I don't want to have to write a bad review- but I really want to warn others that if you are coming here for the happy hour prices- please know that it is at the BAR ONLY as this is NOT what is advertised. I love Javelina and I am so upset this was our last experience here. I can't wait for the UES to open back up.

I gave 2 stars because of there ridiculous system of seating patrons.First you need reservations ok fine,Then you go on to a waitlist also fine.The problem is they never explain that u will not get a table if no one cancel.So you will be forced in between the present reservations.And that is every other hour.My friend and myself stood at rhe for an hour,then host staff comes and tells you They can seat you but they need the table within an hour.Food qnd drinks were good.But that crazy system I have never in countered.I will do takeout if I decide to return.
we went for brunch, my quesadillas were great, we also had tacos and frozen margaritas. Staff is nice , atmosphere is good. We would come back
The service and drinks were amazing. The food was good. I loved the cilantro and avocado margarita it was great!

Taco Thursday is now a thing! Had a great dinner with drinks, free flowing chips and salsa, and great entrees. Service was fast & friendly, and everything was super tasty! Will definitely be back to try the queso

I really loved the food! We had reservations and were seated immediately. The service was great and very quick. The queso was amazing and I have had lots to compare it to; I love Texas queso best but this is the MOST authentic I've tried in New York. The steak enchiladas were pretty good but I wish there was more sauce on them. It was pretty dry and the hanger steak ranged from medium rare to well done.

Came here on a Friday night with friends. Packed. Make a reservation to save time. Super delish margaritas. They get right to the point. Fresh guacamole and tasty tortilla chips that crunch.  I had the enchiladas. Just the right size portion...not too much...not too little. Will come back again!

I found Javelina after being thoroughly let down by my previous favorite tex mex joint in town. These guys are channeling their inner Sam Houston. The queso has this fantastic flavor that I can't really pinpoint. The chips are made in house and thin but don't break too easily under the intense pressure of their thick queso. The tacos had a bit too much lettuce which made it messy, but the fried avocado was perfect and crispy. 

On top of that, the service was exactly what you want. He didn't bother us, but was on it every single time we needed something! Literally once I looked down at our chips and thought to myself "oh, wow, I ate all those tasty chips, I'd better get more." And bam, there he was with more chips. He may have been able to read my mind. And I'm ok with it.

Veg Traveler - As a Texan I was skeptical about Mexican food in New York. Especially, one billed as TexMex. However, I was pleasantly surprised by Javelina. The atmosphere is comfortable and quiet enough to have a please conversation with out raising your voice.  

The margaritas were handmade (no mix). The veggie enchiladas were excellent. As I ordered them the server asked if I was vegetarian. Then proceed to suggest the rice and black beans that were also vegetarian. Thus, eliminating the dance of asking if the beams and rice were vegetarian. The guacamole was fresh and chunky. There are several option Queso which were really good too. Non-veg friends in my party enjoyed the chickens tamales, and brisket nachos. 

The service was attentive without being intrusive. 
The portions were enough that I asked for a to go box. They were kind enough to pack them up for me. Always a nice touch. 

Maybe not a thing we always think about but tells me a lot about a restaurant. The bathrooms were clean and well kept. 

I will visit again when I have a Mexican food graving in NYC. I'd recommend it to any Texan.
Went for dinner, ate at the bar. The margarita was served half full. Ordered meat medium, it came out bloody rare. The steak was like a piece of rubber, and all the food was served luke warm.  Avoid.

Was not impressed at all! Got guacamole for the table and was asked if we wanted it spicy or not. We asked for it to be spicy but it was the blandest guacamole ever! We asked for extra jalapeños and got a little cup of chopped up jalapeños, but it still wasn't enough. There was no flavor to the guacamole. The fried fish tacos were not bad and the sauce on that actually had more spices to it, but without good guacamole it's not worth a try.

I love this lil bottom floor mexican oasis in the hussle and bussle of union square. The staff was friendly and kind. Greated us at the door. Let us sit where we wanted too! And introduced out server (the famous dre) he was super  knowledgable kind and "on it". To start off they brought chips and salsa out to the table and my my my they kept them coming. Everyone I know eats a ton of chips and salsa. I always endulge but man I got few friends that will put them down. I have to say alot of times at mexican places you got a decent fresh flavor with an awesome cilantro, tomatoe and garlic. A very special thing with javelina is this fantastic smoked habenero salsa perfection. This was the opposite of a watery mess. Low moisture salsa perfect for scooping with crispy and fresh corn chips. The smokey habernero flavor to the front of the pallete complimented with your salsa staple rockstars. We enjoyed the shrimp tacos which honestly I could eat for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Everything was fresh and professional. I do need to mention the music was kind of disconnected it was like folky punk stuff. Id really like to hear some beauno vista social club or even possibly contenporary south american world music. Other then that this place comes highly recomended and I really loved everything. The salsa was a stand out star and I am totally impressed.

Stoped in to this cute little restaurant in East Village for a Margarita with family.I had the Jalapeño, my daughter had the Prickly Pear and my husband had the Traditional. All were really good, pricey( not unexpected for NYC), and I would recommend them all. The food looked fantastic- confirmed by my daughter-but we were too full from dinner. Bartender was friendly and attentive.  Will come back to try their food next time!

As a native Texan, I have been to Javelina multiple times, usually with fellow displaced Texans craving some queso.

The restaurant is a medium size, and service is good.  Chips and salsa come with your meal and are refilled frequently.

I have tried the following dishes:

Traditional Queso (3/5): This queso is all right.  It is a bit generic but definitely satisfies your queso cravings if you're in the mood.

White Queso (3.5/5): Definitely my preferred queso of the two that I have tried.  Comes with jalapenos and poblanos, which give it a little kick.

Guacamole (3.5/5): A nice, standard guacamole.  You can get it mild, medium, or hot.  The hot is not as hot as I would like, and I wish there were some lime in the guac, which I love.

Nachos (3.5/5): A nice nacho dish, very standard, nothing special.

Javelina Salad (3.5/5): This is a nice option if you are trying to keep the calorie count low.  The salad is large, with a nice mix of greens.  It is served with a pomegranate vinaigrette that is really interesting and tasty.

Shrimp Sam Houston (4.5/5): I really like this dish.  The shrimp comes in kind of a stew with peppers and tomatillo, and you place this mixture on tortillas to eat.  The shrimp was cooked really nicely, and I loved the sauce it came in.  Definitely would order again.

I have always had good experiences at Javelina and am sure I will return soon.

Javelina is pretty much the only mexican restaurant I've found in NYC that has cheese dip that isn't queso fundido. It's pretty good and that's the best thing I can say about the restaurant. I've been here a handful of times. 

The service here is absolutely horrible. It took 20 minutes after being seated to be even asked about drinks/appetizers. Afterwards, my partner and I waited over 30 minutes to even be asked what we want to eat. After waiting an additional 30 minutes, we asked the waiter to just receive our checks and go. It took an additional 20 minutes and a visit to the bar to get the manager's attention so that we could leave. All around terrible experience. They comp'd our food  after the second round of complaints but that doesn't make up for it.

As an Oklahoman, i am always on the search for good Tex mex in the city. This nailed it. Excellent service from Andre. Amazing drinks. Incredible chips, queso and salsa. The fajitas were fantastic. The tortillas were some of the best I have ever had. Authentic, warm, fresh tortillas. Will be going back and will be bringing friends. Loved it so much. Thank you for a wonderful lunch.

Great food - specifically love the queso and avocado tacos.  You almost always need to have reservations, which is a bit unfortunate, otherwise you will have a bit of a wait or will have to hover around the bar for seats if you walk in.  Have had varying experiences with waitstaff - have been completely ignored before, but I wouldn't say that is a constant.

One word summary: YUM!

I love this place! I've been twice now and each time was a pleasant experience, both great food and great service. Must have's in my opinion include the jalapeno/spicy margaritas & the queso that has black beans, guac, and pico mixed into it! I think you could come here for just margs and queso/apps and be totally happy with the experience.

However, the entrees are pretty darn good, too! The first time I came, I got the chicken enchiladas - it was a tangy verde sauce, and perfect amount of cheesy. The second time, I got chicken fajitas - the chicken was cooked PERFECTLY, seasoned so well with great veggies, and served with steaming tortillas.

Will be back here multiple times - good for groups (family or friends) & dates!

My gf made reservations for 6:30pm on a Thursday and we were immediately seated when we arrived. Our server was quick, friendly, and immediately brought out complimentary chips and salsa as we looked at our menus. They were out of the prickly pear margarita that night so we opted to try the white peach and jalapeño margarita on the rocks instead - so delicious! Both of us being from Texas, we can be harsh critics when it comes to queso, but not only did they have the choices of white and yellow, it was perfectly made! My gf ordered the skirt steak fajita and I ordered the sour cream and steak enchilada. Both dishes were portioned well, filling, and delicious. I don't eat a lot of Mexican food in NY since the flavors and value can't compare to the places back home in Texas, but I will definitely think of Javelina next time I'm having strong Mexican food cravings.

I'll be coming back here countless times I can see already after eating here just once. I would recommend making reservations before going. My boyfriend and I waited an hour and 15 mins to be seated, but I just blame that on the popularity and it being our first time not knowing. So thank goodness Union Square is near by to go play around in if you have to wait. Everything about the food was delicious. The waitress we had was excellent and on top of things. Anybody that comes to NYC to visit me, I take them here if they want Mexican food. LOVE IT! (the bob armstrong queso dip and fajitas....to die for :-)

I had a truly great experience here and will definitely be returning when I'm in the area. 

The restaurant's pleasant atmosphere and friendly staff members made me feel happy with my decision to eat there almost immediately after being seated, but of course the delicious food made it even more enjoyable. The sauce and meat in my meal were so tasty and even remained delicious as leftovers the next day. 

Honestly was one of the best meals and overall experiences I've had at a restaurant in quite a while!

What a great experience at Javelina. We enjoyed the skinny dip and guacamole to start and shared 2 steak fajitas for 3.  Our favorite is always the Bob Armstrong dip. We loved the manager/waitress Samantha! She went above and beyond to make sure our night was great! Thanks!

So there is no confusion, Javelina is not a Mexican restaurant. Javelina is a Tex-Mex restaurant. The food served at Javelina is what you might find in Austin or Houston rather than Mexico City or Juarez. Plenty of sour cream and cheese can be found on many dishes or added. The Bob Armstrong Queso is great. The drinks are pretty awesome as well. So when you need your Tex-Mex fix, head over to Javelina. You will not be disappointed.

This place is great! Make sure to make reservations especially if you intend to come on the weekends...we initially came Friday evening and were quoted a 2 hour wait. We ended up coming Saturday and it was less packed. The drinks were on point...my favorite was the prickly pear..MMMmm. We got steak quesadilla, the brisket taco, and shrimp quesadilla. All were delicious and super filling. I'll definitely be back soon!
One of my fav Tex-mex spots in New York. Great food and awesome drinks , service is good, and come have a chill time atmosphere. Love the fajitas and guacamole. Definitely coming back for some more.

As a Texan living in Brooklyn, it is SO REFRESHING to have found a Tex-Mex spot in the city. Their queso meets my super high standards and their spicy margarita is life-giving. This is my go-to happy hour spot. You must get the Bob Armstrong queso with queso blanco. This place feels just like home away from home.

My girlfriend and I have not been able to stop craving the queso since we came here last week, it was so delicious. Great margaritas too and prices are good during happy hour. Will definitely be back.

We went at ~5PM on a Wednesday; the restaurant was a bit cold but that might just be me.
We got drinks that were supposed to be Happy hour price, but when I looked at the receipt later on we were charged full price. That's the reason for four stars...
Otherwise, we both got Fajitas, and the serving sizes and different options available for the dish were aplenty. My diet is fairly specific, to say the least, and their willingness to offer a plain salad or extra of one thing subbed for another at no charge was very much appreciated.
The Veggie Fajita dish was DELICIOUS and a ton of properly cooked, hearty bunot overly oily vegetables. My wife really enjoyed her Steak Fajitas as well, and all in all we both had a great time.

An honest review of a Manhattan "Tex-Mex" restaurant from an actual Texan.

Came here with high hopes over the weekend, as we have been looking for a good Tex-Mex restaurant in the city for some time now. Made reservations because we read this was a necessity, but when we showed up, there were quite a few tables available and we were seated right away.

First off, the good:

Chips and salsa, and they were plentiful! A rarity for Mexican restaurants in NYC. The margarita prices aren't too bad. $12-13 for frozen or on the rocks. The service is also very good, very attentive. Oh and the white queso, albeit not particularly "Tex-Mex" is wonderful, would highly recommend.

The bad:

I hate to say it, but the food was just not good. Maybe it was the dishes we got. My wife got the chicken mole enchiladas and I got the chicken enchiladas. To start, my chicken enchiladas were pretty decent, basically, a classic chicken verde sauce which would usually have sour cream at most restaurants in Texas, but this was really just the sauce and some cheese. It came paired with refried beans and Mexican rice. The rice was good but the beans were basically a soup. Too watery and too difficult to eat considering they only gave us forks.

My wife's chicken mole was more of a disaster. I'm not sure if it was just a bad night for the kitchen, but the mole was extremely bitter. I've had mole a million times and this was honestly the only time either of us could say we didn't want to take another bite. I grew up having mole in San Antonio and all over south Texas so I'm not going to hold Javelina to that unfair standard, however, even in Manhattan, I can think of numerous places with significantly better mole.

Lastly, the prices... $18 or $19 for two enchiladas and two small sides of rice and beans... I know this is Manhattan, but for the quality of food, totally unreasonable. For two people who split an appetizer, each ordered a drink, each got enchilada plates, after tip almost $100. For that, I would've rather gone to Rosie's or La Contenta.

I think we will not likely come back, unfortunately. It's a shame, because there is a real opportunity for some good Tex-Mex in Manhattan. This place isn't it.

I'm a native Texan who moved to NYC 6 months ago, and I've already been here 6 times. It's delicious, and it's definitely the closest thing to real TEX-Mex that I've found (and I've been hunting).
It's hard to find food that's actually spicy up here, but the habanero queso delivers! They also have flour tortillas and chile con queso -- notorious Tex-Mex staples that you won't find at any authentic Mexican food place. And, of course, margaritas and Shiner beers. What more could you want!

Best queso I have ever had. 

I had to start my review with that fun fact just in case you didn't read the whole review. To start off, their drinks are great. Pricey, in my opinion, but great. The staff is extremely friendly and attentive. 

For main courses, I personally like their enchiladas. They are packed with flavor and are extremely fresh. 

Now....for the queso. I thought I had good queso until I came here. It is cheesy and ohhhhhh so delicious. I would  recommend the Bob Armstrong queso but they are all great.
This place is great! Very consistent! Excellent drinks and food. Cozy atmosphere. Kind of loud when crowded, but that is to be expected.
Ah I was hoping to really like this place! Been searching for good breakfast tacos in the city. These weren't bad but just nothing compared to real tex-mex! I'd stop in for some margs and queso!

So the quest comes really close especially if you get it with taco meat/picadillo. The fajitas at the next table sizzled as they should. The pulled pork taco is not authentic Tex Mex but my friend liked it. I went for my go to Tex Mex test. If they can't do enchiladas it's no bueno. What ruined the enchiladas is the grease in the chile con carne. The flavor was right but I had to siphon off the Greene before eating it. Seems they could have done that for me. Guacamole is oddly high priced like it is at most places these days. Margaritas were tasty but mild in effect. I'll return but would try something else. Service was great through. We walked in on a Friday with no reserve and were accommodated. The waitress what nervous bc I'm from TX but did a great job.

Good Tex-Mex food.  Spacious seating with tables not too cramped together to each other.  The drinks are also very good.  They have a really excellent queso dip that I could eat with a spoon!  You can get white or yellow.  The food is reasonably priced and the service is really friendly.

When I think Mexican - I think flavor. 

The food truly lacked flavor. Seasoning was nonexistent. Lacked substance. The rice was tasteless. The refried beans were reheated and almost dry. The brisket tacos were served wet. 

Javelina is mediocre to average at best. Tex-Mex, this place is not. 

Sadly, Taco Bell makes a more flavorful taco. Look elsewhere.

Pretty horrible stopped in for drink and some snacks but never got t order food as when looked  around place was filthy. Most tiles on ceiling were covered take a looK at pics can only imagine what the kitchen must look like

Looks super cute but one of those places where you can't sit until your entire party is here...
Even with a reservation, for two,  and ten open tables... they won't let me sit.  Funny thing is I would probably be onn my second marg by now....

came here with 2 of my girlfriends on a Saturday night for 8:30pm reservation. they sat us right away, place was packed - i did not like the table we got, as it was close to the bar and right by the pathway where everyone would constantly walk. 

the food was unreal - guac was fresh. i got the veggie enchiladas which were AMAZING. the sauce was great, the side of jalapeno rice was great i got the frozen avocado cilantro marg first then got the frozen habanero peach marg next. both were great. my friends got a spicy jalapeno marg and wasnt impressed - said something was missing. our waitress was so sweet and kept apologizing that they ran out of shrimp. i highly recommend this spot !!

Pros: solid food and drink (nothing incredible, but above average as far as Mexican food goes and priced appropriately), friendly staff, fine atmosphere (a little cramped but that's Manhattan)

Cons: I went with 3 other people, we got two apps and two entrees total and 3/4 items were incorrect. No meat on nachos we ordered, wrong queso and wrong fajitas. Staff was apologetic and I get that mistakes happen, but it seemed odd that the majority of our orders were wrong. Didn't necessarily seem like it was the waiter's fault but rather everything seemed hectic and like the staff was working on speed over accuracy in an attempt to get people in and out quickly.

Really not good. I asked for no pico de gallo in my queso and it was in it with and had cilantro which I hate... the queso is NOT as good as the Tex Mex Queso you get in the South contrary to some reviews saying so. The fajitas were overpriced and a very small serving. Would not recommend ordering online or delivery. Maybe it's better in the restaurant.

Wow- how quickly things can go downhill.

I have been a loyal customer at Javelina for months now but am severely disappointed with my recent experience.

I was craving some queso, and if anyone else ever reads my reviews you would know that cheese is queen to me. So naturally, when I opened up my delivery and saw that the $19 Pint of Queso I ordered was not included, I was upset. 

I attempted to call the restaurant directly to reconcile this issue. I called four times with no response!

Out of choices, I contacted Seamless, who was able to get in touch with the restaurant only to discover that it was no accident- they KNEW they were out of queso and still decided to deliver my order KNOWING that I had already paid for said item without contacting me at all!! 

Seamless offered to refund the queso but in all honesty I didn't want to eat the meal anymore because I like it drowning in queso. So I asked for the CR to call them back to ask if they could provide a different flavor. She then received no answer after calling multiple times. Awful.

In the end, I was stuck with food I didn't want and I was in a terrible mood because that is horrific customer service. Seamless was the only saving grace. 

Take note: if you are out of something, that's understandable but you NEED to contact them! 

If they had just called and told me unfortunately they were out of what I wanted, I would have been able to tell them in that case I didn't want the order at all. Now there's just this wasted food. 

I won't be ordering or visiting them again. Poor service is the limit. 

1/5

Ok... I am torn between a 3 and a 3.5 stars. The drinks are pretty good and staff works quite quickly on service, which is great, cause this place has been packed every time I come. That said I love the light decor scheme which always makes me feel like the wait is worth it and I will have a good time. 

An ex-bf brought me here my first time as he is from Texas and mentioned something about Texas style queso dip. We both love tequila and so, I was curious about this dip. We sat at the bar and had the queso with brisket which was quite interesting... though I thought it was going to be a little bit saltier or have some type of flavor... it was ok, actually, kind of bland (I'm Latino and am used to bold big flavors).. Don't get me wrong, we ate the whole thing, just not as memorable and the times I have been back, I never ordered it again. I think maybe adding some more heat would have really turned it out. Chips here are pretty great and well slated (I think they may be fried at location). The frozen pear margarita ($10 a pop) here is quite good! I thin actually, it's the only drink I have ordered here every time I come. I can drink a frozen drink even in the middle of winter if it's a good one.. otherwise, normally go for a skinny margarita, and this place can rock that out as well with their good selection of premium tequilas. If you come Mon-Friday form 3-6 pm the drinks are $6 - so shave off 40% on drinks and appetizers. Not bad.

As an entree - I have had the fried fish tacos an the shrimp tacos. Both orders were really good.. and I honestly like to stay with light meals cause   I prefer my calories in liquid form (bottoms up!). I will say that overall, the prices for the tacos here a a little higher than at other restaurants.. but it's good quality as far as I'm concerned and I've never left hungry. I honestly think it's just that while tasty, it's not the first restaurant that pops in my head when asked about amazing Mexican food. 

I'd recommend for a third date. They do something right cause they are always full (in my experience), but sometimes you have to wait, and when you don't, costumers can be a little noisy in this narrow restaurant.

I've been going to Javelina for years and until recently, I wouldve given them a 5-star for sure.  But, first of all, they re-did their menu--I wouldn't even bother going there for anything but drinks and queso anymore.  Also today, the host, Nick refused to seat me, my sister and sleeping baby in the mid-afternoon although the place was basically empty.  He said they were "fully booked," even though I could see it was empty.  We grabbed a drink at the bar, and only after an hour did they finally offer us a table (the place was still half empty at that point).  I know that babies can be disruptive at restaurants, especially in the evening, but mine was sleeping the entire time.  The host was just plain rude.

We ordered through Caviar last night and it was delicious! That's saying a lot since we are from Texas and love TexMex! Got the beef taco and chicken/beef fajitas - delicious! How they were still that good all the way to FiDi is amazing! Also had chips and queso that were about as good as we can get in Dallas!! Will definitely be ordering again and can't wait to try in person once this craziness is over (and of course try their margaritas)! Thanks for giving us a taste of home during this quarantine!!

So mad at myself for skipping over this place for so long. It's pretty authentic Tex-Mex! Having grown up along the southern border, Javelina takes me back. I've ordered from there several times and it never disappoints, though I do have my favorites. Any of the enchiladas are bomb (chicken being my go-to), the rice and refried beans are authentic and whether you go with the white or yellow queso, you can't go wrong. The corn tortillas appear to be homemade and the tortilla chips are addicting. All of the frozen margs are a real treat too and a cut above those frozen syrup-y drinks you find at a lot of bars. If we ever get back to eating indoors, it has a really cute ambience and is a great place for happy hour or a date!

Delicious and very fresh tasting. The tortillas i have to admit are my favorite thing from here - they taste hand made and come with the fajitas. 

I would also recommend the peach or strawberry margaritas- always a fan favorite!

Had a lovely dinner there this evening sitting at a table nicely distanced with plant boxes around it separating us from the street. No happy hour but the drinks are good and the food was really good. The service was also terrific. It's nice to be able to eat out at a restaurant comfortably outdoors.

We just ordered from them and it was DELICIOUS!! Fresh and beautifully prepared. Fast delivery.  Margarita was so yummy I am typing in CAPS!! Fresh fresh guac.  Fresh supple tortillas. Crisp chips. Wow!  Kids ate up the chicken fingers.  Highly recommend.

I have been going to this place for years -- it's amazing. Great staff, such great food, lots of outdoor seating for Covid. 

My favorites:
-- prickly pear and habanero and white peach FROZEN ALWAYS frozen margaritas: perfection and always filled to brim!
-- the bob armstrong queso or the white queso: everything about these are amazing. My roommate is from Texas and she loves this queso!! Also the queso sampler is a good option if you want to try multiple. 
-- the red headed stranger tacos: perfect, filling, and exactly what you need if you're hungover. 

The guac is solid and the CHIPS ARE INSANE. They always come out hot and crispy with fresh, perfectly spiced salsa that you will want to marry -- it's that good!!

I just love it here
Lots of outdoor seating, and amazing fun and service.  My friend had the steak quesadilla and the steak was cooked perfectly. Definitely exceeded expectations.

When Javelina first opened a few years ago I left a pretty scathing review. I have to say they've really turned things around the last 6-12 months! It's my go to now whenever I have a hankering for Tex-Mex. Soooo glad they figured things out!!! It will likely satisfy most Texans living in NYC when they need a fix. Is it your neighborhood Tex-Mex spot that makes the best enchiladas ever? No; but it's pretty darn close for NYC. Props!

The worst food experience I've had in NYC. My meal was delivered an hour late, they didn't follow the special instructions so we couldn't even eat what they gave us, the food was cold and mushy, and the customer service was awful. Go to Taco Bell instead

I love queso and when I found out they had a sampler, I knew I had to go and check it out.

The service was great, we did outdoor seating and the tables were at least 6ft apart. We ended up getting the queso sampler with a side of corn tortillas and holy shit was it fantastic! 
I legit could've had only that and I would've been content.

We ended up getting the tacos and the enchiladas, but to be honest, it was nothing special. 

I would come back just for the sampler and drinks.

This used to be one of my favorite places - I love the food and the staff is friendly. I ordered from Postmates yesterday and found a piece of hard metal in my food (possibly a bent staple). I also saw a mouse running around inside the last time I was there. The server gave us a free round of drinks and I was going to give this place the benefit of the doubt, but now with two safety issues, I wouldn't risk eating here.

Hands down best tex mex in the city. Really the only tex mex I have found that is comparable to Texas. Bob Armstrong Queso and fajitas are my favorites! They also have excellent margaritas and a great outdoor dining set up. Only criticism is to beware if you are ordering delivery from them on apps it can sometimes take up to 2 hours so it's better to order directly from them!
Great Tex-mex spot. Emphasis on the Texas sized portions, but the food is too good not to finish. We ordered a combo plate and asada enchilada - very good!

If I could give this spot 6 stars I would!! I am a huge Tex-Mex fan, and this place truly takes the cake. I'm giving 5 stars for the quality of the food and the service.

Today, I did indoor dining with my fiance and his cousin. They checked our temperatures, had us scan their app for contact tracing and sat us to our table. They have dividers between tables so you can enjoy your meal without worrying about being too close to another party. When we arrived to our table, there were chips and salsa WAITING FOR US there. Seriously such a small gesture, but it made us feel so welcomed and ya girl was hungry so this was perfect.

Shortly after, they provided another sweet small gesture. The waitress handed us three small cups of hot chocolate and said they were giving them away for free today. They were delicious!! How thoughtful is that?!

Throughout the visit, we never had to ask for more water, chips or salsa. They kept such a close eye on us with refills so that we could focus on and enjoy our conversation.

I ordered the sizzling skirt steak fajitas and WOW!! I've had many steak fajitas in my day, and I'm obsessed. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare.

I highly recommend this restaurant!!!

When I'm missing Texas and it's Tex Mex Javelina hits the spot! They're classic queso and chicken fajitas. Maybe get some quesadillas and corn. Plus every margarita they have is incredible! I'm normally a purist when it comes to a lime frozen margarita, but i really love their spicy and other flavor too! Would definitely recommend
The best queso I have ever had. I usually get take out from this location however the UES location is great to dine in

Having seen some of the reviews and read NYT review (way back from the early days), I was dubious of this place. But they did an OK job! However, they have a ton of outdoor seating and were following proper precautions inside. The whole block was blocked off from traffic, which made dinning on the sidewalk / street much nicer without cars whizzing by. We were a 6 top, and the waiter was so great--all the staff was--attentive and kept the table stocked with water, drinks, and chips/salsa. We made a reservation on Open Table, and it was easy peasy. The best thing were the chips & salsa--a hearty consistency with an even heat but not overwhelming. The chips were crispy and salty. I was not a fan of the queso--it was fine, but not extraordinary. When I asked if we could substitute beef for chicken in one of the enchilada platters, they were more than accommodating which is always appreciated as a customer. The flour tortillas were definitely the highlight of the show--really flavorful and made me want to have ordered fajitas instead... Everything dinner-wise tasted fine, but not mind-blowing. My friends really enjoyed the prickly pear margs, so score some when you come. Standard for NYC, they automatically rolled in gratuity for a 6 top (or larger) into the bill.

Super disappointing. Food was fine, standard Tex mex as advertised- fajitas, white queso, chips. All fine but the quality of something you'd pay about $20 for if not located beside gramercy park. Margarita was truly one of the worst I've had though, $13 for what I think was margarita mix alone- no tequila, no salt.
Hello there. Unfortunately my order never arrived. Wtf am I supposed to do? Postmates said it arrived and it never came. I called and nobody answered the phone. Great business you have here. Fuck you

I love Javelina and simply cannot stop talking about it. Love the atmosphere! I've tried many different items and have not been disappointed. All of the staff are incredibly polite - you definitely feel welcome and looked after. Overall, I love Javelina.

The restaurant took all the precautions to make sure it was covid safe. We had our temps taken at the door and had to put a contact down for retrace. The only inconvenience is you do need an apple phone to put the contact down, which took us a while to realize(went through 2 people who had androids to find out).

The restaurant was clean, had dividers and the lighting was nice & dim. We started the meal with chips and salsa/queso. The chips are so delicious!!!!! I could not stop eating the appetizers. I have yet to have amazing queso in the northeast until I came to this restaurant. I thought there was only good queso down South. We ended up getting the jalapeño queso & it was so delish!!!! I loved it! The one that we got had friend jalapeños on the top which added an extra crunch and was amazing! 

The chicken tacos were good, honestly like any other tacos I would have at a restaurant. When you buy 3 tacos, you get a side of rice & beans. It was a nice combo with my meals. The margarita was divine as well!

Honestly. I would absolutely go back just for the queso! Staff was friendly and kind, it took about 30mins for our food order to be taken, but we didn't mind at all. The appetizers were so divine and delicious - it kept us entertained & it was really busy on a  sat night. Loved the place!
New favorite Mexican takeout spot! Delivery was well packaged, good portions, and arrived still nearly too hot to eat. The white queso and chicken fajitas were delicious.

Within the last year, I moved from the south to NYC. My favorite thing about the south is the Tex Mex. Very hard to find here. I searched for awhile and eventually found Javelina. My friend and I (also craving queso) loved this spot so much! The prickly pear margarita was great. The homemade flour tortillas were so good. Queso was the star of the meal. Huge portion and worth it. Free chips and salsa like you'd get in Texas too. Loved every second of it.
The food was great and so were the margaritas. A little pricey but that seems like the norm post pandemic.
Frozen margs are strong! food is average in my opinion, but the overall vibes are very fun!

A restaurant filled with millennials stuffed in at a crowded bar. That's about it. Mexican food goes well with beer, end of discussion. I grew up in a Mexican neighborhood being spoiled by my friends' Mexican grandmothers who truly knew how to cook and season food. Let's just say New York overall has been quite a let down on both Mexican and somewhat Tex-Mex faire. The only thing Mexican about the food in this place is the salsa, which isn't half bad. They claim to make their tortillas, which explains why they're so doughy. The food is average at best, and more significantly the wait staff were naïve servers who felt being over pleasant was the same as good service. The hostess claimed they had many reservations but gave us a table and told us that we needed to exit it by little over an hour. The waiter was informed of the time constraint (which is plenty of time to eat) but he still rushed us throughout the entire meal anyway. He literally came up with a water pitcher in one hand and an order pad and menus in the other, and while he filled our glasses of water asked us what we would like to eat and drink, and added that he could make suggestions quickly. My wife was 75% through her meal when he attempted to take her plate. He had also brought out her meal with the appetizer at the same time (and not my meal which came about the time she was finished). He seemed to think he was justified because her meal was tacos and the appetizer was tamales so I guess he thought size dictated when they came out LOL, only tacos are on the main menu so I don't know why he assumed that. My fajitas came literally about the time she was finished with her meal. Right about then some young woman showed up and asked us what we thought of our meal--couldn't tell if she was the manager because she dressed as though she was a patron, and we just mouthed off that it was good and sent on her way so we could finish chewing the food in our mouths. I've always said that that's the sign of a great waiter--he knows to ask questions in between bites not while you're trying to swallow one. It seemed that no one would give us a moment to just enjoy our food and a conversation--kind of the point of going out to eat--which is what servers need to learn how to to do to truly be considered professional. Gotta love how I had about 1/3 if my meal left and he came by and said "are we still picking" and I want to say yes dummy because my wife finished her meal five minutes before you gave me mine so I need a little more time"... or better yet "Oh my God go away you little punk and let someone freaking digest their meal." Let's get to the food. Tamales, they truly take a gentle hand because on the one side they can become too wet and difficult to separate from the husk and on the other too dry because you removed it from the husk way too early to make it look presentable (kind of the case here), and even worse would be to have little seasoning and little flavor--which these did. So they were dry, no sauce, and little flavor. Now let's get to the shrimp fajitas--about six pieces of shrimp that you can tell were previously frozen because they were devoid of flavor, with little or no seasoning on a stack of onions and green peppers that haven't been cooked enough to garner any flavor, refried beans that looks like refried soup, guacamole (that's actually quite good), with sour cream and tomatoes (not salsa), those doughy tortillas, and a rice which only had flavor because jalapeños have been somehow puréed into it. Let's just put it this way, I could've cook this food in my house and I have no skills in Mexican cooking. Average and overpriced food with a pretentious atmosphere which is so typical of "Mexican" food places in New York City it isn't funny. There are so few places in Manhattan to eat decent Mexican food  and this certainly isn't one of them (and Mama Mexico is the same). If you want good Mexican food in NYC and don't want to pay absurd prices for and appreciate flavor, head up to Inwood, Washington Heights, the Bronx, Queens, and Brooklyn Mexican neighborhoods and try real food from real immigrants with real seasonings. Get the hell out of lower Manhattan.
Pretty classic delicious mexican food.  Fun staff and good service.  Delicious cocktails.  Nice atmosphere

I love getting Javelina when I need a Tex-Mex fix. The  Bob Armstrong queso is a hit. Brisket enchiladas were delicious. I've also had the fajitas. I was pleasantly surprised on this trip to find out they could do virgin margaritas! Yay! Our server was super friendly and gave us a free rice when we couldn't decide which one to get. Great experience all around. Can't believe the reviews aren't higher on this one!

Solid Tex Mex food at this place. Had some queso and chips to start and then some fish tacos. They were done well and put together nicely. The drinks were free flowing that evening and the margaritas were good. Dined outdoors and the street was shut down which made it comfortable to sit across the road from the restaurant.

We ordered delivery from Javelina and as a Texan, I can fully support this restaurant. It is some of the best Tex-Mex I've EVER had. I really want them to open a location in Texas.
I had the fajitas and Bob Armstrong queso and I couldn't stop eating! The fajitas were so tender and the queso was next level! 
I highly recommend this place for Tex-Mex in NYC!!
this place has the best queso it's so good and worth it! i got three bags of chips for just one order !! definitely worth it
Definitely an overrated Tex Mex spot in NYC.  Food is meh. Service is ok. Inside crammed.

The attitude of everyone we encountered was reason enough to return. The food was quite good, but the fact that every person that worked there seemed grateful that we were there made the evening so special. Bravo!

my favorite place for mexican food in the city! i'm from oklahoma so i knowwww good queso and let me tell you this queso is IT! so delicious!
along with the queso, all of their food is amazing. i love the brisket tacos, fajitas, or quesadillas! 
for drinks, the classic frozen margarita really can't be beat! it's the perfect size, delicious, and STRONG. 
the environment is fun and relaxed, cute decor, great staff, and good location! super fun for a girls night out, date night, or dinner with parents! my mom and i love to go here when she visits!
i've gotten it to go a few times also and everything was packed and traveled really well!  highly recommend!

This place is gross. The first time I had it I was like wow! Super yummy! But then I had it a few times again (not consecutively) and it truly has bad food. I'm not sure what the drinks are like because I ordered takeout, but wow is it bad. The queso is ok. Everything else is pretty awful. Tacos are crap. The tortillas are raw. The beans and rice!!! How do you eff up beans and rice?? Well they have! The beans are practically water. I'm pretty sure they are reconstituted beans. The rice is gross. Go to Taco Bell. Taco Bell would be a better option.

We had a lovely time at Javelina.  My friend is in town and she preferred to dine outdoors.  Given it was going to be in the low 50s, we walked around in search of restaurants with heat lamps and after a 15 minute walk, we came across Javelina. Although OpenTable did not show any availability for a group of 6, I went inside and asked the host if he could accommodate us and he could, and made the reservation for us.

The outdoor section had about 4 tables spaced apart - they pushed two tables together for our group.  I also like that 18th St is not too busy, so not a ton of foot traffic and we were enough away from the sidewalk to feel secluded.

We arrived early and our drink orders were immediately taken, followed by complimentary chips and salsa.  As our group arrived, the waiter came to check on us pretty frequently, providing us feedback and recommendations and bringing our drinks and food quickly.  

First off, I really liked the chips and salsa.  I could not stop eating them.  Once the guacamole came out, I switched to that, but was glad I saved some appetite for the queso - it was creamy and flavorful and addictive.  We ate it all up!  For entree, I ordered the chicken enchiladas, which came with beans and rice.  It was a nice mix of food and filling.  For dessert we shared the churros, which was perfect for our group - only thing i would have asked for was small plates as the ice cream and chocolate sauce was dripping.  The traditional margarita hit the spot as well.

Overall, I thought this was a great pick for a small group dinner outdoors.  The heat lamps kept us toasty and we felt taken care of.  I would definitely return, and maybe check out the inside next time!

I had a reservation for two on a Thursday night at 6pm. I didn't take pictures because I was starvingggg and too excited to eat complimentary chips and salsa!! Definitely filled up on chips though. My fiancé ordered two chicken tacos and the queso sampler and I ordered the veggie fajitas. Fajitas did not disappoint. Came with 4 super soft tortillas and all the fixings. Half of it came home with me and made delicious leftovers. Spacious area inside with very attentive staff. Service was great. Also love a nice clean bathroom! I will absolutely be back!

Huge fan of javelina existing in multiple locations in Manhattan. Would love a location in Williamsburg because Tex-Mex is rather light in the area. Queso queso queso! Highly recommend if your a Texan and craving the original goods. Plus a frozen margaritas on tap, can't ask for nothing more.

Question is - why haven't we been here before? Being a frequent Texas visitor I've had my fair share of authentic Tex Mex meals. Not to say that this was super authentic but wow did this place hit the spot. 

First off. The QUESO. Unbelievably good. We ordered the sampler with the Mag Mud queso. Quite literally could not stop eating it. The other quesos were so good and unique too! You could taste how fresh this and everything else was. For our main dishes we got the chicken quesadilla and the avocado tacos. So so good. Everything was well flavored and the sauces and dips that it came with really made our meals. 

If I had to recommend anything, it would be to try the queso (can't go wrong with any of them) and the avocado tacos were ridiculously good. My friend and I both ordered the prickly pear margaritas, also which paired perfectly with our meals. 

Highly recommend coming here if you haven't already!

Good Tex mex spot in the city. The drinks are strong, my friend and I both got prickly pear on the rocks. Their queso sampler is really fun, lots of option, my favorite was the habanero. We also got the chicken quesadilla and avocado tacos to split. Overall the food was good, ambiance was lively, drinks were great.

There used to be something called "spicy taco" pizza rolls.  This place made me miss them.  On the plus side, the margaritas are very, very sweet and don't have much booze in them, which is a plus for me since I'm not a big drinker.

This is a fine spot, and one of the only I've found in NYC that has queso (not cheese dip, tho). It's authentic in that they offer Lone Star beer in their silly little Texas bottles, and serve done-up tacos just like they would in Austin. However, the queso wasn't amazing--although there were many options and none of them were bad--but it was good for NYC. Totally a good spot to take your s/o, but maybe not quite a date. It's worth checking out, but my search for any/good cheese dip in the city continues...

I ordered delivery and got a quesadilla. It looked good but tasted so gross, like cinnamon and cardamom. I started chewing it and was so put off by the flavors that I spat it out. Had the queso as well which was very mediocre. Would not order from here again.

Just managed to move my mom closer to me in the city from Texas and we were both jonesing for some true Tex-Mex enchiladas, rather than the delicious, more authentic Mexican cuisine that seems plentiful here.
